JOURNAL DE SHANGHAI January 17, 1940.

WANG CHING-WEI'S APPEAL TO THE CHUNGKING GOVERNMENT

Yesterday Wang Ching-wei sent a telegram to General Chiang Kai-shek inviting his collaboration in re-establishing peace between China and Japan.

Wang Ching-wei stated that after much difficult negotiation he has succeeded in concluding an agreement with the Japanese and fixed the peace terms. He does not make these terms known but simply states that they will not cause the ruin of China, that they will safeguard his independence and liberty and that they will render possible the reconstruction of the nation according to the Three Principles of the People.

These are the main points in the appeal. It is worthy of note that Wang Ching-wei is actually asking Chiang Kai-shek to form with him a Peace Front in order to put an end to the hostilities. Does this mean that the conditions of the Wang Ching-wei-Itagaki agreement are not definitive and that the Chungking Government equally has a word to say in the discussion?

Wang Ching-wei seems to admit that peace without the adhesion of Chungking would be uncertain and be still far away. If that be so, does Wang Ching-wei think that Chiang Kai-shek and his collaborators will have also to give their approval to the peace terms and in that event be allowed to demand some modification of the agreement? This would imply the opening of parleys, direct or indirect, between Chungking and Japan. On the other hand, the proposal to the Chungking Government to associate itself with Wang Ching-wei in forming a National Peace Front implies a fusion of the two Kuomintangs. President Lin Sen will remain the sole Chief Executive for all China and it is he who will eventually ratify or sign the Treaty with Japan. There will be no new central government at Nanking.

Prince Konoye had declared that Tokyo will refuse to have any dealings with Chiang Kai-shek or the Kuomintang, but the Prince is no longer Premier and his successors have agreed to permit Wang Ching-wei to act as the advocate of the Kuomintang.

So long as the peace conditions are unknown it will not be possible for us to say how far the proposal will interest the Chungking Government. It will be recalled that Chungking had announced that it would oppose any concession that is harmful to the political or economic sovereignty of China or to her territorial integrity.

Wang Ching-wei's appeal gives no information regarding the withdrawal of Japanese troops. Without doubt, Japan, as Wang Ching-wei says, has no desire to maintain a lengthy occupation which does not appear to her necessary, and Japan's budget has shown that it has weighed heavily upon the Japanese people and on Japan's finances. Such an important question cannot be discussed until details are known.

Perhaps General Chiang Kai-shek and President Lin Sen are already informed of the terms of the agreement of December 30. In that case, we shall soon know, by their replies, what they think of the appeal and we can then estimate any chance for success which this appeal
18 may have.

汪精卫呼吁重庆政府

昨日，汪精卫致电蒋介石将军，邀请其合作，以重建中日和平。

汪精卫称，经过艰难谈判，他已成功与日方达成协议并确定了和平条款。他并未公布这些条款，仅声明这些条款不会导致中国毁灭，将保障中国的独立与自由，并使依据三民主义进行国家重建成为可能。

以上是该呼吁的主要要点。值得注意的是，汪精卫实际上是在请求蒋介石与其共同组建“和平阵线”，以结束敌对行动。这是否意味着汪精卫-板垣协定的条件并非最终定论，重庆政府在讨论中同样拥有发言权？

汪精卫似乎承认，若无重庆方面的加入，和平将是不确定的，且仍遥不可及。若果真如此，汪精卫是否认为蒋介石及其同僚也必须批准和平条款，并在此情况下被允许要求对协定进行修改？这将意味着重庆与日本之间开启直接或间接的谈判。另一方面，向重庆政府提议与汪精卫联合组建全国性和平阵线，暗示着两个国民党的融合。林森主席将继续担任全中国唯一的国家元首，并由他最终批准或签署对日和约。南京不会成立新的中央政府。

近卫亲王曾宣称东京拒绝与蒋介石或国民党进行任何接触，但近卫已不再担任首相，其继任者已同意允许汪精卫作为国民党的代言人行事。

只要和平条件尚不为人知，我们就无法判断该提议在多大程度上会引起重庆政府的兴趣。需回顾的是，重庆方面曾宣布，它将反对任何损害中国政治或经济主权或领土完整的让步。

汪精卫的呼吁未提供关于日军撤军的任何信息。毫无疑问，正如汪精卫所言，日本无意维持其认为非必要的长期占领，且日本的预算显示，这种占领已给日本人民及日本财政带来沉重负担。在细节知晓之前，这一重要问题无法进行讨论。

或许蒋介石将军和林森主席已获悉12月30日协定的条款。若是那样，我们将很快通过他们的回复得知他们对该呼吁的看法，届时我们便可评估此呼吁
18 可能成功的几率。

Hongkong on January 3.
It is said that Wang Ching-wei has been much
excited over the desertion of these three trusted followers.
Much uneasiness is now prevalent among the members of
Wang's clique.
Following the leakage of the news of the
departure of these three persons, denials of the truth of
the report have been made by a certain news agency of
Wang's clique, but this can in no way conceal from the
public the facts which are already known to all. Even
Wang's own followers have admitted the departure of these
three persons though they have explained that it was due
to the indisposition of his mother that Chen Kung-poh
left Shanghai for the south, while Tao Hsi-sen left here
because there exists a serious disagreement between him
and Wang Ching-wei over the peace proposals. Kao Chung-
wu is said to be on very bad terms with the Japanese and
was therefore unable to stick to his post. Consequently,
he was forced to leave Shanghai.
Owing to this desertion of his trusted
followers, Wang Ching-wei has sustained a serious setback
in his peace proposals. On January 16, he sent a telegram
to General Chiang Kai-shek requesting him to decide on
a definite policy for the nation and to cease fighting
and initiate peace talks. The telegram reads as follows:-
"I was determined long ago to work for the
salvation of the nation. If you continue to insist on
the refusal of my proposals, I can assure you that this
will in no way affect my determination and I will be
forced to work wholeheartedly first for the realization
of a partial peace and then to bring about peace for
the nation. However, if you will take into serious
consideration the safety of the nation and the people,
cease fighting and enter into peace talks with Japan
according to the statement of Prince Konoye, until the
realization of fundamental peace, then I will work
wholeheartedly together with all the comrades to help
you to bring about an early realization of peace for the
nation. You are now the only person in Chungking who
enjoys full right to decide on a future policy for the
nation as to war or peace. You are now undertaking a
very heavy responsibility and the nation is hoping much
from you. I shall be much obliged if you will give
your consideration to these heart-to-heart views of mine".
pages.zh:
1940年1月17日。
晨间译稿。

《大美报》：

汪精卫致电蒋介石

陈公博、陶希圣
和高宗武原为汪精卫的亲信
追随者。他们被视为
他的主要助手。近期，由于日本当局
对傀儡政权的苛刻要求被揭露，以及
汪的和平提议变得愈发不合情理，他们发现
自己无法继续支持
汪精卫。因此，他们于1939年12月31日离开上海前往
香港，并宣布与汪的政权决裂。据信他们已于
1月3日抵达香港。
据说汪精卫对这三位亲信追随者的
离去感到极为激动。目前汪派成员中
普遍存在不安情绪。
在这三人离去的消息泄露后，
汪派某通讯社曾否认报道的真实性，但这
丝毫无法向公众掩盖众人皆知的事实。即便是
汪自己的追随者也承认了这三人的离去，尽管他们解释说，陈公博
离开上海南下是因其母身体不适，而陶希圣离开此地
是因为他在和平提议问题上与汪精卫存在严重分歧。高宗
武据称与日方关系恶劣，
因此无法坚守岗位。故而，
他被迫离开上海。
由于亲信追随者的这一背离，汪精卫在其和平提议上遭受了严重挫折。1月16日，他致电
蒋介石将军，请求其为国家确定明确政策，停止战斗并启动和谈。电文如下：
“余久已决心为国救亡。若阁下坚持
拒绝余之提议，余敢保证，这
绝不会影响余之决心，余将被迫
首先全心致力于实现局部和平，进而
促成国家和平。然而，若阁下能认真
考虑国家与人民之安危，停止战斗，
并根据近卫亲王的声明与日本进行和谈，直至
实现根本和平，则余将全心
与全体同志合作，协助
阁下早日实现国家和平。如今阁下是重庆方面
唯一拥有对国家未来战和政策
完全决定权之人。阁下正承担着
极重的责任，国家对阁下寄予厚望。若阁下能
考虑余这番肺腑之言，余将不胜感激”。

January 17, 1940. Morning Translation.

December 6, 1939. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao, Hwa Pao and Sin Wan Pao (Peiping telegram) :-

DEATH OF MARSHAL WU PEI-FU

According to Dr. "Stickfolk," the Chief Surgeon of a German Hospital here, he was sent for by the late Marshal Wu Pei-fu to look after his toothache on the sixth day after he had been sick, when the Chinese General was already found to be experiencing difficulty in breathing as his throat was swollen. Consequently, the late Marshal was advised to go to the German Hospital to undergo an operation but this was refused by both the deceased General and his family on the ground that the hospital is located within the legation quarters. Later he was attended to by a Japanese doctor named Terada (another report says that the Japanese doctor is named Ito) who assured him that there was nothing serious in his indisposition. Unexpectedly, however, the late Marshal expired at the time when the operation was in progress. It is said that the deceased General had so far left no will as regards to both his family and national affairs.-----Associated Press.

Chinese-American Daily News and Circulation Daily News :-

The news of the sudden death of Marshal Wu Pei-fu has caused much grief among the local public bodies. Ever since the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, the late Marshal had on various occasions been approached by the Japanese to come out as a figure head but on each occasion the invitation was flatly refused by the late Marshal, thereby preserving his reputation as well as his moral principles. He was indeed worthy of being looked upon as an outstanding figure among the Chinese military officers. It is learned that a joint telegram of condolence was sent to the family of the deceased General in Peiping by local public bodies yesterday.

Ta Mei Pao, Hwa Pao and Sin Wan Pao (Chungking telegram) :-

In connection with the sudden demise of Marshal Wu Pei-fu, a telegram of condolence was sent to Madame Wu in Peiping by General Ho Ying-chin, Minister of War of the National Government, on December 5.

Ta Mei Pao :-

Editorial Comment

Much speculation has been prevalent since the death of Marshal Wu Pei-fu. Several days prior to his death, information given out from Chungking revealed that the late Marshal had already made clear to the Japanese authorities that he would never be willing to act as a puppet. Though the Japanese authorities denied the truth of this report, confirmation has, however, been secured by the Reuter News Agency from reliable sources. The late Marshal was of the opinion that unless the Japanese authorities withdrew their troops from China, he could have no co-operation with them.

1939年12月6日。晨间译稿。

《大美报》、《华报》和《新晚报》（北平电）：

吴佩孚元帅逝世

据本市一家德国医院的外科主任“Stickfolk”医生（音译）称，吴佩孚元帅病逝前第六天，因牙痛召其诊治，当时这位中国将军已被发现呼吸困难，喉咙肿胀。因此，建议已故元帅前往德国医院接受手术，但已故将军及其家属以医院位于使馆区为由予以拒绝。随后，一位名叫寺田（Terada）的日本医生（另有说法称该日本医生名为伊藤/Ito）为其诊治，并向他保证病情并不严重。然而，出乎意料的是，已故元帅在手术进行时去世。据说，已故将军在家庭和国家事务方面均未留下遗嘱。-----美联社。

《中美日报》和《循环日报》：

吴佩孚元帅突然逝世的消息在当地公共团体中引起了极大悲痛。自中日敌对行动爆发以来，日本人曾多次邀请已故元帅出面担任名义领袖，但每次均遭到已故元帅断然拒绝，从而保全了他的声誉及道德原则。他确实不愧为中国军官中的杰出人物。据悉，当地公共团体昨日向北平已故将军的家属发送了联合唁电。

《大美报》、《华报》和《新晚报》（重庆电）：

就吴佩孚元帅突然逝世一事，国民政府军政部长何应钦将军于12月5日向北平的吴夫人发送了唁电。

《大美报》：

社论评论

自吴佩孚元帅逝世以来，猜测纷纷。在他去世前几天，来自重庆的消息透露，已故元帅已向日本当局明确表示，他绝不愿意充当傀儡。尽管日本当局否认了这一报道的真实性，但路透社已从可靠来源获得证实。已故元帅认为，除非日本当局从中国撤军，否则他无法与其合作。

pages.en:
The late General was undoubtedly an upright
gentleman of moral principle. Though he was a soldier,
he was able to preserve his honour and moral principle even
up to the time of his death. It is, therefore, not
accidental that the public should have so admired the
personality and uprightness of the late General.
It is true that the late General had given
some consideration to the Japanese proposals but he
understood that he could not do things against the wishes
of the people, though the Japanese authorities had promised
him terms favourable to China as a condition for his
co-operation and had assured him that they had not the
slightest intention to do things to impair the sovereign
rights of China.
What drew the most attention by the late
Marshal was whether or not Japan would station troops in
this country. When he realized that Japan would never
willingly recall her troops from this country, he at once
split with the Japanese because he did not wish to act as
a puppet.
Alas! Marshal Wu is now dead, but his death
has inspired a feeling of straightforwardness among the
general public and will inspire the Chinese people to march
forward bravely for the sake of righteousness and justice.

In a leading article to-day, the "Shun Pao"
states that the straightforward and unwavering spirit shown
by the late Marshal Wu Pei-fu despite Japanese approaches
for his co-operation has made him worthy of the highest
respect of the people throughout the country. The paper
concludes by saying that the late Marshal deserves to be
regarded as one of the most honourable characters in Chinese
history.

In an editorial, the editor of the "Chinese-
American Daily News" reproduces the following poem which
was written by Marshal Wu in 1930, at a time when he was
seriously ill:-
Whilst in power, my conscience has been clear,
For I have no concubine nor riches;
My life is that of an ordinary scholar.
After my defeat, I did not go abroad,
Nor sought protection in Foreign Concessions.
I simply retired and became a common citizen.
pages.zh:
已故将军无疑是一位正直的
有道德原则的君子。虽然他是一名军人，
但他直至临终仍能保持荣誉和道德原则。因此，
公众如此钦佩已故将军的人格和正直并非
偶然。
诚然，已故将军曾对日本的提议
进行过一些考量，但他明白不能做违背
民意之事，尽管日本当局曾承诺
以有利于中国的条款作为其合作的条件，并
向他保证绝无丝毫损害中国主权的意图。
已故元帅最关注的问题是
日本是否会在本国驻军。当他意识到日本绝不
愿意从本国撤军时，他立即与日本决裂，因为他不愿充当傀儡。
唉！吴元帅虽已离世，但他的死
激发了公众的正直感，并将激励中国人民
为了正义和公道勇敢前进。

在今日的社论中，《申报》
指出，已故吴佩孚元帅在面对日本拉拢合作时表现出的
直率和不屈精神，使他值得
全国人民的最高敬意。该报
总结说，已故元帅堪称中国
历史上最光荣的人物之一。

在《中美日报》的一篇社论中，编辑转载了
吴元帅于1930年重病期间所写的一首诗：
掌权之时，良心清白，
无妾室，无财富；
生平如同普通书生。
战败之后，未出国门，
亦未寻求外国租界庇护。
 merely 退隐成为普通公民。

April 29, 1939.
Morning Translation.
No. 5. 8986
Date 6 / 12 . 39

Morning Leader (Hongkong telegram).

WANG CHING-WEI MEETS HIGH JAPANESE WAR OFFICE OFFICIAL

According to reliable information, Wang Ching-wei arrived at Shanghai secretly on about April 24. The Japanese War Office detailed a high official to Shanghai to interview him. The meeting place was kept secret and even high officials of the Japanese authorities in Shanghai were unaware of it. No information is available on what transpired at the meeting between the Japanese official and Wang Ching-wei.

However, a telegram to Hongkong from a certain party in Shanghai reveals that the general outline of the discussion was as follows:-
1) Wang requested that the Japanese should not cease their military operations until they had occupied Hanyang (漢陽), Sian (西安) and Kweilin (桂林).
2) The Central Federal Government with Wang as Chief Executive will first secure recognition from Japan, Germany and Italy and then by any one of the other Powers, such as Great Britain or America or France, before it is regarded as the supreme government.
3) The Federal Government shall form 12 armies of expeditionary troops against Chiang Kai-shek and the Communists, with Wang Ching-wei as Commander-in-Chief.
4) The Federal Government shall make the following changes:-
a) To abolish the Peiping Provisional Government and to rename it the "Autonomous Government of the United Provinces of North China".
b) To abolish the "Reformed Government" in Nanking and to rename it the "Autonomous Government of the United Provinces in East China".
c) As soon as Sian and the Canton-Hankow Railway have been captured, autonomous governments shall be formed at Sian for North-west China, at the Wuhan for Central China and at Canton for South China.
d) The Federal Government shall be located at Peiping or Nanking; this is to be decided by Tokyo.
5) Japanese shall advance $30,000,000 monthly for the expenses of the Federal Government. The consolidated tax within the jurisdiction of the Federal Government will be offered as security.

It is reported that most of the points have already been decided upon. On April 27 Tokyo detailed a cruiser to Shanghai to take Wang Ching-wei to Tokyo together with a certain high official of the Japanese War Office. Whether Wang will leave immediately for Tokyo will be decided on April 28 or April 29. If Wang cannot go to Tokyo, the Japanese authorities will send Konoye and Tocho (former Vice War Minister) to Shanghai to meet him.

《南华早报》（香港电报）。

汪精卫会见日本陆军省高官

据可靠消息，汪精卫于4月24日左右秘密抵达上海。日本陆军省派遣一名高官赴上海与其会晤。会面地点保密，甚至在上海的日本当局高官亦不知情。关于日本官员与汪精卫会谈的具体内容，目前尚无消息。

然而，上海某方发给香港的一份电报显示，讨论的大致纲要如下：-
1) 汪要求日军在占领汉阳、西安和桂林之前，不得停止军事行动。
2) 以汪为行政首长的中央联邦政府，将首先争取日本、德国和意大利的承认，然后再争取其他任一强国（如英国、美国或法国）的承认，之后才被视为最高政府。
3) 联邦政府将组建12支远征军，讨伐蒋介石和共产党人，由汪精卫担任总司令。
4) 联邦政府将进行以下变更：-
a) 撤销北平临时政府，将其更名为“华北联合自治政府”。
b) 撤销南京“维新政府”，将其更名为“华东联合自治政府”。
c) 一旦攻占西安及粤汉铁路，将在西安成立西北自治政府，在武汉成立华中自治政府，在广州成立华南自治政府。
d) 联邦政府所在地定为北平或南京；此事项由东京决定。
5) 日本每月提供3,000万美元作为联邦政府的经费。联邦政府辖区内的统税将作为担保。

据报道，大部分要点已获决定。4月27日，东京派遣一艘巡洋舰前往上海，拟将汪精卫连同日本陆军省某高官一并带往东京。汪是否立即启程赴东京，将于4月28日或4月29日决定。若汪无法前往东京，日本当局将派近卫文麿和东条（前陆军次官）赴上海与其会晤。

January 31, 1939. Afternoon Translation

Sin Shun Poo (Japanese owned Chinese language newspaper) :-

"WANG CHING WEI EXPRESSES HIS VIEWS : ONLY PEACE
CAN SAVE CHINA"

Hongkong, January 30.
In an interview several days ago with a certain important personage who had left Chungking for Hongkong via Hanoi, Wang Ching-wei is said to have expressed the following views :-

To declare war or to talk peace is a function belonging to the Government. The object of war or peace is to protect the existence and independence of the nation. If the object can be attained by war, then fighting must be carried out, and if the object can be attained by peace, then peace should be arranged. The present war of resistance is simply one of the methods to preserve the existence and independence of the country. Now I have discovered several weak points in the policy of resistance, so I advocated peace because it will also secure the existence and independence of our country. I am strongly opposed to a Kuomintang-Communist co-operation as the object of the war of resistance. The reasons held by the Communist Party in opposing peace are as follows :-
(1) So long as the Sino-Japanese hostilities continue, Soviet Russia will have peace; therefore, to protect herself, Soviet Russia desires a prolongation of the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
(2) Protracted hostilities will reduce China to deeper poverty and she will have to depend on the Communists.

If Japan is determined to conquer China, then there is no alternative for China but to offer resistance and peace may be viewed as a great danger. However, we can say that Japan does not want to conquer China; what she wants is Sino-Japanese collaboration, a harmonious and neighbourly co-operation against Communism with economic rapprochement, reciprocal understanding and mutual assistance as the foundation. Such a peace in the Orient will bring about peace in the world. This policy should be adopted by China and Japan, particularly by China, because if she does not take this stand, she will not be able to preserve her existence and independence and she will never be able to become a modern nation. -- Domei.

1939年1月31日。午后译件

《新顺报》（Sin Shun Poo，日资中文报纸）：

“汪精卫发表观点：唯有和平才能救中国”

香港，1月30日。
据称，汪精卫在数日前接受一位经河内离开重庆赴港的重要人物采访时，表达了以下观点：

宣战或议和是政府的职权。战争或和平的目的是保护国家的生存与独立。如果通过战争能达到此目的，则必须作战；如果通过和平能达到此目的，则应安排和平。目前的抗战只是保存国家生存与独立的方法之一。如今我发现了抵抗政策中的几个弱点，因此我主张和平，因为这也能够保障我们国家的生存与独立。我强烈反对以国共合作作为抗战的目标。共产党反对和平的理由如下：
(1) 只要中日敌对状态持续，苏联就能保持和平；因此，为了保护自身，苏联希望延长中日敌对状态。
(2) 长期的敌对状态将使中国陷入更深的贫困，从而不得不依赖共产党。

如果日本决心征服中国，那么中国除了抵抗别无选择，和平可被视为巨大的危险。然而，我们可以说，日本并不想征服中国；她想要的是中日合作，即以经济亲善、相互理解和互助为基础，建立和谐友好的反共合作。这种东方的和平将带来世界的和平。这一政策应被中国和日本采纳，尤其是中国，因为如果不采取这一立场，中国将无法保全其生存与独立，也永远无法成为一个现代国家。-- 同盟社。

January 18, 1939. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers (Hongkong telegram) :-

WANG CHING-WEI LEAVES FOR EUROPE

According to information from Chinese
sources, Wang Ching-wei left for Europe on January 14.
No definite information is available nor could
confirmation of this report be secured from authoritative
sources.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers (Hongkong telegram) :-

Attack on Wang's Follower in Hongkong

Ling Pah-sen (林柏生), managing
director of the "Nan Hwa Jih Pao" (南華日報) in Hongkong,
an official organ of Wang Ching-wei, whilst walking on the
streets on January 17, was attacked by two Chinese, one
carrying an iron hook and the other a hammer. He was
seriously injured and is at present undergoing treatment
in hospital. One of the assailants was arrested on the
spot, but the other made good his escape.
It is said that the Hongkong Police are
paying much attention to this affair.

1939年1月18日。晨间译件。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸（香港电报）：

汪精卫赴欧

据中方消息来源，汪精卫已于1月14日启程赴欧。
目前尚无确切消息，也无法从权威渠道证实此报道。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸（香港电报）：

汪之追随者在港遇袭

汪精卫官方机关报香港《南华日报》总经理林柏生，于1月17日在街头行走时，遭到两名中国人袭击，一人手持铁钩，另一人手持锤子。他身受重伤，目前正在医院接受治疗。其中一名袭击者当场被捕，另一名逃脱。
据悉，香港警方正密切关注此事。

January 11, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News (Hongkong Correspondence) :-

HONGKONG LABOUR UNIONS SUPPORT NATIONAL GOVERNMENT

The various bodies of overseas Chinese
in Hongkong are highly indignant over Wang Ching-wei's
treasonable activities. More than 50 Chinese labour
unions in Hongkong have pledged their unanimous support
of the National Government.
At a meeting held on January 8 by the
Chinese Reporters' Association in Hongkong, it was
resolved that a manifesto be issued denouncing Wang
Ching-wei's peace proposals and pledging support to
the Government in the war of resistance.

Hwa Mei Chen Pao (Editorial) :-

Traitors Within Government Circles Must Be Suppressed

It will be wrong to conclude that Wang
Ching-wei's treason has been dealt with because he
has been dismissed from the Kuomintang by the Central
Executive Committee. We must understand that it was
not on the day of his departure from Chungking nor on
the date that he issued his first telegram that he
became a traitor. He must have been in the service of
the Japanese Special Service Department for a long time
already. He remained in Government circles to
undertake activities harmful to our national unification
and progress. His great thirst for power and wealth
has now led him to become a traitor.
The action taken by the Kuomintang in
dismissing Wang Ching-wei and relieving him of all
his posts cannot be regarded as having settled Wang's
case; actually it marks the beginning of the work for
the suppression of traitors within Government circles.
In order to win final victory, all traitors must be
eradicated and unless this is done, there can be
no improvement in our political situation and this will
seriously affect our military operations.
Wang Ching-wei's betrayal was not due
to any differences of opinion with other leaders of the
Kuomintang; it is part of his work for Japan. As has
been said by Dr. Kan Chia-hou (甘介侯), member of the
People's Political Council, Wang had intended to bring
about the materialization of his peace plots with Japan
so that he might count on Japan's help to overthrow
General Chiang Kai-shek. On that account his dismissal
from the Kuomintang and from his posts is not sufficient
punishment for his treasonable activities. He has even
said that with the exception of the communist and
unscrupulous elements, there is no person in this country
who is opposed to peace. As a matter of fact, with the
exception of only a small number of traitorous elements,
no one is willing to surrender. The whole nation is
opposed to Wang Ching-wei's peace movement.

1939年1月11日。午后译件。

《中美日报》（香港通讯）：

香港工会支持国民政府

香港各华侨团体对汪精卫的叛国活动深感愤慨。香港50多个中华工会已宣誓一致支持国民政府。
在1月8日举行的香港中国记者协会会议上，决议发表宣言，谴责汪精卫的和平提议，并宣誓支持政府抗战。

《华美晨报》（社论）：

必须肃清政府圈内的汉奸

如果认为汪精卫因被国民党中央执行委员会开除党籍而其叛国行为已得到处理，那是错误的。我们必须明白，他并非在离开重庆之日或发出第一封通电之日才成为汉奸。他必定早已为日本特务机关效力。他留在政府圈内，从事危害我国统一和进步的活动。他对权力和财富的巨大贪欲，如今导致他沦为汉奸。
国民党开除汪精卫党籍并免除其一切职务的行动，不能被视为已解决了汪的案件；实际上，这标志着肃清政府圈内汉奸工作的开始。为了赢得最终胜利，必须根除所有汉奸，除非做到这一点，否则我们的政治局势无法改善，这将严重影响我们的军事行动。
汪精卫的背叛并非由于与其他国民党领导人的意见分歧；这是他为日本工作的一部分。正如国民参政会参政员甘介侯博士所说，汪曾企图实现其与日本的和平阴谋，以便指望日本帮助推翻蒋介石将军。因此，将其开除出国民党并免职，不足以惩罚其叛国活动。他甚至声称，除了共产党分子和无耻之徒外，国内无人反对和平。事实上，除了一小撮汉奸分子外，没有人愿意投降。全国上下都反对汪精卫的和平运动。

pages.en:
Secondly, the Government should adopt
vigorous measures to bring about the complete suppression
of all those elements who, like Wang Ching-wei, are
looking forward to personal glory and power. The
existence of such elements is harmful to the interests
of the nation and national unification and should,
therefore, be removed from Government circles.

Sih Pao (扫荡报), a mosquito paper :-

Wang Ching-wei's Insult to the Chinese People

Wang Ching-wei has made public a letter
sent to the National Government containing absurd
suggestions for peace. In this letter, he regards as
traitors all those Chinese who are opposed to peace and
who are unwilling to become slaves. This is an insult
to the 450,000,000 Chinese people.
Wang Ching-wei is thus maliciously
accusing patriots. What a shame! As he may resort to
other dishonest trickery, the Chinese people should
deal with him.
pages.zh:
其次，政府应采取有力措施，彻底镇压所有像汪精卫那样追求个人荣耀和权力的分子。这类分子的存在有害于国家利益和国家统一，因此应将其从政府圈子中清除。

《扫荡报》，一家小型报刊：

汪精卫侮辱中国人民

汪精卫公布了一封致国民政府的信件，其中包含荒谬的和平建议。在这封信中，他将所有反对和平、不愿成为奴隶的中国人视为汉奸。这是对四亿五千万中国人民的侮辱。
汪精卫如此恶意诬蔑爱国者。真是无耻！鉴于他可能会使用其他不诚实的伎俩，中国人民应对付他。

January 11, 1939.                                      Morning Translation

Standard and other local newspapers (Chungking telegram) :-

        WANG CHING-WEI LEAVES HANOI IN DISGUISE

            There is absolutely no truth in the allegation
that General Chiang Kai-shek had proposed to make a peace
offer to Japan in an interview with Wang Ching-wei as alleged
in Wang's telegram issued in Hongkong on January 8 and
addressed to the National Defence Council.  It was only a
casual remark in the course of an ordinary conversation and
cannot be regarded as a formal proposal.
            The telegram sent jointly by Generals Li Tsung-
jen, Pei Chung-hsi, Chang Fah-kwei and Yu Han-mou demanding
the arrest of Wang Ching-wei was published in Chungking on
the night of January 9 and is attracting much public attention.
It is generally believed that if Wang Ching-wei will quickly
repent and leave for Europe to recuperate his health, the
Government may treat the matter as having come to an end.
            According to Japanese reports, Wang Ching-wei
suddenly disappeared from Hanoi on the night of January 9.
It is said that fearing attempts on his life he has escaped
with two of his trusted servants disguised as ordinary
merchants.  His present whereabouts are unknown.

1939年1月11日。                                      晨间译稿

《标准报》及其他本地报纸（重庆电）：-

        汪精卫乔装离开河内

            所谓蒋介石将军在与汪精卫的会晤中提议向日本提出和平条件一事，纯属子虚乌有；此说源自汪精卫1月8日自香港发出、致国防最高委员会的电报。那不过是日常交谈中的随口之言，不能视为正式提议。
            李宗仁、白崇禧、张发奎和余汉谋诸将军联名要求逮捕汪精卫的电报，于1月9日晚在重庆公布，引起公众广泛关注。普遍看法认为，如果汪精卫能迅速悔悟并前往欧洲疗养，政府可能会将此案作罢。
            据日方报道，汪精卫于1月9日晚突然从河内失踪。据悉，因担心有人暗杀，他已伪装成普通商人，携两名亲信仆从出逃。其目前下落不明。

pages.en:
Morning Leader publishes the following leading article :-

"Let Us Not Relax Our Traitor Extermination Work"

The military commanders in the various war
areas, such as Generals Li Tsung-jen, Pai Chung-hai, Chen
Cheng and others, have sent telegrams requesting the
National Government to effect the arrest of Wang Ching-wei
and to punish him. This shows that Wang Ching-wei's
conspiracy with the enemy and his desertion of the nation
will not be closed by his expulsion from the Kuomintang and
his removal from his government posts, for these measures
are inadequate to redeem Wang. At first the Kuomintang
and the National Government had hoped that Wang would repent
his action, but he has not only failed to repent but has
issued more rebellious statements.

The enactment of the "Measures governing
penalties of traitors" is intended to deal specially with
such people as Wang Ching-wei. We must not tolerate him
any longer lest our forbearance should encourage wickedness.
Wang Ching-wei should be severely punished.
However, there is one thing of great importance remaining
to be done: we must ascertain the cause of his rebellion so
as to put a stop to similar defections. What made Wang
Ching-wei conspire with the enemy? This is not easy to
answer.

According to Mr. Hu Ching-yi (胡景伊), a
member of the People's Political Council, Wang had an
ambition to become the leader and, secondly, he had fallen
in love with the Japanese Yen. According to Mr. Kan Kai-
hou (甘介侯), another member of the People's Political
Council, Wang had hoped to oust General Chiang Kai-shek
with assistance from Japan.

Why did Wang Ching-wei rebel as he holds a
high position?

There are two probabilities behind this
question: (1) His conspiracy with the enemy is decidedly
not of recent date. He had already been won over by the
Japanese Special Service Section at the time when he was
in power and was enforcing his pro-Japanese policies.
(2) Since his political influence is founded
on his pro-Japanese policy, he has been afraid of offending
Japan and the continuance of the war of resistance would
endanger his position.

Wang Ching-wei's rebellion against the National
Government is an aftermath of his pro-Japanese policies.
pages.zh:
《晨导报》发表如下社论：——

“切勿松懈肃清汉奸工作”

李宗仁、白崇禧、陈诚等各战区军事将领纷纷致电国民政府，要求逮捕汪精卫并予以惩处。这表明，将汪精卫开除出国民党并撤销其政府职务，并不能了结其通敌叛国之阴谋，因为这些措施不足以挽救汪精卫。起初，国民党与国民政府曾希望汪精卫能悔过自新，但他不仅未加悔改，反而发表了更多叛逆言论。

颁布《惩治汉奸条例》旨在专门处置汪精卫之流。我们绝不能再容忍他，以免我们的宽容助长邪恶。汪精卫应受严惩。然而，尚有一件至关重要的事情有待完成：我们必须查明其叛变的原因，以便杜绝类似的投敌行为。汪精卫为何通敌？这不易回答。

据国民参政会参政员胡景伊先生称，汪精卫一是野心勃勃，企图成为领袖；二是贪恋日元。据另一位国民参政会参政员甘介侯先生称，汪精卫曾希望借助日本之力排挤蒋介石将军。

汪精卫身居高位，为何仍要叛变？

对此问题有两种可能性：（1）其通敌阴谋绝非近期之事。早在其掌权并推行亲日政策之时，便已被日本特务机关收买。（2）由于其政治影响力建立在亲日政策之上，他唯恐得罪日本，而抗战的持续将危及其地位。

汪精卫背叛国民政府，是其亲日政策的余波。

December 31, 1938. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Hongkong telegram) :-

WANG CHING-WEI'S TELEGRAM TO CENTRAL KUOMINTANG HEADQUARTERS
SUGGESTING OPENING OF PEACE NEGOTIATIONS WITH JAPAN.

Mr. Wang Ching-wei has sent the following
telegram to the Central Kuomintang Headquarters :-
In April this year, the National Congress
issued a manifesto explaining China's war of resistance
as follows :-
"Since the Tangku Agreement, we have been
forbearing when dealing with Japan, our object being
to try by peaceful means to safeguard the provinces
in the North and to find a just solution of the question
of the Four North-Eastern Provinces. Politically,
our minimum desire is to preserve China's sovereign
rights and economy, we want mutual benefit and
equality."
Following the occurrence of the Lukuochiao
Incident in July, 1937, China was compelled to fight a
war of resistance. I have now read a statement issued
by the Japanese Government on December 22 dealing with
fundamentals for a readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations;
it contains the following three points :-
(1) GOOD NEIGHBOURS.- Japan has no territorial
designs on China nor will she demand compensation for
military expenses. Japan not only will respect the
sovereign rights of China, but she will return her
Concessions to China and abolish extraterritoriality so
that China may obtain complete independence.
Since the Japanese Government has issued such
a statement, we shall be in a position to protect the
Northern provinces, recover all territories lost during
the operations and preserve China's sovereign rights and
administrative integrity by peaceful means. Thus, we
may find a reasonable solution of the problem of the Four
North-Eastern Provinces according to the manifesto issued
by the National Congress.
(2) JOINT ANTI-COMMUNISM.- A few years ago,
Japan made such a suggestion on many occasions. We did
not accept it because we feared that our military and
civil affairs might be interfered with. Now the Japanese
Government has clearly stated that a Sino-Japanese Anti-
Communist Agreement should be signed in the spirit of the
Japan-Italo-German Anti-Communist Pact. The object of
guarding against Communists is to suppress plots for
disturbances by the Communists; it will have no adverse
effect upon the relations between China and Soviet Russia.
Since the members of the Chinese Communist Party have
expressed their willingness to fight for the Three
Principles of the People, they should give up their
organization and propaganda and abolish their army and
subject themselves completely to the law of China.
Anything that is done against the Three Principles of the
People, the supreme principle for the foundation of the
Republic of China, must be suppressed.
(3) ECONOMIC RAPPROCHEMENT.- This point has
been repeatedly suggested by Japan to China during the

1938年12月31日。晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸（香港电）：-

汪精卫致国民党中央总部电文
建议与日本开启和平谈判。

汪精卫先生已向国民党中央总部发出如下电报：-

今年四月，全国代表大会发表宣言，阐述中国抗战之宗旨如下：-

“自《塘沽协定》以来，我方对日采取隐忍态度，旨在试图以和平手段保全华北各省，并寻求东北四省问题之公正解决。在政治方面，我方最低限度之诉求为保全中国之主权与经济，谋求互利与平等。”

继1937年7月卢沟桥事变发生后，中国被迫进行抗战。本人现已阅悉日本政府于12月22日发表的关于调整中日关系基本原则之声明；该声明包含以下三点：-

（1）善邻友好。- 日本对中国无领土野心，亦不要求军事费用赔偿。日本不仅将尊重中国之主权，并将归还其在华租界，废除治外法权，从而使中国获得完全独立。

既然日本政府已发表此项声明，我们将有能力通过和平手段保护华北各省，收复作战期间丧失之所有领土，并保全中国之主权及行政完整。据此，我们可依照全国代表大会所发表之宣言，寻求东北四省问题之合理解决。

（2）共同防共。- 数年前，日本曾多次提出此项建议。我们当时未予接受，因担心我国军政事务受到干涉。现日本政府已明确声明，应本着《日意德防共协定》之精神，签订中日防共协定。防范共产党之目的，在于镇压共产党之扰乱阴谋；此举不会对中苏关系产生不利影响。鉴于中国共产党党员已表示愿意为三民主义而战，他们应当放弃其组织与宣传，解散其军队，并完全服从中国法律。任何违背作为中华民国建国最高原则之三民主义的行为，必须予以镇压。

（3）经济提携。- 此点在日本对华关系中曾被多次提及，在此期间

pages.en:
December 31, 1938. Morning Translation.

past few years. Now the Japanese Government clearly
declares that Japan will respect China's sovereign rights
and her administrative integrity and that Japan has no
desire to have sole control of economics in China nor has
she a desire to request China to restrict the interests
of any third Power in China. She desires economic
rapprochement on the principles of equality. Therefore,
we should accept this suggestion.
After careful consideration, I am of the
opinion that the National Government should adopt the
above three points as a basis for a sincere exchange of
views with the Japanese Government in an effort to restore
peace. The statement of the Japanese Government of
November 3 modifies the attitude as outlined in the
declaration of January 16. If the National Government
enters into peace talks on the basis of the foregoing
three points, then the door to peace parleys has been
opened. The object of China's war of resistance is to
secure the independence and existence of the nation.
The war has lasted over a year and China's sufferings have
been great. If China can end the war by an equitable
peace with her existence and independence assured, her
object will have been attained. The aforementioned
three points should form the basic principles of any peace
talk. Careful consideration, however, should be given
to the conditions attached to these three points: the
withdrawal of all the Japanese forces from China which
should be acceptable should be effected quickly and should
be made to cover all places. If permission were to be
given for the stationing of troops in specially designated
areas during the life of the so-called anti-Comintern pact,
such areas should be limited only to the vicinity of Inner
Mongolia; if done in any other way, it would affect the
integrity of China's sovereign and administrative rights.
After this China can devote her energy to reconstruction
as a modern nation. Careful study should be made to
ascertain the causes of rupture in districts bordering on
China and Japan and each party should be made aware of its
responsibilities. Hereafter, China should adopt friendly
relations, while Japan in particular should instruct her
people to abandon their traditional thoughts of aggression
on China and should adopt an attitude of friendship to
China in her educational policy. This will set up the
foundations of a permanent peace between the two countries.
All of us should strive hard for the welfare of the Orient
and should co-operate with other nations for the
establishment of a lasting peace and order on the Pacific
and in the world. I respectfully make this suggestion
for consideration and in the hope that it will be
accepted."

Standard publishes the following brief comment :-

Criticism of Wang Ching-Wei

Wang Ching-wei yesterday issued a statement
suggesting a reconciliation with Japan. If this report
be true, then it would be the greatest suicidal report of
the year 1938.
pages.zh:
1938年12月31日。晨间译文。

过去几年。如今日本政府明确宣称，日本将尊重中国的主权权利及其行政完整，且日本无意单独控制中国的经济，亦无意要求中国限制任何第三国在华的利益。她希望基于平等原则实现经济亲善。因此，我们应当接受这一建议。
经过慎重考虑，我认为国民政府应以以上三点为基础，与日本政府真诚交换意见，以努力恢复和平。日本政府11月3日的声明修正了1月16日宣言中所概述的态度。如果国民政府以前述三点为基础进行和谈，那么和平谈判的大门就已经打开。中国抗战的目的是确保国家的独立与生存。战争已持续一年多，中国遭受了巨大的苦难。如果中国能以公平的和平结束战争，并确保其生存与独立，那么她的目标就已达成。上述三点应构成任何和平谈判的基本原则。然而，对于附属于这三点的条件应予以仔细考量：所有日军撤出中国，这一可接受的条件应迅速实施，并应涵盖所有地区。如果在所谓的《反共产国际协定》有效期间允许在特别指定区域驻军，此类区域应仅限于内蒙古附近；若以其他方式处理，则将影响中国主权和行政权利的完整。此后，中国可以致力于作为一个现代国家的重建工作。应仔细研究导致中日毗邻地区关系破裂的原因，并使各方认识到其责任。今后，中国应采取友好关系，而日本尤其应教导其人民放弃传统的侵华思想，并在其教育政策中采取对华友好的态度。这将为两国之间的永久和平奠定基础。我们所有人都应为东方的福祉而努力，并与其他国家合作，在太平洋及世界范围内建立持久的和平与秩序。我谨提出此建议供考虑，并希望其被接受。”

《标准报》发表如下简短评论：——

对汪精卫的批评

汪精卫昨日发表声明，建议与日本和解。如果此报道属实，那将是1938年最大的自杀性报道。

pages.en:
December 31, 1938. Morning Translation.

There are many ways to end one's life,
but why should one choose a Japanese sword with which
to commit harakiri? From now on in what light will
Wang Ching-wei be regarded by the people? What sort
of a degenerate is he to be described in the history of
China? The situation is truly beyond comprehension.
Wang is not only digging his own grave.
If Wang Ching-wei really wishes to end his
life, it will not have any effect on the war of resistance,
because individually he is a man of no importance. Common
sense tells us that he cannot have fallen so low!

Shun Pao publishes the following editorial :-

Wang Ching-wei's Absurd Suggestion

According to a telegram received from
Hongkong this morning, Wang Ching-wei has made a suggestion
to the National Government that it accept Japan's peace
proposals on condition that the Japanese forces withdraw
from China, while China will accept the three principles
of "rapprochement", "joint anti-Comintern" and "economic
co-operation". Wang Ching-wei's suggestion contravenes
China's national policy of reconstruction by a war of
resistance and is contrary to the wishes of the people.
Wang is known for his great wisdom, but his present
action which is alienating himself from the affections
of the people, is most deplorable.
China's national policy was decided by a
meeting of the Kuomintang and its decision was supported
by the People's Political Council. The supreme National
Defence Council carries out the national policy. Wang
Ching-wei is a prominent member of all three organizations,
yet he is now violating the decision which he, as a
member of the three organizations, had previously
supported. Thus, the Chinese people cannot pardon
him.
The most striking point of his statement
is the demand that a withdrawal of the Japanese forces
from China must be total, prompt and universal, but such a
demand was made by the Nationalist Government immediately
after the Lukuochiao Incident and because of Japan's
rejection of the demand the war started and has lasted
18 months. If Japan will really withdraw her troops
from China, peace can be established at once. This is
clear even to a school boy and much more so to an
experienced man like Mr. Wang Ching-wei. The reason
why peace could not be preserved and a war could not be
avoided is because Japan desires to compel China to
accept terms that will ruin China. Mr. Wang knows this,
yet he is now advocating the withdrawal of Japanese troops,
friendship, anti-comintern collaboration and economic
co-operation.
If China is willing to accept terms that
will place her in the position of a slave, there ~~there~~
will be no more puppets or idols or running dogs and
there will be no need for Japan to station troops in
China.
General Chiang's speech has already referred
to Prince Konoye's speech as a plan to ruin China.
Prince Konoye's speech has revealed Japan's ambitions;
it deceives nobody except perhaps Mr. Wang Ching-wei!
pages.zh:
1938年12月31日。晨间译稿。

结束生命的方式有很多种，
但为何要选择用日本刀来
切腹自尽？从今往后，
汪精卫在民众眼中将如何看待？
在中国历史上，他将被描述为
何种程度的堕落之徒？局势实在令人费解。
汪不仅是在自掘坟墓。
如果汪精卫真的想结束自己的生命，
这对抗战不会有任何影响，
因为就个人而言，他是一个无足轻重的人。
常识告诉我们，他不可能堕落到如此地步！

《申报》发表以下社论：——

汪精卫的荒谬建议

据今晨收到的来自
香港的电报称，汪精卫已向国民政府提出建议，
要求接受日本的和平提议，条件是日本军队
撤出中国，而中国则接受“亲善”、“共同防共”
和“经济合作”三项原则。汪精卫的建议违背了
中国通过抗战进行重建的国家政策，也违背了
人民的意愿。汪以睿智著称，但他目前这种
疏远民心的举动，最令人痛心。
中国的国家政策是由国民党会议决定的，
其决定得到了国民参政会的支持。最高国防会议
负责执行国家政策。汪精卫是这三个机构的
重要成员，然而他现在却违反了他作为这三个机构
的成员此前曾支持过的决定。因此，中国人民不能
原谅他。
他的声明中最引人注目的一点是，
要求日本军队从中国撤军必须是彻底、迅速和普遍的，
但这一要求是国民政府在卢沟桥事变后立即提出的，
而由于日本拒绝了这一要求，战争爆发并持续了
18个月。如果日本真的将其军队撤出中国，
和平可以立即建立。这一点连小学生都清楚，
更不用说像汪精卫先生这样经验丰富的人了。
和平无法维持、战争无法避免的原因，
是因为日本企图强迫中国接受将毁灭中国的条款。
汪先生深知这一点，然而他现在却倡导日军撤退、
友好、反共合作和经济合作。
如果中国愿意接受使其处于奴隶地位的条款，
那么就不再需要傀儡、偶像或走狗，
日本也就没有必要在中国驻军了。
蒋委员长的讲话已将近卫文麿亲王的讲话称为
毁灭中国的计划。近卫亲王的讲话已暴露了日本的野心；
它骗不了任何人，或许除了汪精卫先生！

December 30, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao (Noon Edition):

WANG CHING-WEI MAY GO ABROAD

The future movements of Mr. Wang Ching-wei are gradually becoming more clarified. It seems that he will go to Hongkong from Hanoi and after recuperating for a little while in the Colony, he will proceed to Europe in his private capacity to improve his health. Tseng min (曾仲鳴), the former Vice Minister of Railways of the National Government, Lou Kwang-sung (羅廣生), a doctor, and several others will accompany him.

Taking advantage of Wang Ching-wei's departure from Chungking, the Japanese and the puppet authorities are making every endeavour to induce him to join them. According to a report secured from a reliable source, Chen Chung-fu (陳中孚), who is a pro-Japanese and has close relations with General Doihara, has secretly arrived at Hongkong with the intention of inducing Wang to co-operate with the Japanese and to take up the leadership in the new central regime. However, persons closely connected with Wang Ching-wei state that Wang would never allow himself to be misled in this way.

Ta Mei Pao (Tientsin telegram):

Invitation Extended to Wang Ching-wei to Visit North China

On December 28, the "Yung Pao" (庸報), an organ of the Japanese military in Tientsin, published an article inviting Wang Ching-wei to proceed to North China and promising him pardon for his past crimes. The article states that a very high position will be given Wang Ching-wei.

The paper concluded by warning that unless Wang Ching-wei accepts this invitation, the Japanese authorities will regard him as an offender of the same grade as General Chiang Kai-shek.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated Dec.29:

According to a report issued by the United Press of China, Mr. Chu Min-nyi (褚民), a member of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, will leave Shanghai for Hongkong in a few days to interview Mr. Wang Ching-wei.

In a Press interview, Mr. Chu stated that the report was absolutely untrue for he had made no preparations to leave for Hongkong. When asked as to whether Mr. Wang had arrived at Hongkong or whether Mr. Wang may proceed to Hongkong, Mr. Chu replied that he had no information.

1938年12月30日。下午译件。

《大美晚报》（午刊）：

汪精卫或将出国

汪精卫先生今后的动向逐渐明朗。据悉，他将从河内前往香港，在殖民地稍事休养后，将以私人身份前往欧洲疗养。前国民政府铁道部次长曾仲鸣、医生罗广生（Lou Kwang-sung，音译）等数人将随行。

趁汪精卫离开重庆之机，日本方面及傀儡当局正竭力诱使其加入。据来自可靠渠道的报告称，亲日且与土肥原将军关系密切的陈中孚已秘密抵达香港，意图劝说汪精卫与日本合作，并在新中央政权中担任领导职务。然而，与汪精卫关系密切的人士表示，汪绝不会以此种方式受人蒙蔽。

《大美报》（天津电）：

邀汪精卫访问华北

12月28日，天津日军机关报《庸报》发表文章，邀请汪精卫前往华北，并承诺赦免其既往罪行。文章称，将给予汪精卫极高的职位。

该报最后警告称，除非汪精卫接受此邀请，否则日本当局将视其为与蒋介石将军同等级别的罪犯。

12月29日《华美晚报》：

据合众社中国分社发布的报道，国民党中央执行委员会成员褚民谊（Chu Min-nyi，原文如此，应为褚民谊）将于数日后离开上海前往香港，会晤汪精卫先生。

在接受记者采访时，褚先生表示该报道纯属不实，因为他并未做前往香港的任何准备。当被问及汪先生是否已抵达香港或是否会前往香港时，褚先生答复称他并无相关信息。

Date 15 3 40

MAR 15 1940

Support Voiced for
Wang Ching-wei

Head of Ta Min Hui Lauds
Peace Movement Leader on
Eve of New Regime

Nanking, Mar. 14.
Third party Powers today were enjoined against "unnecessarily obstructing the peace movement" in China by Dr. Kung Hsien-keng, president of the Ta Min Hui, a civic organization in Central China.
Pointing out that Sino-Japanese peace would not mean the exclusion of third party Powers from China, but would guarantee "a reasonable development of their legitimate rights and interests in China," he urged other nations to "respect the position of Japan and China in East Asia and appreciate the desire of the Chinese people.
Dr. Kung, commenting upon the manifesto issued on Tuesday by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, who will become the central figure in the proposed new Central Government, declared that the Kuomintang leader had laid down in his statement "the golden rules for the rehabilitation of China."
Japan, Dr. Kung continued, had adhered to the basic principles of the Konoye Statement of December 22, 1938, which laid down the formula "for the establishment of a lasting peace in East Asia" through Japanese respect of China's independence and territorial integrity and the mutual prosperity of the two countries.
"Trusting such genuine Japanese aspirations, we should support Mr. Wang's peace movement to advance along the road to the development of East Asia," Dr. Kung stated.—Domei.

FILE

U.S. Expected to Ignore Wang

Washington, Mar. 14.
State Department officials were silent today regarding yesterday's announcement by the Japanese Premier, Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai, on Japan's policy regarding China and the proposed new Chinese Government under Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
It was understood that the United States would ignore Mr. Wang.
The official attitude of the United States would be to regard Mr. Wang merely as an arm of the Japanese Government and thus no direct American recognition would be accorded either to Mr. Wang or any government that he might form under the present circumstances, responsible quarters said.—United Press.

日期 1940 年 3 月 15 日

1940 年 3 月 15 日

汪精卫获得支持之声

大民会会长在新政权前夕赞扬和平运动领袖

南京，3 月 14 日电。华中民间组织大民会会长孔宪庚博士今日告诫第三方列强不要“无端阻碍”中国的“和平运动”。
他指出，中日和平并不意味着将第三方列强排除出中国，而是会保证它们在华“合法权利和利益的合理发展”，他敦促其他国家“尊重日本和中国在东亚的地位，并体谅中国人民的愿望”。
孔博士评论了即将成为拟议中的新中央政府核心人物的汪精卫先生于周二发表的宣言，宣称这位国民党领导人在其声明中为中国复兴制定了“黄金法则”。
孔博士继续说，日本一直恪守 1938 年 12 月 22 日近卫声明的基本原则，该原则确立了通过日本尊重中国的独立和领土完整以及两国共同繁荣来“建立东亚持久和平”的公式。
孔博士表示：“相信日本这种真诚的愿望，我们应该支持汪先生的和平运动沿着发展东亚的道路前进。”——同盟社。

存档

美国预计将无视汪精卫

华盛顿，3 月 14 日电。国务院官员今日对日本首相米内光政海军上将昨日关于日本对华政策及汪精卫先生领导下拟议中的新中国政府的公告保持沉默。
据悉，美国将无视汪精卫先生。
有关负责方面表示，美国的官方态度是将汪精卫先生仅视为日本政府的一个分支，因此在此种情况下，美国不会直接承认汪精卫先生或他可能组建的任何政府。——合众社。

FEB 8 1940

Wang Regime
Names Picked

Chungking Newspapers
Publish Shanghai
Meeting List

(Reuter's Agency)
CHUNGKING, Feb. 8—Chinese
newspapers here yesterday publish-
ed what was alleged to be a list
of the members of the so-called
Central Political Council, which
will meet in Shanghai in the near
future for the formation of the
"new central regime."
The list includes ten representa-
tives of the "Orthodox" Kuomin-
tang: Messrs. Wang Ching-wei,
Chow Fu-hai, Chen Kung-po, Mei
Sze-ping, Chen Chun-pu, Lin Pah-
sen, Chu Ming-yi, Pu Tung, Kao
Tsung-wu (now dropped) and Miss
Tseng Hsing (sister of Tseng
Chung-min, who was assassinated
in Hanoi last year).
There are four representatives of
the Peiping Provisional Govern-
ment: Messrs. Wang Keh-min,
Wang Yi-tang and Tang Er-ho
and General Chih Sieh-yuan.
The Nanking Reformed Govern-
ment will, it is stated, also have
four representatives: Messrs. Liang
Hung-chi, Chen Chun, Wen Tsung-
yao and Jen Yuan-tao.
Ten representatives of other
parties are named: Messrs. Chen
Chung-fu, Ho Shih-cheng, Kiang
Kang-hu, Tang Hsien-min, Pu
Siao-an, Chiang Yen-hsing, Chang
Yi-chen, Tseng Hsin-shu, Chao
Shu-yung, and one other who, it
is stated, will deny his association
with Wang Ching-wei.
Prince Teh and En-ke-pa-tu
will be among the Mongolian and
Tibetan representatives.

会议名单

（路透社）
重庆，2月8日电——此地中文报纸昨日刊登了一份据称是所谓“中央政治委员会”成员的名单，该委员会将于近期在上海召开会议，以组建“新中央政权”。
该名单包括十名“正统”国民党代表：汪精卫先生、周佛海先生、陈公博先生、梅思平先生、陈春圃先生、林柏生先生、朱明义先生、卜东先生、高宗武先生（现已除名）以及曾醒女士（去年在河内被暗杀的曾仲铭之妹）。
北平临时政府有四名代表：王克敏先生、王揖唐先生、唐尔和先生以及齐燮元将军。
据悉，南京维新政府也将有四名代表：梁鸿志先生、陈群先生、温宗尧先生和任援道先生。
其他党派的十名代表被点名：陈中孚先生、何世桢先生、江亢虎先生、唐贤民先生、卜少安先生、蒋燕兴先生、张一真先生、曾心叔先生、赵书雍先生，以及另一名据称将否认其与汪精卫有关联的人士。
德王和恩克巴图将作为蒙古和西藏代表出席。

EVENING ECHO

DEC 1 7 1939

Steps Are Taken
For New Central
China Government

Academy For Officers
Inaugurated With
1,000 Men

STUDENT PARADE
CARRYING RIFLES

Ex-Wuhan Garrison
Commander Chief
Of Academy

First steps towards the creation of an army for the projected Central Government of China under Mr. Wang Ching-wei were taken recently with the inauguration of a Central Military Officers Training Corps of 1,000 men.

Ceremonies which took place near Shanghai marking the opening of the academy for the training of officers included a review of troops by Mr. Wang, director of the academy, who will be the central figure of the proposed new Central Government of China.

Among those attending the ceremonies were Mr. Chen Kung-po, one-time Minister of Industries and Railways of the Chinese Government; Gen. Pao Wen-yeh, an outstanding Manchurian officer and agent of Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang at Gen. Chiang Kai-shek's headquarters; Gen. Yeh Peng, former Huhan garrison commander; Mr. Chou Fo-hai, Mr. Chu Ming-yi **〔此处转录不清〕** National Salvation Through Peace Movement started by Mr. Wang.

Students With Rifles

Students appeared in the reviewing parade fully equipped with rifles and steel helmets.

The review was followed by the singing of the Orthodox Kuomintang anthem, after which a salute was given to the portrait of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, and a stirring address delivered by Mr. Wang.

Addresses were also delivered by Mr. Chen, representing the Central Executive Committee of the Orthodox Kuomintang; Mr. Pao Wen-yeh, a representative of the Military Affairs Commission, and Mr. Yeh Peng, who will be in charge of education at the academy.

Ceremonies closed with the shouting of Mr. Wang's slogan: "Peace, Anti-Communism, and National Reconstruction."

Four Battalions

Students at the military training academy will be formed into four battalions. One will be devoted to political training and consists of college graduates selected from various parts of China. The other battalions will be composed of former military officers under Gen. Chiang Kai-shek who were hand-picked from all parts of China.

A two-years course of study will be given at the academy. Coupled with operations from Tenghai into Fukien by Gen. Hwang Ta-wu's National Reconstruction Army, the creation of the Central Military Officers Training Corps and the establishment of a Military Affairs Council were regarded as important strides towards the establishment of strong military support for Mr. Wang's movement.

It was noteworthy that no high Japanese Army officers attended the ceremonies of the opening of the academy.

《晚声报》

1939年12月17日

为建立新的华中政府
采取步骤

军官学院成立
招收一千人

学生持步枪游行

前武汉卫戍司令
任学院院长

为组建汪精卫先生麾下拟议中的中国政府中央军队，最近迈出了第一步，即成立了一所拥有一千人的中央军事军官训练团。

在上海附近举行的军官培训学院开学典礼仪式上，包括由学院院长、也是拟议中的新中国中央政府核心人物汪先生检阅部队。

出席典礼的有：曾任中国政府实业部及铁道部部长的陈公博先生；杰出的满洲籍军官、张学良将军在蒋介石将军总部的代表鲍文樾将军；前武汉卫戍司令叶蓬将军；周佛海先生；朱穆一 **〔此处转录不清〕** 汪先生发起的“和平救国运动”。

学生携带步枪

参加检阅游行的学生全副武装，配备步枪和钢盔。

检阅结束后，齐唱正统国民党党歌，随后向孙中山博士遗像致敬，并由汪先生发表激动人心的演说。

代表正统国民党中央执行委员会的陈先生、代表军事委员会的鲍文樾先生，以及将在学院主管教育工作的叶蓬先生也分别发表了讲话。

典礼在呼喊汪先生的口号“和平、反共、建国”中结束。

四个营

军事训练学院的学生将编为四个营。其中一个营专司政治训练，由从中国各地选拔的大学毕业生组成。其余各营则由从全国各地精心挑选的前蒋介石将军麾下的军官组成。

学院学制为两年。随着黄大伟将军的建国军从腾海（音译）向福建进军，中央军事军官训练团的成立以及军事委员会的建立，被视为朝着为汪先生的运动建立强大军事支持迈出的重要步伐。

值得注意的是，没有日本陆军高级军官出席学院开学典礼。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
NOV 29 1939
Extraordinary Story Of
Shanghai Meeting
Mr. Lo Ching-tao Gives Account In Chungking Of
What Happened At Sixth Plenary Session Of
Kuomintang Here; Says He Was Kidnapped

CHUNGKING, Nov. 28.—Inter-
esting revelations of what is alleg-
ed to have occurred at the so-
called "Sixth Plenary Session of
the Central Executive Committee
of the Kuomintang" at Shanghai
on August 29, under the chairman-
ship of Mr. Wang Ching-wei,
were made to-day by Mr. Lo
Ching-tao, a member of the Cen-
tral Executive Committee.
Mr. Lo says he was kidnapped
by Mr. Wang Ching-wei's follow-
ers to attend the session as a
member of the Presidium, but he
escaped after the meeting to Hong-
kong, whence he flew to Chung-
king.
Speaking at a press conference
this afternoon, Mr. Lo stated that
Mr. Chu Min-yi called on him on
the morning of August 29, inviting
him to lunch.
There was, however, no meal, he
said. Instead he was driven by car
to the home of General Chen Tiao-
yuan in the French Concession,
and then near to Jessfield Park,
where he was taken to a room to
meet Messrs. Wang Ching-wei,
Chow Fu-hai, Mei Sze-ping and
Pu Tung.

Unusual Procedure
Mr. Wang, according to Mr. Lo,
requested him to attend the "sixth
plenary session of the Central
Executive Committee."
After explaining that Japan had
agreed to recognize the new
national government and central
Kuomintang to be formed, the
Kuomintang flag and the Three
People's Principles, Mr. Wang is
alleged to have requested Mr. Lo
to be responsible for Mongolian and
Tibetan affairs in the new govern-
ment.
After this, they were taken
downstairs to a large hall, where
the meeting was held.
Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Mr. Lo
declared, proposed seven members
for the presidium, namely, Messrs.
Wang Ching-wei, Yang Kwei-yi,
Chiao Ying, Chow Fu-hai, Mei Sze-
ping, Pu Tung and himself.

Unusual Procedure
Mr. Wang also proposed he said,
to increase the members of the
Central Executive Committee to
260, adding 100 new members.
The names of these new mem-
bers were read out by Mr. Wang,
who is alleged to have justified
this unusual procedure of appoint-
ing new C.E.C. members without
election by mentioning a similar
procedure once adopted by Dr.
Sun Yat-sen.
Mr. Wang, however, Mr. Lo
proceeded, only appointed 80 new
members, reserving the other 20
for later appointments.
None of the 80 was known to
Mr. Lo.

Documents Destroyed
All documents and the agenda
of the meeting were destroyed by
fire, before the delegates dispersed,
"for the safety of members of the
delegation."
Mr. Lo said Mr. Wang also in-
formed him that Mr. Yang Kwei-
yi was a retired military man who
was establishing contacts with
Chinese military leaders, that Mr.
Chiao Ying was responsible for
contacting party delegates in North
China, while Messrs. Chow Fu-
hai and Mei Sze-ping were instru-
mental in completing negotiations
for peace with the Japanese au-
thorities.
Mr. Wang was elected "chair-
man" of the Central Kuomintang,
and the entire session lasted only
five hours, after which the dele-
gates were carted away in trucks.
Mr. Lo added that he was urged
to stay at the residence of General
Chen Tiao-yuan, but he declined.
—Reuter.

《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年11月29日
上海会议的离奇故事
罗敬陶先生在重庆讲述国民党在此间举行的第六届中央执行委员会全体会议的情况；称其遭绑架

重庆，11月28日电。——中央执行委员会委员罗敬陶先生今日披露了据称于8月29日在上海、在汪精卫先生主持下举行的所谓“国民党第六届中央执行委员会全体会议”上发生的内幕，内容引人关注。
罗先生称，他被汪精卫先生的追随者绑架，以主席团成员的身份出席会议，但他在会后逃往香港，随后从香港飞抵重庆。
罗先生在今日下午举行的记者招待会上表示，朱民谊先生于8月29日上午拜访了他，邀请他共进午餐。
然而，他说并没有用餐。相反，他被汽车载至法租界陈调元将军的寓所，随后又被带至靠近兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）的地方，在那里他被带入一个房间，会见了汪精卫、周佛海、梅思平和濮通诸先生。

不寻常的程序
据罗先生称，汪先生要求他出席“中央执行委员会第六届全体会议”。
汪先生在解释日本已同意承认即将成立的新国民政府及国民党中央，并提及国民党旗帜和三民主义后，据称要求罗先生在新政府中负责蒙藏事务。
此后，他们被带下楼进入一个大厅，会议便在此举行。
罗先生宣称，汪精卫先生提名了七位主席团成员，即：汪精卫、杨揆一、乔英、周佛海、梅思平、濮通以及他自己。

不寻常的程序
罗先生还说，汪先生还提议将中央执行委员会委员人数增加至260人，新增100名委员。
这些新委员的名单由汪先生宣读，据称汪先生通过提及孙中山博士曾采用过的类似程序，为这种不经选举而任命新的中央执行委员会委员的不寻常做法进行辩护。
然而，罗先生接着说，汪先生仅任命了80名新委员，将其余20名留待日后任命。
这80人中无一人是罗先生所认识的。

文件被销毁
在代表们解散之前，所有文件和会议议程均被焚毁，“为了代表团成员的安全”。
罗先生说，汪先生还告诉他，杨揆一是一位退役军人，正在与中国军事领导人建立联系；乔英负责与华北地区的党代表联络；而周佛海和梅思平两位先生则在完成与日本当局的和平谈判中发挥了重要作用。
汪先生当选为国民党中央“主席”，整个会议仅持续了五个小时，之后代表们被卡车运走。
罗先生补充说，有人劝他留在陈调元将军的寓所，但他拒绝了。
——路透社。

（批注：档案 C 5/12 警司 1月
无信息 C 11/29
5/12 1月）

CHINA PRESS
DEC 6 1939
8486
Wu Pei-fu Could Have Been Saved, Says German Doctor

(United Press)

PEIPING, Dec. 5.—Dr. K. Stickforth, chief surgeon of the German Hospital here, indicated today that Marshal Wu Pei-fu might have had a chance of living had he taken his advice and had been operated on at the German Hospital.

Marshal Wu failed to leave either a will or a statement for China, his secretaries tearfully told the United Press today after the Japanese spokesman had announced that Japan had suffered a great loss by the warlord's death.

The German surgeon said that he had been called to attend to the late Marshal after the veteran warlord had been suffering for six days.

On Sunday, he said, the infection from the decayed tooth spread to the cheek and then to the throat, threatening his breathing.

Dr. Stickforth said he advised that an operation be performed at the German Hospital, but Marshal Wu and his family refused. His family objected to the Marshal's removal to the German Hospital, which is located in the Legation Quarter, Dr. Stickforth said.

Although the operation was not of a serious nature he refused to undertake it at Marshal Wu's home, Dr. Stickforth said.

A Japanese physician, Dr. Terada, called on him yesterday and said that there was no chance of the old warlord dying suddenly, the German surgeon asserted.

Died During Operation

Marshal Wu, however, died during the operation yesterday, Dr. Stickforth said.

During the first six days of his illness, Marshal Wu was treated by Chinese herb doctors for kidney and stomach ailments which retarded the treatment for his tooth, Dr. Stickforth said.

"The death of Wu Pei-fu is a loss to Japan," the Japanese spokesman declared today.

"He was the most impartial of Chinese generals and had great influence over the Chinese people, especially in north China.

"Loss to Japan"

"If he had co-operated with Japan his aid would have been invaluable to the last in Japan's," he said.

"All who cared for Wu Pei-fu tried in every way to save him," he concluded.

The tooth was removed, it was reported by Dr. Ito, who had made the warlord's false teeth, and Dr. Terada when Marshal Wu died.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

Demand Denied

(Reuters)

PEIPING, Dec. 5.—Questioned at a press conference regarding reports that Marshal Wu Pei-fu, China's warrior poet, who died yesterday afternoon, had recently refused a Japanese demand to head the army of the "Provincial Government" of Peiping, a Japanese spokesman said there was no truth in these rumors.

From reliable local sources, however, it is learned the Marshal had again turned down requests to serve in a "puppet" organization, insisting that Japanese troops should be first withdrawn from China.

He had been repeatedly approached by the Japanese, but adamantly refused to "co-operate" in the new regime.

Marshal Wu Pei-fu, it is learned, died between 4 p.m. and 5 p.m. yesterday, following infection caused by extraction of a tooth. He was attended by a local German doctor who was present when the Marshal died. Immediately afterwards, it is understood, a cordon of Japanese gendarmes was thrown round the house.

The Marshal's illness was mentioned for the first time in the local Chinese-language press today, it being reported he was attended by several local foreign and Chinese doctors.

Wu Given Tribute

(United Press)

MANILA, Dec. 5.—Marshal Wu Pei-fu, colorful Chinese warlord who died yesterday from blood-poisoning in Peiping, was paid a warm tribute in the editorial columns of La Vanguardia. The editorial recounted the veteran warrior's characteristics, including his refusal to join the puppet regimes of his friends until they had left the foreign concessions in Tientsin. The editorial concluded by saying that "he was a great character."

Wu's Death Mysterious, Say Chinese

(United Press)

CHUNGKING, Dec. 5.—News of the death of Marshal Wu Pei-fu at Peiping yesterday came as a painful surprise and was generally regarded by officialdom here today as a "death of mysterious circumstances."

Officials pointed out that it was only natural that the Japanese doctors who operated on the warlord were to be suspected of having something to do with his death since he had resisted Japanese efforts to make him emerge from retirement and assume an important post in a Japanese controlled regime.

Although overthrown thirteen years ago by the Kuomintang, Marshal Wu was respected by all Chinese, especially during the past year when he refused to accept Japanese demands for his emergence from retirement practically at the point of bayonets, competent Chinese quarters said.

Government circles were reported to have suggested that a posthumous honor be granted him to mark his patriotism.

General Ho Ying-chin, Minister of War, prepared to dispatch condolences to Marshal Wu's family. Gen. Ho became close friends with Marshal Wu when staying at Peiping five years ago.

Marshal Wu's friends here considered him to have been the only powerful and influential Chinese in the past three decades who was the least westernized and the most anti-foreign.

Chungking leaders, including Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and President Lin Sen, are expected to send messages of condolence to Marshal Wu's family.

The National Government is to issue a special mandate praising the late warlord for his patriotism and is to make a financial grant for his funeral.

《字林西报》
1939年12月6日
8486
德国医生称吴佩孚本可获救

（合众社）

北平，12月5日电——驻此间德国医院首席外科医生K. Stickforth博士今日表示，如果吴佩孚元帅听从其建议并在德国医院接受手术，或许尚有生还之机。

在日本发言人宣称日本因这位军阀之死遭受重大损失后，吴元帅的秘书们今日含泪告诉合众社，吴元帅未留下遗嘱，也未给中国留下任何声明。

这位德国外科医生称，在这位资深军阀患病六天后，他被召去诊治已故的吴元帅。

他说，周日时，坏牙引起的感染扩散至脸颊，继而蔓延至喉咙，危及呼吸。

Stickforth博士称，他建议在德国医院进行手术，但吴元帅及其家属予以拒绝。Stickforth博士说，其家属反对将吴元帅移送至位于使馆区的德国医院。

Stickforth博士称，尽管手术性质并不严重，但他拒绝在吴元帅家中施行手术。

这位德国外科医生断言，日本医生寺田（Terada）博士昨日曾拜访他，并称这位老军阀不会突然死亡。

术中身亡

然而，Stickforth博士称，吴元帅在昨日的手术过程中去世。

Stickforth博士称，在患病的前六天里，吴元帅一直由中医治疗肾胃疾患，这延误了对他牙齿的治疗。

“吴佩孚之死是日本的损失，”日本发言人今日宣称。

“他是中国将领中最公正无私的一位，对中国人民，尤其是华北民众，拥有巨大影响力。”

“日本的损失”

“如果他能与日本合作，他的援助对日本而言将是无价的，”他说。

“所有关心吴佩孚的人都竭尽全力试图挽救他，”他总结道。

据报道，为吴元帅制作假牙的伊藤（Ito）博士和寺田（Terada）博士在吴元帅去世时拔除了那颗牙齿。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

要求被拒

（路透社）

北平，12月5日电——在记者会上被问及有关报道时，一位日本发言人称，所谓昨日午后去世的中国“诗人武将”吴佩孚元帅近期曾拒绝日本方面要求其出任北平“省政府”军队首领的说法纯属谣言，毫无事实依据。

然而，从当地可靠消息源获悉，吴元帅再次拒绝了在“傀儡”组织中任职的请求，并坚持要求日军首先撤出中国。

日本人曾多次接触他，但他坚决拒绝在新政权中“合作”。

据悉，吴佩孚元帅于昨日下午4时至5时之间去世，死因是拔牙后引发的感染。一名当地德国医生对其进行了诊治，并在吴元帅去世时在场。据信，随后立即有日本宪兵包围了该住宅。

当地中文报刊今日首次提及吴元帅的病情，报道称有多名当地外籍医生和中国医生为其诊治。

向吴致敬

（合众社）

马尼拉，12月5日电——昨日在北平因败血症去世的中国色彩鲜明的军阀吴佩孚元帅，在《先锋报》（La Vanguardia）的社论栏中获得了热情的赞誉。该社论回顾了这位资深战士的特征，包括他拒绝加入其朋友们的傀儡政权，直到他们离开天津的外国租界。社论最后称，“他是一个伟大的人物。”

中国人称吴之死疑点重重

（合众社）

重庆，12月5日电——昨日吴佩孚元帅在北平去世的消息传来，令人痛心且意外，此地官方今日普遍视其为“死因可疑”。

官员们指出，既然吴元帅抵制日本方面迫使其复出并在日本控制的政权中担任要职的努力，那么对他进行手术的日本医生被怀疑与其死亡有关，也是自然之事。

中方权威人士称，尽管吴元帅在十三年前被国民党推翻，但他受到所有中国人的尊敬，尤其是在过去一年里，他在几乎刺刀相逼的情况下仍拒绝接受日本方面要求其复出的要求。

据报道，政府圈内人士建议授予其身后荣誉，以表彰其爱国精神。

军政部长何应钦将军准备向吴元帅家属致唁。何将军五年前在北平时与吴元帅结为密友。

此间吴元帅的朋友认为，他是过去三十年中唯一权势显赫、影响力巨大，且西化程度最低、最排外的中国人。

预计包括蒋介石委员长和林森主席在内的重庆领导人将向吴元帅家属发送唁电。

国民政府将发布特别命令，赞扬这位已故军阀的爱国精神，并将拨款资助其葬礼。

WANG CHING WEI MAINTAINS THREE POLITICAL ORGANIZATIONS
IN SHANGHAI.

According to information secured from a fairly
reliable source, Mr. Wang Ching Wei is claimed to have three
secret organizations in Shanghai, which are propagating his
peace campaign here. They are as follows:- The "Reorganization
Fellowship of the Kuomintang of China" (中國國民黨改組同志會) which
is under the leadership of his right hand man, Mr. Chen Kung-
po, former minister of Industries. The organization was
established during the time when General Chiang Kai-shek was
at war with General Feng Yu-hsiang and General Yen Hsi-shan.
As a measure to strengthen his political stand, Mr. Wang
convened the so-called "Enlargement Conference" and sought for
the reorganization of Kuomintang, hence the name of the "Re-
organization Group" attached to Mr. Wang's following. Mr.
Chen Kung-po has been going back and forth between Hanoi and
Hongkong to arrange for the recrudeneces of this organization.
Recently the headquarters of the fellowship has been moved
to Shanghai and Mr. Wu Tao-chen (吴道静) had been appointed to
take charge of the organization. This group is now working to
win old Kuomintang members to their side. Mr. Chen Chung-fu
who is now in charge of the Peoples Peace Association of China
(中国人民和平会) in Hankow under the auspices of Japanese Special
Service and with General Wu Pei-fu as its leader and Dr. Ho
Shih-tseng, a local lawyer and former associate of the late
Mr. Hu Han-min are reported to be supporting this organization.

Then there is the "Anti-Communist National Salvation
League" (反共救国同盟会) with Mr. Mei Shih-ping (梅思平), former
magistrate of Kiangning Hsien and member of the Legislative
Yuan, as the responsible executive. This organization is
recruiting anti-Communist elements from all different parties
and is co-operating with the International Anti-Communist

汪精卫在上海维持三个政治组织。

据从相当可靠来源获得的情报，汪精卫先生据称在上海设有三个秘密组织，在此宣传其和平运动。具体如下：——“中国国民党改组同志会”，该会由其亲信、前工商部长陈公博先生领导。该组织成立于蒋介石将军与冯玉祥将军及阎锡山将军交战期间。为巩固其政治立场，汪先生召开了所谓的“扩大会议”，并寻求改组国民党，因此附属于汪派系的团体得名“改组派”。陈公博先生往返于河内与香港之间，以安排该组织的复兴。近期，该同志会总部已迁至上海，并任命吴道静负责主持该组织。该团体目前正致力于争取旧国民党成员加入其阵营。据悉，目前在日本特务机关支持下、以吴佩孚将军为首领、在汉口负责“中国人民和平会”的陈中孚，以及当地律师、已故胡汉民先生的前同僚何世桢博士，均支持该组织。

此外还有“反共救国同盟会”，由前江宁县知事、立法委员梅思平先生担任主管执行人员。该组织正在从各党派招募反共分子，并与国际反共

League organized by Japanese. Negotiations are said to be
conducted with the Japanese to finance a project for Mr. Wang
Ching-wei to organize an anti-Communist army in this part of
China. Steps are being taken to approach the various guerilla
and mobile units around Shanghai to give up their stand against
Japan and to side up with Mr. Wang's anti-Communist camp.

Again there is the organization of the "New Kuomin-
tang" (新國民黨) with Mr. Chow Fu-hai as the promoter. It must
be recalled that once there was an organization under the same
name sponsored by Mr. Hu Han-ming a few years ago when the
late leader made a stand against General Chiang Kai-shek but it
soon liquidated following the death of Mr. Hu. This time
Mr. Wang's men found it expedient to revive this organization
with the hope of organizing a new Kuomintang in place of the
old. Since his arrival in Shanghai in March, Mr. Chow has
been staying at the house of Dr. Chu Ming-yi,. The main object
of this body is to build up a favourable atmosphere for Mr.
Wang's peace campaign by means of the press. Owing to the fact
that Mr. Chow was until recently vice Minister of Propaganda
of Kuomintang, he possesses extensive connections with local
newspaper men and educationalists. He is now working on the
publication of two daily papers to be known as the "Ming Lih
Jih Pao (民立日報) and the Far Eastern Daily News (遠東日報) and
a weekly magazine called the "Ming Lih Weekly" (民立週報) which
has appeared already. Then he is organizing a news agency
called the "Kuo Ming Press" (國民通訊社). Negotiations for the
purchase of several local papers including the Hwa Mei Press,
which publishes the Hwa Mei Chen Pao, the Hwa Mei Wan Pao and
the Hwa Mei Weekly is said to be in progress. Several mosquito
papers are also said to be negotiating to transfer their control
to Mr. Wang's interests.

由日本人组织的联盟。据称，正与日方进行谈判，以资助汪精卫先生在中国这一地区组建一支反共军队的计划。目前正在采取措施，接触上海周边的各游击队和流动部队，劝其放弃抗日立场，转而支持汪先生的反共阵营。

此外，还有周佛海先生作为发起人的“新国民党”（新國民黨）组织。须回顾的是，数年前胡汉民先生曾赞助过一个同名组织，当时这位已故领袖采取了对抗蒋介石将军的立场，但该组织在胡先生去世后不久即告清算解散。此次，汪先生的人马认为恢复该组织较为适宜，希望以此组建一个新的国民党来取代旧国民党。自三月抵达上海以来，周先生一直居住在朱明夷博士家中。该机构的主要目标是通过新闻界为汪先生的和平运动营造有利氛围。鉴于周先生直至最近仍担任国民党宣传部副部长，他与本地报界人士和教育家有着广泛的联系。他目前正致力于出版两份日报，分别名为《民立日報》和《遠東日報》，以及一份名为《民立週報》的周刊，该周刊已问世。随后，他正在组建一家名为“國民通訊社”的新闻通讯社。据称，收购包括华美报社在内的几家本地报纸的谈判正在进行中，该报社出版《华美晨报》、《华美晚报》和《华美周刊》。另有数家小型报纸据称也在谈判将其控制权移交给汪先生方面的利益集团。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
NOV 30 1939

Letters To
The Editor

Communications intended for
publication in this column must
be accompanied by the name and
address of the sender, as a guar-
antee of good faith.

REPORT DENIED
Editor.
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—I was very much surprised
to read in your to-day's paper a
most inaccurate and false account
of the proceedings of the Sixth
National Congress of the Kuomin-
tang (not Sixth Plenary Session of
the C. E. C. as alleged) given by
a certain Mr. Lo Ching-Tao at a
press conference in Chungking sev-
eral days ago.
Mr. Lo took his refuge after the
outbreak of the Sino-Japanese war
on August 13, 1937. His where-
abouts were not known to me. In
May, 1939, he called on me at the
l'Institute Technique Franco-Chinois,
asking me to secure for him a pass-
port to Kunming via French Indo-
China under the pseudonym of "Mr.
Lee." I knew that he was formerly
one of the C. E. C. members, so
I consented to do so. Since that
time, however, I have not seen him
again until at the end of August,
1939, the Sixth National Congress of
the Kuomintang was convened, in
Shanghai. On August 28 last I took
part in the Conference and on the
next day (August 29) unexpectedly
noticed that Mr. Lo Ching-tao was
sitting in the Session. My conjecture
was that probably he might be one
of the supporters of our Peace Move-
ment and so I did not pay much
serious attention to his presence. I
had had no conversations with him,
so I did not actually know why and
for what purpose he came to the
meeting. The story that he was
kidnapped or tricked by me into
attending the meeting is therefore
a malicious invention.
At the close of the Session next
day, I learnt that Mr. Lo had de-
manded from Mr. Wang Ching-wei
an important post of political signi-
ficance (this post might be what Mr.
Lo referred to as the Chairmanship
of the Commission for the Mongolian
and Tibetan Affairs).
However, he did not succeed in
getting the job. A disappointed
man, he allowed himself to be per-
suaded by the Blue Shirt Society
in Shanghai, under the protection
of that Society, went to Chungking
via Hongkong. But to his great sur-
prise, the Chungking authorities took
no interest in him and treated him
with little consideration. Disap-
pointment led him to fabricate the
story of the "Sixth Plenary Ses-
sion," hoping that in this way he
may please the Chiang regime.
In the interest of the truth, I
ask the publication of this letter
in your columns.
〔此处转录不清〕
Shanghai, Nov. 30, 1939.

（右侧手写批注：）

1939年11月30日

致编辑的信

凡拟在本栏刊登的来信，必须附有寄信人的姓名和地址，以资诚信保证。

报道失实
编辑先生：
《上海泰晤士报》
敬启者，——阅及贵报今日刊载关于数日前罗敬陶（Lo Ching-Tao）先生在重庆记者招待会上所述国民党第六次全国代表大会（并非如所称之中央执行委员会第六届全体会议）会议情况的报道，其内容极不准确且虚假，令本人深感惊讶。
罗先生于1937年8月13日中日战争爆发后避难出走。其行踪本人并不知晓。1939年5月，他到中法工学院（l'Institute Technique Franco-Chinois）拜访我，请求我以“李先生”为化名，帮他办理经法属印度支那前往昆明的护照。我知道他曾是中央执行委员会委员之一，故同意照办。然而，自那以后直至1939年8月底国民党第六次全国代表大会在上海召开之前，我再未见过他。上月28日我出席了该会议，次日（8月29日）意外发现罗敬陶先生正坐在会场中。我推测他可能是我们和平运动的支持者之一，因此并未对他的出席给予过多关注。我未曾与他交谈，故实际上并不知他为何以及出于何种目的前来参会。因此，所谓他被本人绑架或诱骗出席会议的说法，纯属恶意捏造。
次日会议结束时，我获悉罗先生曾向汪精卫先生索要一个具有重要政治意义的职位（该职位可能就是罗先生所提及的蒙藏委员会委员长一职）。
然而，他未能得到该职位。作为一个失意之人，他听信了上海蓝衣社的劝诱，在该社的保护下，经香港前往重庆。但令他大为惊讶的是，重庆当局对他毫无兴趣，待他也甚为冷淡。失望之余，他便编造了关于“第六届全体会议”的故事，希望以此取悦蒋政权。
为求真相起见，恳请贵报刊登此信。
〔此处转录不清〕
上海，1939年11月30日。

（右侧手写批注：）

SHANGHAI TIMES.

NOV 21 1939

Italy Likely To
Recognize Wang

ROME, Nov. 20.—Italy probably will be the first Occidental nation to recognize the proposed Central Government of China headed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, informed political circles indicated here to-day.
The Italian Government, it was further understood, would seek to conclude as soon as possible a new Treaty of Commerce with the Wang regime.
With Italian quarters interested in the Far East following closely political developments in China, the interview held here to-day between Mr. Eiichi Araki, new Japanese Ambassador to Italy, and Count Galeazzo Ciano, Italian Foreign Minister, aroused comment. Mr. Araki called on Count Ciano at the Chigi Palace at 10 o'clock this morning.—Domei.

Lili

1939年11月21日

意大利可能承认汪精卫政权

罗马，11月20日电——据今日此地政治界人士透露，意大利可能成为第一个承认由汪精卫先生领导的拟议中的中国中央政府的西方国家。
另据悉，意大利政府将寻求尽快与汪伪政权缔结新的商务条约。
由于在华拥有利益的意大利各界密切关注中国的政治动态，今日此处举行的日本新任驻意大利大使荒木荣一（Eiichi Araki，音译）先生与意大利外交部长加莱阿佐·齐亚诺伯爵之间的会晤引起了议论。荒木先生于今天上午10时在基吉宫拜会了齐亚诺伯爵。——同盟社

November 3, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Pac :-

WANG CHING-WEI FLIES TO TOKYO TO ASK PRINCE KONOYE
FOR ASSISTANCE

According to reliable information from
foreign quarters, certain changes have taken place
regarding the support of the Japanese authorities for
Wang Ching-wei in his attempt to form a new Central
Government. On the afternoon of November 2, Wang Ching-
wei hurriedly flew to Tokyo to ask Prince Konoye for
assistance. Although the Tokyo authorities recently
indicated that the Japanese Government would assist
Wang in forming a new Central Government, Japan is in
fact desirous of making use of his influence; she is not
willing to see a united puppet regime in occupied areas
in China, thereby worsening her relations with the U.S.A.
Two days ago, a Tokyo telegram reported
that the Asia Development Board had decided to accelerate
the formation of a puppet organization in China and
would submit this suggestion to the Cabinet meeting on
November 2 for approval, after which it would be presented
to the Japanese Emperor for signature. However, the
matter was not submitted to the Japanese Cabinet for
discussion on November 2 and this shows that certain
questions have arisen relating to the proposed formation
of a puppet organization in China.

汪精卫飞赴东京请求近卫亲王援助

据来自外籍人士方面的可靠消息，日本当局在支持汪精卫组建新中央政府一事上已发生某些变化。11月2日下午，汪精卫匆忙飞抵东京，请求近卫亲王提供援助。尽管东京当局近期表示日本政府将协助汪精卫组建新中央政府，但日本实际上意在利用其影响力；她并不愿见到中国占领区出现一个统一的傀儡政权，从而恶化其与美国的关系。两天前，一则发自东京的电讯报道称，东亚振兴院（Asia Development Board）已决定加速在中国组建傀儡组织，并将于11月2日将该建议提交内阁会议批准，随后呈请日本天皇签署。然而，该事项并未于11月2日提交日本内阁讨论，这表明在拟议的中国傀儡组织组建问题上出现了某些疑问。

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 28 1939

Wang Vacates Residence Off
Yu Yuen Road For Frenchtown

Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Japanese choice to head the widely publicised "Central Government" at Nanking, shifted his residence yesterday afternoon. He moved from his fortified house in Nipponese occupied territory off Yu Yuen Road to his old residence at 635 Rue Frelupt.

Moving day for Mr. Wang proved quite an event. The ousted Kuo-mintang executive had a heavy guard of French Police around his Frenchtown house when he arrived. And following his own personal car came some 30 other machines filled with his intimate followers, body-guards and Japanese army officers.

According to all reports, Mr. Wang gave a house-warming party between 6 and 9 p.m. Most of the guests were Japanese officers and various puppet officials in this area. As a precautionary measure, the French Police dispatched about 300 men to the scene together with four armored cars.

The police were active throughout the evening and searched pedestrians and private motorists who chanced to used the streets in front of the Wang residence. The idea back of all this precaution was to prevent any possible attack on Mr. Wang's life and the lives of his followers.

No reason for Mr. Wang's sudden move from his impressive and well-fortified quarters off Yu Yuen Road to his French Concession establishment could be learned last night. Whether or not the move is of a permanent nature also was not known in local journalistic circles at press time.

1939年10月28日

汪精卫迁出愚园路寓所，前往法租界

被日本人选中担任南京广为人知的“中央政府”首脑的汪精卫先生，于昨日下午迁移住所。他从位于日军占领区、愚园路附近的一处设防宅邸，搬至其位于辣斐德路（Rue Frelupt）635号的旧居。

汪先生的搬迁之日颇引人注目。这位被罢黜的国民党执行委员抵达法租界寓所时，周围有大批法国警察护卫。紧随其私人汽车之后的是约30辆其他车辆，车内载有其亲信随从、保镖以及日本军官。

据各方报道，汪先生于晚间6时至9时举行了乔迁宴会。宾客多为日本军官及该地区的各类伪政权官员。作为预防措施，法国警察派遣了约300名警员及四辆装甲车赶赴现场。

警方在整个晚间保持活跃，对偶然经过汪宅门前街道的行人和私家车主进行了搜查。采取这些预防措施的目的在于防止任何可能针对汪先生及其追随者生命的袭击。

截至昨晚，尚无法得知汪先生突然从愚园路附近那处宏伟且戒备森严的寓所迁往法租界住所的原因。在截稿之时，本地新闻界也不清楚此次搬迁是否具有永久性。

October 31, 1939. Morning Translation

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper):-

RUMOURED DEATH OF WANG CHING-WEI

On the morning of October 30 the "Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury" and other foreign papers in Shanghai received through the post some printed matter purporting to have emanated from the Kung Wo Hospital (公和醫院), No.479 North Szechuen Road. It is an attempt to undermine the new regime.

According to this document, Wang Ching-wei was admitted into the Kung Wo Hospital on August 26 suffering from poisoning. On September 14 his condition became serious; he died in the hospital on September 23. The document also gives the daily recording of Wang Ching-wei's temperature and pulsation since his admission into the hospital.

When approached by our reporter about this report, Dr. Chu Min-nyi, a close follower of Wang Ching-wei, branded it as a deliberate fabrication by unscrupulous elements and stated that Wang Ching-wei was in good health, attending to his business everyday and that he had telephone only a minute ago.

（批：no confirmation Jan 1/11）

October 20, 1939. Morning Translation.

Ta Ying Yeh Pao dated October 29:

WHY WANG CHING-WEI REMOVED INTO THE FRENCH CONCESSION

Wang Ching-wei has removed from his fortress-like residence on Yu Yuen Road to House No.635 Route Frelupt in the French Concession. This has attracted much attention among the local public. There must be some reason behind Wang Ching-wei's action in removing his residence from the bosom of the Japanese military authorities into the French Concession and it is not at all unreasonable to surmise that Wang has probably been discarded by the Japanese, like a fan in autumn.

According to information from foreign sources, Wang Ching-wei, wearing a grey foreign suit of clothing, called at the Lukawei Station of the French Police in his private car at 4 p.m. October 27 and had an interview with the Chief of the French Police. This visit was made without previous notification and came as a great surprise to the French Police. Consequently, precautions were immediately adopted.

In the course of the interview, Wang informed the French Police Chief that he was removing into the French Concession and requested police protection. He added that he was no longer interested in political affairs and that hereafter he would refuse to receive callers and abstain from taking part in any other activities. He was subsequently escorted to his private residence in the French Concession under the protection of the police.

On the same evening, Wang Ching-wei gave a dinner party at his residence on Route Frelupt. The guests were mostly persons interested in the maintenance of peace and order in the Foreign Settlements. The function had absolutely no political significance; its sole object was to make friends thereby assuring his own safety.

It is learned that when Wang Ching-wei was at Tsingtao discussing the formation of a puppet government with the officials of the Provisional Government and the "Reformed Government," he was much disappointed and became very much excited because of the opposition from these two regimes. It is said that he made an attempt to end his life by taking a certain poisonous drug. This was discovered by his two doctors, one a British and the other a Japanese, and efforts were made immediately to save him from the effects of the poison. Wang Ching-wei is very pessimistic nowadays.

《大英夜报》10月29日讯：

汪精卫为何迁入法租界

汪精卫已从其位于愚园路的堡垒式寓所迁至法租界弗雷吕普路（Route Frelupt）635号。此举引起了当地公众的广泛关注。汪精卫将其住所从日本军方的庇护之下迁往法租界，背后必有原因；推测汪氏可能已像秋扇见捐一般被日本人抛弃，这并非毫无道理。

据外籍人士消息来源称，10月27日下午4时，汪精卫身穿灰色西式服装，乘坐私人汽车前往法国巡捕局卢家湾站，并与法国巡捕房总监进行了会晤。此次拜访未事先通知，令法国巡捕房大为惊讶。因此，当局立即采取了预防措施。

在会晤过程中，汪精卫告知法国巡捕房总监，他正迁入法租界，并请求警方保护。他补充说，他不再对政治事务感兴趣，此后将拒绝会见访客，并不再参与任何其他活动。随后，他在警方的护卫下被护送至其在法租界的私人寓所。

当晚，汪精卫在其弗雷吕普路的寓所举行晚宴。宾客多为关心公共租界治安维持的人士。该活动绝对没有任何政治意义；其唯一目的是借此结交朋友，从而确保自身安全。

据悉，汪精卫在青岛与“临时政府”及“维新政府”的官员讨论组建傀儡政府事宜时，因遭到这两个政权的反对而深感失望，情绪极为激动。据说他曾试图服用某种毒药自杀。这一举动被他的两名医生——一名英国人和一名日本人——发现，并立即采取措施进行解毒救治。如今的汪精卫非常悲观。
