SHANGHAI TIMES.
OCT 29 1938

Mr. Wang Ching-wei: Is He
“Traitor” Or Patriot?

How Advocate Of Peace With Japan Has Had The
Courage To Make Public Stand For Principle

The following article, which is of timely interest, is published by
permission of the Editor of "The Peoples Tribune" in advance of its
publication in the October issue of the journal which is to make its
appearance in a few days.

Not for the first time in its long
and stormy history, a serious split
has occurred within the ranks of
the Kuomintang, but never
before has the issue at stake been
of such vital and urgent importance
to every citizen of the Chinese
Republic. Frequently during the
past there has been conflict of
political and sometimes purely
personal views which, to the great
mass of the people, did not appear
to be of any general interest or
importance. Such clashes came to
be regarded as quarrels within
the Party such as happen all over
the world at times—actually con-
cerning only the principals and
their immediate or distant follow-
ers, and frequently arising out of
old personal grievances which
should have been long forgotten or
from disgruntlement among disap-
pointed office-seekers. The Kuomin-
tang like all other political parties
in the world, has earnest members
willing to make any personal
sacrifice which is calculated to
advance the interests of the Party
and the principles for which it
stands. It also has members much
more concerned about satisfying
personal ambitions than the
execution of political principles
which they profess both to hold
and uphold. In other words, the
splits and crises which have
occurred hitherto within the ranks
of the Kuomintang—ever since
the establishment of the Republic
—have been conflicts of opinion
and interest such as are inevitable
in any political organization which
aims at carrying-out a national
policy likely to affect adversely
the interests of influential groups,
and especially in a democratic
Party which, from the beginning,
included many accustomed to
military methods of administration
in territory which they had come
to regard as their own personal
domain rather than part of a great
Republic.

Reason For Split

The most recent split in the
Kuomintang, however, is much
more serious than any of the
ruptures preceding it, for it has
resulted from a difference on an
issue of immense gravity—an
issue which directly affects every
citizen of the Republic, at home
and abroad, and indirectly has an
important bearing upon inter-
national relations in general. The
issue is quite a simple one—
whether or not it is possible to
bring Sino-Japanese hostilities to
an end on terms which China can
accept with honour. For having
expressed the opinion that such a
settlement is possible, Mr. Wang
Ching-wei has been expelled from
all his posts, been expelled from
the Party, formally and publicly
denounced as a traitor, with a
warrant issued for his arrest.
Now, treason is regarded in every
country as a grave offence—as it
undoubtedly is—and those proved
guilty of it can hope for little
mercy. They are regarded as
having committed a crime against
their own people—of doing or
attempting something which is
against the interests of the State,
and for so heinous an offence the
usual penalty is death, while the
traitor's memory is held in execra-
tion by those who were endangered
by his illicit relations and activi-
ties with enemies of the State.
The Chungking Government, head-
ed by General Chiang Kai-shek,
has declared that Mr. Wang Ching-
wei is an enemy of his own
people, has branded him as a
traitor, and denounced him and
his associates as objects of national
contempt and public obloquy.

This is not the first occasion on
which prominent leaders of the
Kuomintang have not been able
to see eye to eye with Mr. Wang
on matters of national policy.
There have been several such
disagreements within the Party,
some of which led to his temporary
retirement from politics, but
always those who had forced him
out were glad to welcome him
back when some new difficulty
arose the solution of which, they
realized, would be more readily
attained if the Government had
the advantage of his counsel and
support. Never before, however,
has Mr. Wang Ching-wei been
openly denounced as a traitor, and
to those who know the man and
his political record of close on
40 years it is outrageous that
such an accusation should be
made against him—for what? The
charge is that he is guilty of "sub-
versive activities." It is a grave
charge, and if true Mr. Wang has
forfeited all claim to respect from
his fellow-countrymen—but is it
true?

《字林西报》。
1938年10月29日

汪精卫先生：是“汉奸”还是爱国者？

主张与日本和平的人士如何有勇气为原则公开表态

以下文章具有时效性意义，经《人民论坛》编辑许可，在该刊即将于数日后出版的十月号提前刊登。

在国民党漫长而动荡的历史中，党内发生严重分裂已非首次，但此次所涉议题对中华民国每一位公民而言，其重要性与紧迫性前所未有。过去经常发生政治观点乃至纯粹个人见解的冲突，这些冲突在广大民众看来，似乎并不具备普遍的利益关联或重要性。此类冲突逐渐被视为党内的争吵，这类争吵在世界各地的政党中时有发生——实际上仅关乎当事人及其直接或追随者，且往往源于本应早已遗忘的旧日个人恩怨，或是失意的求官者心中的不满。国民党如同世界上所有其他政党一样，拥有诚挚的党员，他们愿意为推进党的利益及其所秉持的原则做出任何个人牺牲。但它也有一些成员，比起践行他们所宣称持有并拥护的政治原则，更关心满足个人野心。换言之，自民国建立以来，国民党内部迄今发生的分裂与危机，均为意见与利益之争，这在任何旨在执行可能 adversely 影响权势集团利益的国家政策的政治组织中都是不可避免的，尤其在一个从创立之初就吸纳了许多习惯于在其视为个人领地而非伟大共和国一部分的领土上实行军事化行政管理的成员的民主政党中，更是如此。

分裂的原因

然而，国民党最近的这次分裂比以往任何一次破裂都更为严重，因为它源于一项极其重大议题上的分歧——这一议题直接关系到海内外每一位共和国公民，并间接对整体国际关系产生重要影响。该议题十分简单——即是否有可能以中国能够体面接受的条件结束中日敌对状态。因表示认为这种和解是可能的，汪精卫先生被免去所有职务，被开除出党，被正式公开谴责为汉奸，并发布了逮捕令。如今，叛国罪在任何国家都被视为重罪——事实也确实如此——那些被证实有罪的人几乎无法指望得到宽恕。他们被视为犯下了危害本国人民的罪行——做了或试图做损害国家利益之事，对于如此令人发指的罪行，通常的惩罚是死刑，而叛徒的记忆则因其与国家敌人的非法往来和活动而危及他人，从而遭到那些人的唾弃。以蒋介石将军为首的重庆政府已宣布汪精卫先生是其本国人民的敌人，给他贴上汉奸的标签，并谴责他和他的同伙为全国所鄙视和公众所辱骂的对象。

这并非国民党主要领导人在国家政策问题上无法与汪先生达成一致的首次情况。党内曾发生过数次此类分歧，其中一些导致他暂时退出政坛，但每当出现新的困难时，那些曾将他排挤出去的人总是乐于欢迎他回归，因为他们意识到，如果政府能得到他的建议和支持，问题的解决将更容易达成。然而，汪精卫先生此前从未被公开谴责为汉奸，对于那些了解此人及其近四十年政治履历的人来说，对他提出这样的指控是荒谬的——究竟为了什么？指控是他犯有“颠覆活动”之罪。这是一项严重的指控，如果属实，汪先生便丧失了同胞对他的所有尊重——但这是否属实？

Peace With Honour
Let it be at once admitted that
Mr. Wang Ching-wei has ad-
vocated making peace with Japan
—but not an abject and uncondi-
tional surrender, not a peace
humbly begged for by a China
“beaten to her knees,” but a peace
such as can be accepted only and
uprightly, with honour and dignity
—a peace on better terms than
General Chiang Kai-shek and the
Supreme National Defence Council
were prepared to discuss as far
back as December 2, 1937, before
the fall of Nanking! In the
previous November the German
Ambassador to China, Dr. Traut-
mann, had called on Dr. H. H.
Kung, President of the Executive
Yuan, and on Dr. Wang Chung-
hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs,
and informed them of the result
of certain conversations between
the Japanese Minister for Foreign
Affairs and the German Am-
bassador in Tokyo. Subsequently
Dr. Trautmann explained the
situation to General Chiang Kai-
shek, who expressed willingness
to accept the points submitted by
Japan as a basis for negotiating
peace, on condition that Germany
acted as mediator and that Chi-
nese sovereignty in North China be
guaranteed. General Chiang dis-
cussed Japan’s proposals with the
military commanders then in Nan-
king, who all agreed that the
points submitted to China through
the German Ambassador were
acceptable as forming a basis for
peace-talks with Japan. Were
these men all “traitors”? If so,
why have they not been denounc-
ed as such; if not, why should Mr.
Wang Ching-wei be branded as a
traitor simply because he, too,
favours discussion with Japan of
the Konoye terms of December
22, 1938, which, in actual fact, are
much more favourable to China
than those presented through
the German Ambassador 21
months ago, and which General
Chiang and the highest military
leaders in the land were then
willing to consider?
What frightful slaughter, suffer-
ing, and sacrifice China would have
been spared if the effort at media-
tion towards the end of 1937 had
proved successful? Nanking was
then still held by Chinese troops,
with Hankow, Canton, and scores
of less vital points still being
gallantly defended, but for various
reasons this precious opportunity of
coming to terms with Japan was
lost, and what China has also lost
in men and money since the fall
of Nanking—what her unhappy
and helpless people have suffered
during the subsequent year and
three-quarters of continued but
unsteady retreat—these appalling
facts are only too familiar. About
12 months after the unsuccess-
ful effort at mediation by Germany
various statements were made by
Prince Konoye, on behalf of the
Japanese Government, which Mr.
Wang Ching-wei regarded as offer-
ing another opportunity for China
to discuss reasonable terms of
peace. His colleagues in the Gov-
ernment—especially General Chiang
Kai-shek—did not share his views,
whereupon Mr. Wang left Chung-
king on December 18, 1938, and

光荣的和平

必须首先承认，汪精卫先生曾主张与日本议和——但这并非卑躬屈膝、无条件的投降，也不是一个“被击垮至跪地”的中国所卑微乞求的和平，而是一种只能以正直、荣誉和尊严接受的和平——其条件甚至优于蒋介石将军及最高国防会议早在1937年12月2日南京陷落之前就准备商讨的条件！在此前一个月，德国驻华大使陶德曼博士（Dr. Trautmann）曾拜会行政院院长孔祥熙博士和外交部长王宠惠博士，向他们通报了日本外务大臣与德国驻东京大使之间某些会谈的结果。随后，陶德曼博士向蒋介石将军说明了局势，蒋表示愿意接受日本提出的要点作为谈判和平的基础，条件是德国担任调停人，并保证中国在华北的主权。蒋介石将军与当时在南京的军事指挥官讨论了日本的提议，这些指挥官均同意，通过德国大使向中国提交的要点可以作为与日本进行和平谈判的基础。难道这些人都是“汉奸”吗？如果是，为何他们未被如此谴责；如果不是，为何仅仅因为汪精卫先生也赞成就1938年12月22日的近卫声明条款与日本进行讨论，就被贴上汉奸的标签？事实上，这些条款比21个月前通过德国大使提出的条款对中国更为有利，而蒋介石将军和全国最高军事领导人当时也曾愿意予以考虑。

如果1937年底的调停努力取得成功，中国本可避免多么可怕的屠杀、苦难和牺牲？当时南京仍由中国军队驻守，汉口、广州以及数十个次要据点仍在英勇防守，但由于各种原因，这一与日本达成协议的宝贵机会丧失了。自南京陷落以来，中国在人力和财力上的损失，以及其不幸而无助的人民在随后一年零三个月持续但不稳定的撤退中所遭受的苦难——这些可怕的事实已为人所熟知。在德国调停失败约12个月后，近卫亲王代表日本政府发表了各项声明，汪精卫先生认为这为中国提供了讨论合理和平条件的另一次机会。他在政府中的同僚——尤其是蒋介石将军——并不认同他的观点，于是汪精卫于1938年12月18日离开重庆，

soon afterward (December 29,
1938), published a statement open-
ly advocating the views he had
already expressed when discussing
the situation in Government con-
ferences. Briefly, Mr. Wang con-
tended that Prince Konoye's latest
statement, of December 22, 1938,
of Japan's policy provided a basis
upon which negotiations for peace
might be honourably opened. That
was all—there was no suggestion
that humbled China should cringe
upon her knees for mercy, but
simply that a nation which had
shown the world how gallantly it
could defend itself under condi-
tions of extraordinary difficulty
could and should express willing-
ness to open negotiations for peace
in response to what appeared to
be an offer from Japan which
could be honourably considered as
affording a basis for discussion.

Frank Line of Action

A traitor would not have taken
the line of action which was
followed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei
—a course which was marked all
along which absolute frankness.
First, the then Chairman of the
Central Political Council and De-
puty General Executive of the
Kuomintang went on December
3, 1938, to the Chairman of the
Supreme National Defence Coun-
cil, General Chiang Kai-shek, and
urged that Prince Konoye's de-
claration of November 3, 1938
modifying the Declaration of Jan-
uary 16, 1938 be accepted by the
Government as affording an
opportunity to open peace negotia-
tions without loss of prestige on
the part of China. There was
only an angry refusal on General
Chiang's part to discuss the
matter, whereupon Mr. Wang left
Chungking on December 18 and
proceeded to address, on December
29, a telegraphic appeal to General
Chiang and members of the C.E.C.
and Central Supervisory Com-
mittee, in which he repeated the
arguments already submitted ver-
bally to General Chiang Kai-
shek. The day before, on Decem-
ber 28, he addressed a similar
written appeal to his colleagues on
the Standing Committee of the
C.E.C. and the Supreme National
Defence Council (of which he was
Vice-Chairman), begging them not
to allow another chance to pass of
bringing hostilities to an honour-
able conclusion. These frank and
undisguised expressions of opinion
while Mr. Wang still held high
office in the Government and
Party cannot possibly be regarded
as the acts of a traitor, and what
he has done since his expulsion
from office and membership of the
Kuomintang has been merely to
continue the efforts he had been
persistently and openly making, as
Deputy General Executive of the
Party and a member of the Na-
tional Government, to bring peace
to his unhappy country and an
honourable end to the frightful
sufferings of his fellow-country-
men, sacrifices which seemed to
him to be no longer necessary, and
unlikely to leave China in any
better position to make terms
than she then was, no matter how
long the struggle were continued,
that is to secure a peace without
war indemnity, without territorial
cessions, a peace which recognizes
neither victor nor vanquished, a
peace which will turn two un-
natural enemies into natural
friends again.

Must it be considered, no matter
what the attendant circumstances,
a traitorous act to speak about the
possibility of peace—to strive for
bringing about a cessation of
hostilities, when millions of men
and women are suffering the most
agonizing tortures conceivable as
a direct consequence of war?

不久之后（1938年12月29日），他发表了一份声明，公开倡导他在政府会议讨论局势时已经表达过的观点。简而言之，汪先生认为，日本于1938年12月22日发布的近卫亲王最新政策声明，为体面地开启和平谈判提供了基础。仅此而已——其中并无暗示屈辱的中国应当跪地乞怜，而仅仅是说，一个在异常艰难的条件下向世界展示了其英勇自卫能力的国家，能够且应当表示愿意开启和平谈判，以回应日本看似提供的一项可被体面地视为讨论基础的提议。

坦率的行动方针

叛徒不会采取汪精卫先生所遵循的行动路线——这一路线自始至终以绝对坦率为特征。首先，时任中央政治委员会主席兼国民党副总裁的他，于1938年12月3日晋见最高国防会议主席蒋介石将军，力促政府接受近卫亲王1938年11月3日关于修改1938年1月16日声明的宣言，视其为在不损中国威望的情况下开启和平谈判的机会。蒋介石将军愤怒地拒绝讨论此事，汪先生遂于12月18日离开重庆，并于12月29日向蒋介石将军及国民党中央执行委员会和中央监察委员会成员发出通电呼吁，重申此前已向蒋介石将军口头陈述的论点。前一日，即12月28日，他向国民党中央执行委员会常务委员会及最高国防会议（他任副主席）的同僚发出类似的书面呼吁，恳请他们不要让另一个使敌对行动得以体面结束的机会溜走。汪先生在仍担任政府和党的高职期间，这些坦率且毫不掩饰的意见表达，绝不可能被视为叛徒行径；而他自被开除公职及国民党党籍以来所做的一切，不过是继续他作为党的副总裁和国民政府成员时一直公开坚持的努力，即为这个不幸的国家带来和平，为其同胞可怕的苦难带来体面的终结；在他看来，这些牺牲已不再必要，而且无论斗争持续多久，都不太可能使中国在比当时更有利的地位下去达成条款，也就是说，去争取一种没有战争赔款、没有领土割让的和平，一种不承认胜者也不承认败者的和平，一种将两个非自然的敌人重新变为自然朋友的和平。

难道无论伴随何种情况，谈论和平的可能性——在数百万男女正遭受战争直接后果带来的难以想象的极度痛苦折磨之时，努力促使敌对行动停止——都必须被视为叛国行为吗？

pages.en:
An advocate of "peace at any
price" possibly may be condemned
as a coward, though in fact it may
call for no little courage, moral
and physical, to stand up and
speak out on behalf of those un-
able or unwilling to voice their
own views. But what of the man
who believes that peace is to be
had on terms which are not dis-
honourable and not ungenerous,
which recognise neither victor nor
vanquished—is he a traitor to the
hundreds of millions who are
helpless victims of war if he seeks
to bring an end to their long-
drawn agony, to find an honour-
able way of escape from the
frightful misery and suffering they
have so patiently endured for over
two years, to bring about by
negotiation agreement upon cer-
tain essential points which
can never be reached by forceful
methods? Or is the real traitor
he who allows a useless struggle
to continue, who refused to realize
plain even if but unpleasant facts,
and pretends to have a confidence
which he knows has no stable
foundation—and is willing that the
slaughter and suffering should con-
tinue in the vain hope that some-
thing will happen some day in
some way which will make the
bloody sacrifice worth while?

Is He a Traitor?

Mr. Wang Ching-wei has acted
on the principle enunciated a
century and a half ago by that
great democrat Benjamin Franklin
—that there never was a good war
or a bad peace. For more than
two years the Chinese people have
suffered tortures and endured
agonies unprecedented in the
history of the world. From Pe-
king to Canton citizens of the
Republic have been subjected
since the summer of 1937 to every
conceivable torment of mind and
body. From fighting-men in the
front line to infants in arms—from
women working in the fields to
fishermen in deep-sea junks—from
young folk at college, with life
just beginning to reveal its absorb-
ing interests, to old people hap-
pily looking forward to peaceful
days among their families—to all
these, rich and poor alike, war has
brought sorrow and suffering. The
appalling record of slaughter and
destruction is so ghastly that they
must be considered the more
fortunate who have not survived
to see and share the frightful
misery spread so far around them
—and still spreading. Is he to be
regarded as a traitor who sees a
way out of so appalling a situation
—a way which can be followed
without China surrendering a
single one of the points which
really matter in regard to her
continued existence as a sovereign
State? Is he to be branded
as a traitor who advocates
a course of action which will
enable the Republic of China to
resume the work of national recon-
struction started by Dr. Sun Yat-
sen? The people of China have
shown amazing courage and deter-
mination in warlike measures of
defence: now they have an oppor-
tunity of displaying similar courage
and determination in expressing
willingness to negotiate peace on
terms which will give them the
right of self-determination, the
right to manage their own affairs,
and the power to contribute their
share towards the attainment of
international peace and under-
standing.

一个主张“不惜任何代价求和平”的人或许会被斥为懦夫，尽管事实上，挺身而出，代表那些无力或不愿表达自身观点的人发声，可能需要不小的道德与身体上的勇气。但是，对于那些认为和平可以在既不辱没尊严也不失宽厚的条件下获得、既不分胜者也不分败者的条款下实现的人，又当如何呢？如果此人试图终结数亿战争无助受害者漫长的痛苦，为他们耐心忍受了两年多的可怕苦难与折磨寻找一条体面的出路，并通过谈判就某些靠武力手段永远无法达成的关键要点达成协议，那么他算是背叛了这数亿人吗？抑或，真正的叛徒是那个让无谓的斗争持续下去、拒绝正视即使令人不悦却显而易见的事实、假装拥有明知缺乏稳固基础的信心、并甘愿让屠杀与苦难继续下去，只抱着虚无缥缈的希望，期待某天以某种方式发生某些事情，使血腥的牺牲变得值得的人？

他是叛徒吗？

汪精卫先生所遵循的原则，是一个半世纪前伟大的民主主义者本杰明·富兰克林所阐明的——即从未有过好的战争或坏的和平。两年多来，中国人民遭受了世界历史上前所未有的折磨与痛苦。自1937年夏以来，从北京到广州，中华民国的公民们身心备受各种可以想象的摧残。从前线的战斗人员到襁褓中的婴儿——从田间劳作的妇女到深海舢板上的渔民——从人生刚刚展现出迷人趣味的大学生，到安享天伦之乐、期盼平静晚年的老人——无论贫富，战争给所有这些人都带来了悲伤与苦难。屠杀与破坏的记录如此骇人听闻，以至于那些未能幸存下来目睹并分担周围广泛蔓延且仍在扩散的可怕苦难的人，反而应被视为更为幸运。难道一个看到了摆脱如此可怕局势出路的人——一条无需中国在其作为主权国家存续方面真正关键的任何一个点上做出让步的道路——就应该被视为叛徒吗？难道一个倡导采取能使中华民国恢复孙中山博士开启的国家重建工作的行动方针的人，就应该被贴上叛徒的标签吗？中国人民在军事防御措施中表现出了惊人的勇气与决心；现在，他们有机会表现出同样的勇气与决心，表示愿意在赋予他们自决权、管理自身事务的权利以及为达成国际和平与理解贡献自身力量的条款下进行和平谈判。

Chinese-American Daily News (Chungking telegram) :- 13.10.39 (PM)

GENERALS DENOUNCE WANG CHING-WEI

The following telegram jointly signed by
Generals Yu Hsueh-chung (于學忠), Sung Heng-lien (沈鴻烈),
Han Tuh-chuin (韓德勤) and many others, denouncing
Wang Ching-wei, has been sent to the National Government:-

"According to intelligence reports from
various sources, Wang Ching-wei is at present hiding in
Shanghai and is planning to form a puppet Kuomintang and
a puppet government under the protection of the Japanese.
We are highly indignant upon learning of this news.
"Wang's activities of betrayal against the
nation and the Kuomintang are known to all, and yet the
Government is very lenient towards him, simply dismissing
him from Kuomintang membership and relieving him of all
his official posts. If Wang still has some nationalistic
understanding, he should quickly take this opportunity
to repent his misdeeds before it is too late. Nevertheless,
he remains unconscious of his traitorous activities and
advocates peace. Recently he became more outrageous in
his activities and has done things that call for nation-
wide condemnation; he has become a public enemy of the
nation. If such outrageously traitorous activities are
left to be carried out without public denunciation, how
can the Kuomintang discipline be upheld, national
legislation be maintained and the indignation of the
450,000,000 people of the country be appeased? We,
therefore, earnestly hope that he be brought to capital
punishment so that righteousness can be upheld and
wickedness can be curbed and discouraged."

《中美日报》（重庆电）：- 1939年10月13日（下午）

将领们谴责汪精卫

以下由于学忠、沈鸿烈、韩德勤等多位将军联合签署的谴责汪精卫的电报，已发送至国民政府：-

“据多方情报报告，汪精卫目前藏匿于上海，正计划在日方庇护下组建伪国民党及伪政府。获悉此消息，我们深感愤慨。
“汪氏背叛国家与国民党之行径众所周知，然而政府对其甚为宽仁，仅将其开除出国民党并免除其一切官职。若汪氏尚存些许民族大义之认知，应趁此机会尽快悔过自新，以免为时已晚。尽管如此，他仍对其叛国行径毫无觉悟，反而鼓吹‘和平’。近期其行径愈发猖獗，做出种种招致全国谴责之事；他已成为全民公敌。若任由如此猖獗的叛国行径实施而不加以公开谴责，何以维护国民党之纪律、保持国家之法度、平息全国四亿五千万民众之愤慨？因此，我们恳切希望将其处以极刑，以伸张正义，遏制并震慑奸恶。”

Ta Mei Pao (United Press telegram from Peiping) 8- 13.10.39 (PM)
NEW PEOPLE'S ASSOCIATION TO RIVAL WANG CHING-WEI

Wang Keh-min (王克敏), Chairman of the
Peiping Provisional Government, has been appointed
President of the New People's Association (新民會), the
only legitimate political party in North China. It is
generally believed that this appointment was made as a
means of checking the expansion into North China of the
influence of Wang Ching-wei's Kuomintang. The political
bodies in North China are said to be opposed to the
establishment of a new Central Government under the auspices
of Wang Ching-wei and it is said that the new arrangements
made by the New People's Association will very likely
increase the disputes between the parties concerned.
According to the "Sin Min Pao" (新民報), an
official organ of the Japanese authorities, close
co-operation is now in existence between the New People's
Association and the Peiping Provisional Government and
Wang Keh-min has been appointed chief of both of these
two organs. He will endeavour to consolidate the authority
of this political body which will work to form the people
into a strong army for the defence of New China.
According to the Japanese official organ, the New People's
Association is at present an important political
organization and will become a strong rival of the New
Kuomintang formed by Wang Ching-wei.

大美报（北平合众社电稿）1939年10月8-13日（下午）
新民会与汪精卫抗衡

北平临时政府主席王克敏已被任命为新民会总裁，该会是华北地区唯一的合法政党。普遍认为，此项任命旨在遏制汪精卫国民党势力向华北扩张。据悉，华北各政治团体反对在汪精卫主持下建立新的中央政府，且据称新民会所作的新安排很可能会加剧有关各方之间的争端。据日本当局官方机关报《新民报》报道，新民会与北平临时政府目前存在密切合作，王克敏被任命为这两个机构的首脑。他将致力于巩固该政治团体的权威，该团体将致力于把民众组建成一支保卫新中国的强大军队。据日本官方机关报称，新民会目前是一个重要的政治组织，并将成为汪精卫组建的新国民党的有力竞争对手。

Ta Mei Pao and Hwa Pao :- 4.10.39 (AM)

WANG CHING-WEI ENTERTAINS HIGH JAPANESE OFFICIALS

A large number of City Government policemen was on post duty along Yu Yuen Road from Tifong Road to Jessfield Park at 11.30 a.m. yesterday and pedestrian traffic in the district was greatly restricted. Such a phenomenon had never occurred before.
Subsequently, it was ascertained that Lieutenant General H. Yanagawa, Chairman of the Asiatic Rehabilitation Bureau, accompanied by a large number of bodyguards and other officials, were arriving to attend a luncheon party given by Wang Ching-wei at No. 31, Lane 1136, Yu Yuen Road.
Strict precautions were maintained by both the Settlement Police and the City Government authorities along the route through which the 14 motor cars used by the group passed.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-

At noon yesterday, Lieutenant-General Yamada, Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Forces in Central China, accompanied by Lieutenant-General Yoshimoto and a number of military officers, travelled through the Settlement, under the protection of both British and French military and police forces, from Garden Bridge to Wang Ching-wei's residence on Yu Yuen Road via Nanking Road and Bubbling Well Road. There were more than ten motor cars.

Upon arrival at Wang's residence at 12.30 p.m., the party was given a hearty welcome by the Youths' Dare-to-Die Corps of the Reformed Kuomintang.
In the course of an interview with Lieutenant-General Yamada, Wang Ching-wei expressed his heartfelt appreciation for the warm support given his work to accelerate the establishment of a new Central Government and for the establishing of peace in East Asia.
The function lasted until 3 p.m. at which hour the party terminated.

Ta Mei Pao :-

Tokyo, October 3.

According to the Shanghai correspondent of the "Tokyo Nichi Nichi," Wang Ching-wei has instructed Ting Muh-tsun (丁默村) and Tao Hsi-sung (陶希聖) to undertake precautionary measures day and night together with bodyguards. This is a precautionary measure against any attempt that may be made on his life.---United Press.

《大美报》及《华报》：1939年10月4日（上午）

汪精卫宴请日本高官

昨日上午11时30分，大量市政府警察在从提篮桥路（Tifong Road）至兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）的愚园路沿线执勤，该地区的行人交通受到极大限制。此类现象此前从未发生过。
随后获悉，亚洲复兴局主席柳川平助中将（Lieutenant General H. Yanagawa）在大批保镖及其他官员的陪同下，抵达愚园路1136弄31号，参加汪精卫举办的午宴。
在该团体所乘坐的14辆汽车途经的路线上，租界巡捕房与市政府当局均采取了严密的防范措施。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：

昨日中午，日军华中方面军司令官山田乙三中将（Lieutenant-General Yamada）在吉本贞一中将（Lieutenant-General Yoshimoto）及多名军官的陪同下，在英国和法国军队及警力的保护下，经由南京路和静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road），穿过租界，从外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）前往汪精卫位于愚园路的寓所。车队共有十余辆汽车。

下午12时30分抵达汪宅时，该代表团受到了改组国民党青年敢死队的热烈欢迎。
在与山田中将的会谈中，汪精卫对加速建立新的中央政府以及实现东亚和平的工作所获得的热烈支持表示衷心感谢。
活动持续至下午3时结束。

《大美报》：

东京，10月3日。

据《东京日日新闻》驻上海记者报道，汪精卫已指示丁默村和陶希圣与保镖一起日夜采取预防措施。这是针对任何可能对其生命进行的企图而采取的预防性措施。——合众社。

September 21, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

China Evening News, Sin Wan Pao and Hwa Pao (Chungking
telegram) :-

REPORTED ARRIVAL OF KONOYE AT HONGKONG TO OPEN NEGOTIATIONS
ENTIRELY UNFOUNDED

A spokesman of the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs at Chungking has issued the following statement:-
"The report to the effect that with the arrival in
Hongkong of Prince Konoye, the former Japanese Premier,
General Chang Chun, Vice-President of the Executive Yuan,
acting on behalf of the National Government, had discussed
peace between China and Japan with Konoye is entirely
unfounded.
"The Japanese authorities have on many
occasions fabricated false reports in Hongkong with the
object of disturbing the minds of the people. For
instance, two days ago, a report was current that T.V.
Soong, Governor of the Bank of China, had left for Moscow,
and on the following day, it was reported that General
Chang Chun was discussing peace with Prince Konoye.
"In addition to solemnly refuting such
reports, the National Government has warned a certain
foreign news agency against spreading propaganda on behalf
of the Japanese. There can be no peace talks so long as
the Japanese soldiers are not withdrawn from China. People
should not allow themselves to be misled by poisonous
rumours."

（左侧边注：FILE / WA）

1939年9月21日。下午译件。

《中国晚报》、《新闻报》及《华报》（重庆电）：-

关于近卫抵港开启谈判之报道纯属子虚乌有

重庆外交部发言人发表如下声明：-
“有关前日本首相近卫公爵抵达香港，国民政府行政院副院长张群将军代表中国政府与其商讨中日和平一事之报道，纯属子虚乌有。
“日本当局曾多次在香港捏造虚假报道，旨在扰乱民心。例如，两日前曾有传言称中国银行行长宋子文已启程前往莫斯科，次日又报道称张群将军正与近卫公爵商谈和平。
“国民政府除严正驳斥此类谣言外，并已警告某外国通讯社不得散布亲日宣传。只要日军不撤出中国，便不可能进行和谈。民众切勿受有毒谣言之误导。”

（左侧边注：档案 / WA）

Ta Ying Yeh Pao of September 15 :- 16.9.37 (AM)

MAYOR FU SIAO-EN SAID TO BE REPLACED BY CHU MIN-NYI :
CENTRAL GOVERNMENT TO BE ESTABLISHED IN NANKING ON
OCTOBER 10

According to information given out by the
employees of the so-called Shanghai City Government,
Wang Ching-wei is planning to establish a Central
Government in Nanking on October 10, when the five-barred
flag will be abolished and the "blue sky and white sun"
flag will be restored.

It is said that as soon as Wang assumes
authority, the "Dah Dao" influence in Shanghai will be
overthrown and Fu Siao-en, the so-called Mayor of the
Shanghai City Government, will be replaced by members
of the Wang's clique, amongst whom Chu Min-nyi (褚民誼)
has the greatest opportunity to secure the post of Mayor.

Loo Ying (盧英), Commissioner of the
Police Bureau, will probably be promoted to a post
resembling Garrison Commissioner and will undertake the
responsibility for reorganization of the Shanghai Tangpu
and the registration of Kuomintang members.

《大英夜报》9月15日报道：- 1937年9月16日（上午）

据称傅筱庵将被褚民谊取代：
中央政府将于10月10日在南京成立

据所谓上海市政府雇员透露的消息，
汪精卫正计划于10月10日在南京建立中央政府，届时将废除五色旗，恢复“青天白日”旗。

据悉，汪精卫一旦掌权，上海的“大刀”势力将被推翻，所谓上海市政府市长傅筱庵将被汪派成员取代，其中褚民谊（褚民誼）最有希望获得市长一职。

警察局局长卢英（盧英）可能会晋升为类似卫戍司令的职位，并负责重组上海塘浦地区以及国民党党员的登记工作。

September 18, 1939. Afternoon Translation

Central China Daily News publishes the following special article written by Dr. Chu Min-nyi:-

DR. CHU MIN-NYI'S ARTICLE

The Sino-Japanese war has been going on for over two years and both parties have their difficulties. The fighting will not stop yet. If the leader of a country wages a war by using the country as a stake in a gamble and has no sympathy for the sufferings of the people, every one should attack him and dismember his body.

Coastal regions have been occupied and towns in the interior have fallen. Hundreds of years of construction work has been destroyed and they are still advocating a scorched earth policy. They have no sense of shame. How can a country that has not made the least preparation fight a strong nation with a record of 60 years of progress! The outcome of such a war can be in no doubt. Russia wants to help the Communists, while Britain is assisting China because she has to protect her own interests.

After the signing of the German-Russian Non-Aggression Pact, Britain and France became involved in a war and they have no time to think of assisting China. Will Russia help China? But Russia has reached an agreement with Japan. Chungking, therefore, is no longer safe, for Russia will no longer be able to assist China. If Britain and France become allies with Japan, they also will not be able to help and will care nothing more about China's friendship. Will China then be able to carry on the war without outside assistance? Will she be able to end the war?

Peace is the only way to save the country. War has broken out in Europe. Now is the best time for China and Japan to conclude peace, for if the war can be ended at this time, the conditions will be fair. China and Japan should then co-operate and maintain peace in East Asia.

The Open Door Policy is a big success for America. Britain, taking advantage of the friction between America and Japan, has been able to maintain her interests in the Far East and on this account, Britain and America have always been cool towards each other in their attitude over the Far East. For instance, at the time of the Mukden Incident, America wanted to interfere but Britain declined; the reform of the currency system in China was brought about with British assistance but actually Britain wants to win over America economically in the Far East. Thus, on the outbreak of the Lukouchiao Incident, Britain decided to assist China but America only showed sympathy for our country while selling supplies to Japan. This shows that if Japan and America were allied, they could control all European interests in East Asia and the Sino-Japanese war would not have taken place.

《华中日报》刊登了褚民谊博士撰写的以下特约文章：-

褚民谊博士的文章

中日战争已持续两年有余，双方均面临困境。战事尚不会停止。若一国领袖以国家为赌注发动战争，对民众的苦难毫无同情之心，人人皆应起而攻之，将其碎尸万段。

沿海地区已被占领，内地城镇相继沦陷。数百年的建设成果毁于一旦，而他们仍在鼓吹焦土政策。他们毫无廉耻之心。一个毫无准备的国家，怎能与一个拥有六十年进步历程的强国作战！此类战争的结果毫无疑问。俄国欲援助共产党人，而英国援助中国则是为了维护其自身利益。

德苏互不侵犯条约签订后，英法卷入战争，无暇顾及援华。俄国会援助中国吗？但俄国已与日本达成协议。因此，重庆不再安全，因为俄国将无法再援助中国。若英法与日本结盟，它们也将无力施助，且不再重视中国的友谊。那么，中国在没有外援的情况下能否继续作战？能否结束战争？

和平是救国的唯一途径。欧洲已爆发战争。此刻正是中日缔结和平的最佳时机，因为若此时能结束战争，条件将是公平的。中日随后应合作，维持东亚和平。

门户开放政策对美国而言是一大成功。英国利用美日之间的摩擦，得以维持在远东的利益，因此英美在远东问题上的态度一直彼此冷淡。例如，在沈阳事变（九一八事变）期间，美国欲加干涉，但英国予以拒绝；中国币制改革是在英国的协助下实现的，但实际上英国意在经济上拉拢美国以对抗其在远东的影响。因此，在卢沟桥事变爆发时，英国决定援助中国，而美国仅对我国表示同情，同时却向日本出售物资。这表明，若日美结盟，它们便能控制欧洲在东亚的所有利益，中日战争也就不会发生。

September 18, 1939. Afternoon Translation

Japan now realizes that her policy
has been all wrong; therefore she wants to end the war.
This is indeed a happy way of bringing stability t:
East Asia.

The world situation is changing
every minute. When the war was first started, the
Chinese people believed that the Powers would apply
sanctions against Japan within two years, but no action
has been taken. Britain has remained silent with
Russia standing aloof.

The Customs Agreement between Britain
and Japan, the compromise between Russia and Japan over
the Changkoufeng affair, the agreement between Britain
and Japan, are they all favourable to China? How
much have Britain and Russia assisted China? When
putting signatures to loans to China, Britain is very
prompt, but when she has to pay out the money she
becomes close-fisted. All cities and forts have
fallen through the hands of wilful Chiang.

Wang Ching-wei has returned from
Tokyo. He has made an inspection of the occupied
areas in Shanghai, and is now leading us in the peace
movement. As soon as peace is established, all the
occupied areas will be returned to us. The war of
resistance carried on by General Chiang Kai-shek aims
at the recovery of the lost territory but we can
achieve the same object without shedding a single
drop of blood. This shows that politics is mightier
than the sword. The Japanese Cabinet has been
reorganized three times but Prince Konoye's
manifesto has remained unchanged, while Wang Ching-wei's
peace proposals have remained also as firm as ever.
Dr. Sun Yat-sen once said: "The two countries China
and Japan will constitute the generative force in the
independence movements of the Asiatic races."
Chairman Wang Ching-wei is also laying the foundation
for permanent peace between these two countries. He
will look after the welfare of East Asia, the safety
of the Pacific and world peace.

1939年9月18日。下午译件

日本如今意识到其政策全然错误；因此，她希望结束战争。这确是实现东亚稳定的可喜途径。

世界局势瞬息万变。战争初起时，中国人民相信列强会在两年内对日本实施制裁，但迄今未采取任何行动。英国保持沉默，俄国则置身事外。

英日海关协定、俄日就张鼓峰事件达成的妥协、以及英日协定，这些难道都有利于中国？英国和俄国究竟援助了中国多少？英国在签署对华贷款时十分迅捷，但在实际付款时却变得吝啬抠门。所有城市和要塞皆因蒋介石的刚愎自用而失守。

汪精卫已从东京归来。他视察了上海的占领区，目前正领导我们开展和平运动。一旦和平确立，所有占领区都将归还给我们。蒋介石将军所进行的抗战旨在收复失地，但我们无需流一滴血即可达成同一目标。这表明政治力量胜于武力。日本内阁已改组三次，但近卫文麿亲王的宣言始终未变，而汪精卫的和平提议也依然坚定如初。孙中山博士曾说：“中日两国将构成亚洲民族独立运动的生成力量。”汪精卫主席也在为这两国之间的永久和平奠定基础。他将关照东亚的福祉、太平洋的安全以及世界和平。

CHINA PRESS.
SEP 20 1939
25410

Wang Bitterly
Denounced By
People's Meet

70 Resolutions Passed
During Chungking
Session

(United Press)

CHUNG-KING, Sept. 19.—Mr. Wang Ching-wei, ousted Kuomintang official, was bitterly denounced and Chinese troops were given a message of encouragement by the 4th session of the Peoples Political Council which adjourned yesterday.

Among the more than 70 resolutions adopted at the session was a measure urging the Government to fix a date for the National Peoples Convention with a view of adopting the constitution and realizing the constitutional rule and also asking the speaker of the Council to appoint a committee to assist the Government in achieving the constitutional form of government.

Measures suggested for this purpose requested the Government to issue a public mandate declaring all Chinese, with the exception of traitors, to be equal in legal and political status and also to improve the administrative machinery of the Government in accordance with wartime requirements.

Reconstruction Urged

The resolutions also urged the hastening of various phases of internal reconstruction, especially the development of Szechwan and Sikong as industrial bases, the improvement of the peoples' livelihood in those areas and the suppression of opium. The resolutions said that measures adopted by the special mission which investigated the two provinces should be followed.

The members urged that the Government publicly declare that all actions of "puppet regimes," whether internal or external, cannot be recognized by the Chinese nation.

They also resolved not to recognize any documentary contracts signed by the "puppet regimes" with any foreign country.

Wang Denounced

In connection with this, the P.P.C. prior to adjournment, issued a circular telegram denouncing Wang Ching-wei for "betrayal of his fatherland" and also declaring that all his utterances and actions since his departure from Chungking had run counter to the will of the Chinese nation.

The Council also issued separate messages to Chinese soldiers in the front lines and the Chinese people in Japanese occupied areas, conveying encouragement and sympathy respectively to them.

1939年9月20日
25410

民众集会
严厉谴责汪精卫

重庆会议期间
通过七十项决议

（合众社）

重庆，9月19日电——被罢黜的国民党官员汪精卫先生遭到严厉谴责，国民参政会第四届会议于昨日闭幕，并向中国军队传达了鼓励信息。

在此次会议通过的七十多项决议中，有一项措施敦促政府确定召开国民大会的日期，以期制定宪法并实现宪政，同时要求议长任命一个委员会，协助政府实现宪政体制。

为此目的提出的措施要求政府发布公开命令，宣布除汉奸外，所有中国人在法律和政治地位上一律平等，并根据战时需要改善政府的行政机构。

敦促重建

决议还敦促加快内部重建的各个阶段，特别是将四川和西康（Sikong）发展为工业基地，改善这些地区人民的生活，并禁止鸦片。决议称，应遵循调查这两个省份的特派团所采取的措施。

议员们敦促政府公开声明，“傀儡政权”的任何内外行动均不能得到中华民族的承认。

他们还决议不承认“傀儡政权”与任何外国签署的任何书面合同。

谴责汪精卫

鉴于此，国民参政会在休会前发出通电，谴责汪精卫“背叛祖国”，并声明他自离开重庆以来的所有言论和行动均违背了中华民族的意志。

议会还分别向前线的中国士兵和日军占领区的中国人民发出文告，分别向他们传达鼓励和同情。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
24939
SEP 20 1939
Plans Rushed for
New Government
Parties Negotiating for
Share, But Establishment
Unlikely by October 10

There is ample evidence in Shanghai that as the Russo-Japanese border armistice has provided moral support, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, the self-exiled deputy chief of the Kuomintang and his subordinates in Shanghai are doubling their efforts to advocate peace with Japan and confirmatory information is on hand that he is preparing to inaugurate a central government in Nanking, although it is premature to mention the date of inauguration.

Inquiries made by the "North-China Daily News" reveal that Mr. Wang has sent representatives to Nanking to make necessary preparations for setting up the new government. Informed Chinese circles find it hard to agree with the report that the new regime will be established on October 10 for negotiations among parties concerned will take some time.

Mr. Wang Keh-min, head of the provisional regime in Peiping has come here to negotiate with Mr. Wang Ching-wei. While Mr. Wang Keh-min may serve as a regional political political leader in Peiping, the Reformed Government in Nanking will be absorbed when the new central administration in the making comes into existence.

Maintaining Kuomintang principles and using the original Kuomintang flag, Mr. Wang Ching-wei will head the new Nanking regime in the making and, as such, his government will be different from the present one in Nanking which is considered to be more or less a temporary administration supported by the special service section of the Japanese military, it is learned.

Telegram to Colleagues

Soon after Soviet troops had entered into Poland, Mr. Wang Ching-wei again sent a telegram to his former colleagues at Chungking asking them to join his peace movement, asserting that help from other countries is not reliable. He says in the telegram that since the outbreak of hostilities in Europe hope for foreign help to China has been more and more diminished.

"People then argue that although Great Britain and France have no time to meddle with the Far East help from Soviet Russia can still be counted upon. But now Soviet Russia has joined Germany in attacking Poland. While the policy of a strong country is thus suddenly changeable and a weak country is suffering from the policy of making friends with remote countries while attacking its neighbour we can easily foresee our own future."

Mr. Wang asks his former colleagues not to question the sincerity of the Japanese in making peace terms for after all, the execution of peace terms depends on the sincerity shown and efforts made by both parties. He points out the danger of siding with communists and asserts that genuine Sino-Japanese co-operation by ending the hostilities is the only way to lasting peace.

《字林西报》。
24939
1939年9月20日
加速筹划新政府
各方正就席位进行谈判，但10月10日前成立的可能性不大

上海有充分迹象表明，随着苏日边境停战协定提供道义支持，自我流亡的国民党副总裁汪精卫先生及其在上海的下属正加倍努力倡导与日本和平相处；现有确凿消息表明，他正准备在南京成立中央政府，尽管提及成立日期尚为时过早。

《字林西报》的调查显示，汪先生已派遣代表前往南京，为建立新政府做必要准备。知情华人圈子难以认同新政权将于10月10日成立的报道，因为相关各方之间的谈判需要一些时间。

北平临时政权头目王克敏先生已来沪与汪精卫先生谈判。虽然王克敏先生可能担任北平地区的政治领袖，但当正在筹建的新中央行政机构成立时，南京的维新政府将被吸收合并。

据悉，汪精卫先生将坚持国民党原则并使用原国民党党旗，领导正在筹建中的南京新政权；因此，他的政府将不同于目前的南京政府，后者被认为或多或少是一个由日军特务机关支持的临时行政机构。

致同僚的电报

在苏军进入波兰后不久，汪精卫先生再次致电他在重庆的前同僚，邀请他们加入他的和平运动，声称其他国家的援助不可靠。他在电文中称，自欧洲战事爆发以来，中国获得外援的希望日益渺茫。

“人们当时争论说，虽然英国和法国无暇顾及远东，但仍可指望苏联俄罗斯的援助。但现在苏联俄罗斯已联合德国进攻波兰。既然强国的政策如此瞬息万变，而弱国因奉行远交近攻的政策而受苦，我们可以轻易预见我们自己的未来。”

汪先生要求他的前同僚不要质疑日本在提出和平条款方面的诚意，因为和平条款的执行毕竟取决于双方所表现的诚意和做出的努力。他指出依附共产主义者的危险，并断言通过结束敌对行动实现真正的中日合作是通往持久和平的唯一途径。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
SEP 20 1939

Letters To The Editor
Communications intended for publication in this column must be accompanied by the name and address of the sender, as a guarantee of good faith.

MR. WANG CHING-WEI'S PEACE MOVE
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—The speedy conclusion of peace in this part of the world being of such vital interest to all of us who reside here, I have recently been making such inquiries as are possible to the ordinary person into the only peace movement that has as yet made any progress, namely, that headed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei. From such sources as are available the following seems to be its history to date:
1.—In December, 1937, Dr. Trautmann, the German Ambassador, conveyed, to the Chinese Government, then established at Nanking certain proposals from Japan for the conclusion of peace. These were accepted by the Chinese Government as worthy of consideration; in particular General Chiang Kai-shek stated that they could be accepted as the basis on which to negotiate an honourable peace. Negotiations were started, but ultimately were broken off. No authoritative explanation has yet been given for this, but one learns from reliable sources that it was due to the action of General Chiang Kai-shek in referring the draft terms to Stalin for approval.
2.—In April, 1938, an Emergency Congress of the Kuomintang, held at Wuchang, laid down certain basic principles in regard to the negotiation of peace, and General Chiang Kai-shek and Mr. Wang Ching-wei were appointed to see this policy was carried out. These basic principles, summed up, amounted to (1) the inviolability of China's sovereign rights; (2) the maintenance of China's administrative independence; (3) economic equality and reciprocity.
3.—Immediately following on this Congress Mr. Kao Chung-wu was dispatched to Hongkong by General Chiang Kai-shek to initiate peace negotiations with the Japanese. Again negotiations broke down because of the vacillating attitude of the Generalissimo.
4.—During the same period, Mr. Ho Shih-chen was also entrusted by General Chiang Kai-shek with participation in peace talks with the Japanese in Shanghai.
5.—In December, 1938, Japan enunciated the Konoye peace proposals. These made no demand for an indemnity, or for any surrender of Chinese territory though they did require the recognition of Manchoukuo, which, it has been revealed, General Chiang Kai-shek had announced himself as ready to concede at the Wuchang Congress. No demand was put forward for the appointment of Japanese advisers to the Chinese Government, and full respect was promised for China's sovereignty. Disregarding the advice of Mr. Wang, who had been jointly charged with him by the Wuchang Congress with the duty of surveying possible avenues to peace, General Kai-shek refused even to consider the Konoye proposals, though they were less onerous to China than those which a year earlier he had declared could be accepted as the basis of an honourable peace.
6.—In consequence of General Chiang Kai-shek's "non possumus" attitude, Mr. Wang left Chungking in order to carry out by himself the duty of investigating peace proposals with which he had been charged. In his view, the Konoye proposals did constitute a basis for negotiations, subject to the granting by the Japanese as an integral condition of peace that "the withdrawal of the Japanese army from China in its totality should be prompt and universal in all directions."
7.—Since leaving Chungking, Mr. Wang has thoroughly explored the avenue to peace opened up by the Konoye proposals, and in conversation with the Japanese authorities, both military and civil, has obtained a clarification of the terms on which peace can be obtained. He proclaims himself satisfied that these do not infringe China's sovereignty or territorial rights, and, judging from what has been revealed of them to the public, there is no reason why his opinion should be disputed.

《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年9月20日

致编辑的信
凡拟在本栏发表的通信，必须附有发信人的姓名和地址，以资诚信。

汪精卫先生的和平举动
编辑先生，
《上海泰晤士报》
先生：——鉴于本地区的和平迅速达成对我们所有居住于此的人至关重要，我最近就唯一已取得进展的和平运动，即由汪精卫先生领导的和平运动，向普通人所能进行的范围进行了查询。根据现有资料，其迄今为止的历史似乎如下：
1.——1937年12月，德国大使陶德曼博士向当时设在南京的中国政府转达了日本方面关于缔结和平的某些提议。中国政府认为这些提议值得考虑；特别是蒋介石将军表示，可以接受这些提议作为谈判体面和平的基础。谈判随即开始，但最终还是破裂了。对此尚未给出权威解释，但从可靠消息来源得知，这是由于蒋介石将军将条款草案提交斯大林批准所致。
2.——1938年4月，在武昌举行的国民党紧急代表大会制定了关于和平谈判的某些基本原则，并任命蒋介石将军和汪精卫先生负责执行这一政策。这些基本原则概括起来包括：(1) 中国主权权利不可侵犯；(2) 维持中国的行政独立；(3) 经济平等与互惠。
3.——大会结束后不久，蒋介石将军即派遣高宗武先生前往香港，启动与日本的和平谈判。谈判再次因委员长摇摆不定的态度而破裂。
4.——在同一时期，何世桢先生也受蒋介石将军委托，参与在上海与日本进行的和平谈判。
5.——1938年12月，日本发表了近卫和平提议。这些提议没有要求赔款，也没有要求割让任何中国领土，尽管确实要求承认满洲国，而据透露，蒋介石将军曾在武昌大会上宣布自己准备在此问题上做出让步。提议中并未提出向中国政府派遣日本顾问的要求，并承诺充分尊重中国的主权。蒋介石将军不顾汪先生的建议——汪先生曾与他共同受武昌大会委托，负责考察可能的和平途径——甚至拒绝考虑近卫提议，尽管这些提议对中国造成的负担比一年前他宣称可作为体面和平基础的那些提议要轻。
6.——由于蒋介石将军采取“无法接受”（non possumus）的态度，汪先生离开重庆，以便独自履行其受命调查和平提议的职责。在他看来，近卫提议确实构成了谈判的基础，前提是日本方面作为和平的一个完整条件给予保证：“日军从全中国全面、迅速地撤军。”
7.——自离开重庆以来，汪先生已彻底探索了近卫提议所开启的和平途径，并在与日本军方和民政当局的会谈中，澄清了获得和平的条件。他宣称满意地认为，这些条件并不侵犯中国的主权或领土权利，而且从已向公众披露的内容来看，没有理由质疑他的观点。

因此，目前的局势是，汪精卫先生领导着一个实力雄厚的派系，而且该派系的追随者在人数和重要性上与日俱增。

另外两点事实值得强调：—

1—汪先生表示，如果蒋介石将军表现出与他合作的意愿，他愿意接受蒋将军的合作，以令人满意地执行所承诺的和平条款。

2.—蒋介石将军本人过去曾愿意在远不如目前所 offered 的条款条件下进行和平谈判。

那么，观察者不禁要问，是什么阻碍了蒋介石将军接受汪先生的合作提议？有人提出了两个理由：—

(a) 重庆的共产党势力已变得过于强大，使他无法违抗；

(b) 与汪先生合作将意味着他必须牺牲权力，而他并不准备做出这种牺牲。在此方面，可以提及朱明义博士（音译）于9月12日发表的声明，他在声明中透露，在汪先生离开重庆之前，他曾与孔祥熙博士的代表一起同日本进行和平谈判，而正是蒋介石将军的个人地位问题导致这些谈判破裂。

换言之，和平的主要障碍是共产党的阴谋诡计和蒋介石将军的个人野心。当然，这不能被陈述为绝对的事实，但值得注意的是，蒋介石将军尚未对这些指控的真实性发出任何令人满意或信服的否认。

上述记录的真实性似乎已得到充分证实。无论如何，最有责任对此加以反驳的一方，即重庆当局，并未试图予以驳斥。既然情况如此，人们几乎不可能怀疑汪精卫先生的诚意，或者在他的运动中看到除了争取体面和平的真诚中国努力之外的任何东西。诚然，鉴于蒋介石将军仍然坚持一种长期的、且就目前看来徒劳无益的抵抗政策，汪先生的运动无疑提供了目前确保此类和平的最佳途径。

从表面上看，因此，似乎没有理由不让它获得外国人以及中国人的祝福，即便不是积极支持。对于前者来说，它还具有额外的吸引力，即为日本与第三方强国之间的分歧提供了一座可能的桥梁。后者不妨利用他们对蒋介石将军可能具有的任何影响力，促使他与汪先生保持一致。

考虑到汪先生准备据以谈判和平的唯一条件，在支持由他领导的和平政府时，不存在背叛中国或以任何方式认可通过单边行动造成的领土或其他变化的问题。

MALAYAN.
上海，1939年9月19日。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
SEP 20 1939
China Incident:
A Plea for Peace
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—The speedy conclusion of peace in this part of the world being of such vital interest to all of us who reside here, I have recently been making such enquiries as are possible to the ordinary person into the only peace movement that has as yet made any progress, namely that headed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei. From such sources as are available the following seems to be its history to date.

1. In December, 1937, Dr. Trautmann, the German Ambassador, conveyed to the Chinese Government, then established at Nanking, certain proposals from Japan for the conclusion of peace. These were accepted by the Chinese Government as worthy of consideration; in particular General Chiang Kai-shek stated that they could be accepted as the basis on which to negotiate an honourable peace. Negotiations were started, but ultimately were broken off. No authoritative explanation has yet been given for this, but one learns from reliable sources that it was due to the action of General Chiang Kai-shek in referring the draft terms to Stalin for approval.

2. In April, 1938, an Emergency Congress of the Kuomintang, held at Wuchang, laid down certain basic principles in regard to the negotiation of peace, and General Chiang Kai-shek and Mr. Wang Ching-wei were appointed to see that this policy was carried out. These basic principles summed up amounted to (1) the inviolability of China's sovereign rights (2) the maintenance of China's administrative independence (3) economic equality and reciprocity.

3. Immediately following on this Congress Mr. Kao Chung-wu was despatched to Hongkong by General Chiang Kai-shek to initiate peace negotiations with the Japanese. Again negotiations broke down because of the vacillating attitude of the Generalissimo.

4. During the same period Mr. Ho Shih-chen was also entrusted by General Chiang Kai-shek with participation in peace talks with the Japanese in Shanghai.

5. In December, 1938, Japan enunciated the Konoye peace proposals. These made no demand for an indemnity, or for any surrender of Chinese territory though they did require the recognition of Manchoukuo, which, it has since been revealed, General Chiang Kai-shek had announced himself as ready to concede at the Wuchang Congress. No demand was put forward for the appointment of Japanese advisers to the Chinese Government, and full respect was promised for China's sovereignty. Disregarding the advice of Mr. Wang, who had been jointly charged with him by the Wuchang Congress with the duty of surveying possible avenues to peace, General Chiang Kai-shek refused even to consider the Konoye proposals, though they were less onerous to China than those which a year earlier he had declared could be accepted as the basis of an honourable peace.

6. In consequence of General Chiang Kai-shek's non possumus attitude Mr. Wang left Chungking in order to carry out by himself the duty of investigating peace proposals with which he had been charged. In his view the Konoye proposals did constitute a basis for negotiations, subject to the granting by the Japanese of an explicit declaration of peace that "the withdrawal of the Japanese army from China in its totality should be prompt and universal in all directions."

7. Since leaving Chungking Mr. Wang has thoroughly explored the avenue to peace opened up by the Konoye proposals, and in conversation with the Japanese authorities, both military and civil, has obtained a clarification of the terms on which peace can be obtained. He proclaims himself satisfied that these do not infringe China's sovereignty or territorial rights, and, judging from what has been revealed of them to the public, there is no reason why his opinion should be disputed.

Thus the situation stands today, with Mr. Wang Ching-wei heading

先生，——鉴于本地区迅速实现和平对我们所有居住于此的人至关重要，我最近就迄今为止唯一取得进展的和平运动，即由汪精卫先生领导的运动，进行了普通人所能进行的调查。根据现有资料，其迄今的历史概况如下。

1. 1937年12月，德国大使陶德曼博士向当时设在南京的中国政府转达了日本方面关于缔结和平的某些提议。中国政府认为这些提议值得考虑并予以接受；特别是蒋介石将军表示，可以接受这些提议作为谈判体面和平的基础。谈判随即开始，但最终以破裂告终。对此尚无权威解释，但从可靠消息来源获悉，这是由于蒋介石将军将条款草案提交斯大林批准所致。

2. 1938年4月，在武昌举行的国民党临时全国代表大会制定了关于和平谈判的若干基本原则，并任命蒋介石将军和汪精卫先生负责执行这一政策。这些基本原则概括起来包括：(1) 中国主权不可侵犯；(2) 保持中国行政独立；(3) 经济平等与互惠。

3. 大会结束后不久，蒋介石将军即派遣高宗武先生前往香港，以启动与日本的和平谈判。谈判再次因委员长摇摆不定的态度而破裂。

4. 同期，何世桢先生也受蒋介石将军委托，参与在上海与日本进行的和平会谈。

5. 1938年12月，日本发表了近卫和平提议。这些提议未要求赔款，也未要求割让任何中国领土，尽管确实要求承认满洲国，而据后来披露，蒋介石将军曾在武昌大会上宣布准备对此作出让步。提议中并未提出向中国政府派遣日本顾问的要求，并承诺充分尊重中国主权。蒋介石将军不顾汪精卫先生的劝告——武昌大会曾共同赋予二人考察可能和平途径的职责——甚至拒绝考虑近卫提议，尽管这些提议对中国造成的负担比一年前他宣称可作为体面和平基础接受的提议要轻。

7. 自离开重庆以来，汪精卫先生已彻底探索了近卫提议所开启的和平途径，并在与日本军政当局的会谈中，澄清了实现和平的条件。他宣称满意于这些条件并未侵犯中国的主权或领土权利，而且从已向公众披露的内容来看，没有理由质疑他的观点。

CHINA PRESS.

SEP 1 5 1939

WANG SET-UP SAID
FIXED OCTOBER 10

Puppet Government
Heads To Meet
Here Sunday

(Reuters)
PEIPING, Sept. 14.—Local movements and news from "Manchukuo" are causing much speculation whether the new Japanese army command in China will pay more attention to China or Russia.
The Japanese spokesman here admits that a number of empty military trains have gone down the Peiping-Hankow Railway, presumably to bring up troops from Shansi, while reliable foreign reports filtering in from Manchuria declare that a few days ago the Russians broke through the Japanese center on the Nomonhan front.
The messages quote reliable Japanese sources in Chungchan as stating that the Russians have advanced five kilometers on a 30-kilometer front.
Renewed Action Seen
For this reason, the general expectation here is renewed Japanese action to restore the "Manchukuo" frontier.
Meanwhile, informed Chinese political circles forecast that Wang Ching-wei's "central government" will be established by October 10.
Wang Keh-min, head of the "Provisional Government," is flying to Shanghai on September 17 to participate in preliminary discussions.
Set-Up Forecast
It is stated here that the "Provisional Government" will contribute five ministers and the "Reformed Government" three, with Wang Ching-wei bringing in the remainder from his followers.
Wang Keh-min, it is stated, will remain here as head of a semi-independent political council, which will exercise its influence north of the Yellow River and will be run on similar lines to the Hopei-Chahar Political Council before the hostilities began.

北平，9月14日电。——当地的动向以及来自“满洲国”的消息，引发了诸多猜测，人们揣测日本在华的新陆军司令部会将更多注意力放在中国还是俄罗斯身上。
此间的日本发言人承认，已有数列空载的军用列车沿平汉铁路南下，据推测是为了从山西调运部队；与此同时，从满洲方面传来的可靠外国报告称，几天前俄军在诺门罕战线突破了日军的中部防线。
这些消息援引中chan（原文不清）方面可靠的日本消息来源称，俄军已在三十公里的正面上推进了五公里。
预计将重新采取行动
因此，此地普遍预期日军将再次采取行动，以恢复“满洲国”的边界。
与此同时，中国政界知情人士预测，汪精卫的“中央政府”将于十月十日前成立。
“临时政府”首脑王克敏将于九月十七日飞抵上海，参加预备讨论。
预计组建架构
据悉，“临时政府”将提供五名部长，“维新政府”提供三名，其余人员则由汪精卫从其追随者中选派。
据悉，王克敏将留在此地，担任一个半独立政治委员会的首脑，该委员会将在黄河以北地区施加影响，其运作方式将与战事爆发前的冀察政务委员会类似。

September 7, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-

DR. CHU MIN-NYI, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE DECISIONS OF THE CENTRAL EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE, DESPATCHES A CIRCULAR TELEGRAM TO COMRADES IN CHUNGKING, URGING THEM TO SAVE THE NATION BY CONCLUDING PEACE

In accordance with the decisions passed at the Central Executive Committee, Dr. Chu Min-nyi, Chief Secretary of the Central Executive Committee of the revived Kuomintang, despatched on September 5 a lengthy telegram to comrades and committee members of the Central Supervisory Committee and of the Central Executive Committee at Chungking, stating that in view of the internal and external conditions in China to-day, the present is the best time for the comrades to rise and save the nation by means of peace so that the military operations may be stopped at once. He advised General Chiang Kai-shek to retire.

The following is a summary of Dr. Chu Min-nyi's telegram :-

Chinese and Japanese troops fought in Shanghai. General Chiang Kai-shek's party sought the co-operation of the Communist Party, thereby permitting military and political control to slip into the hands of the Communist Party. Now affairs seem to have reached such a state that host and guest are changing positions. This is much regretted.

Peace is absolutely essential for the existence of the nation. If our right of independence is to be respected and upheld, all organs of the nation should at once adopt measures for peace. Two years have passed since the outbreak of the incident. How much has the nation lost and suffered during this period! Why is General Chiang Kai-shek still shouting to-day for a protracted war of resistance? Under present circumstances, General Chiang is probably uncertain of winning final victory. Furthermore, Prince Konoye has clearly stated that Japan has no territorial ambitions, will make no demand for concessions of land, nor will she request compensation for war expenses. It is clearly explained that the right of self-determination and independence of China will be unharmed. So we request the Chiang Kai-shek clique to retire.

Wang Ching-wei, in support of Prince Konoye's manifesto, introduced the idea of saving the nation by peace and fled from Chungking, but his fellow-members of the Kuomintang are still in Chungking under the surveillance of the Communist Party and the Chiang Kai-shek clique and cannot give voice to their proposals.

We should think of the nation first and not of ourselves. Now war has broken out between Great Britain and France on the one side and the Germany on the other, but China and Japan should maintain peace in East Asia and be determined to establish a new order in East Asia. The Chiang clique should take advantage of the present opportunity to retire so that Chairman Wang may freely exercise his authority. The comrades at Chungking are advised to come to Shanghai to discuss national affairs.

1939年9月7日。下午译件。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：-

褚民谊博士遵照中央执行委员会之决议，向重庆同志发出通电，促其通过议和以救国

复兴中国国民党之中央执行委员会秘书长褚民谊博士，依据中央执行委员会所通过之决议，于9月5日向在重庆之中央监察委员会及中央执行委员会诸同志及委员发出一长篇电报，称鉴于当今中国之内外部形势，此刻乃同志们奋起通过和平手段救国之最佳时机，以便立即停止军事行动。他建议蒋介石将军下野。

以下为褚民谊博士电文摘要：-

中日军队在上海交战。蒋介石一派寻求与共产党合作，致使军政大权落入共产党之手。如今事态似乎已发展至主客易位之地步。此点令人深感遗憾。

和平对于国家之生存绝对必要。若欲尊重并维护我国之独立权利，国家各机关应立即采取和平措施。事变爆发至今已逾两年。在此期间，国家遭受了多少损失与苦难！为何蒋介石将军今日仍高呼长期抗战？在目前形势下，蒋将军恐怕对赢得最终胜利并无把握。此外，近卫亲王已明确声明，日本并无领土野心，不会要求割让土地，亦不要求赔偿战费。文中清楚阐明，中国之自决权与独立权将不受损害。因此，我们要求蒋介石集团下野。

汪精卫为支持近卫亲王之宣言，提出和平救国之主张并离开重庆，但其国民党同仁仍身处重庆，受共产党及蒋介石集团之监视，无法发表其主张。

我们应先考虑国家，而非个人。如今英法一方与德国一方之间已爆发战争，但中日两国应在东亚维持和平，并决心建立东亚新秩序。蒋集团应利用当前机会下野，以便汪主席自由行使职权。建议重庆诸同志来沪商讨国事。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
SEP 3 1939

Foreign Journalists In
Shanghai Entertained
By Mr. Wang Ching-wei

International Gathering Hears Explanation Of
Peace Move; Says Object Is To Save China
From National Extinction

SUCCESS OF MOVEMENT WILL NOT HURT
FOREIGN RIGHTS AND INTERESTS

A large party of foreign journalists, representing Shanghai foreign-language newspapers, news agencies and leading overseas journals, was entertained to tea by Mr. Wang Ching-wei at his residence yesterday afternoon.

During the course of the gathering, Mr. Wang delivered an address in explanation of his peace move, in which he said that the main aim was to save China from national extinction. The success of the movement should not affect the interests of the foreign Powers, neither will China's co-operation with Japan to safeguard East Asia be detrimental to foreign interests, he said.

Mr. Wang spoke as follows:
Members of the Foreign Press,—
It is with great pleasure that I am meeting you here to-day. Last year, in December, I left Chungking, having failed in my repeated attempts to persuade the Central Kuomintang and the National Government at Chungking to seize the opportunity to negotiate an honourable peace. They know clearly that peace was at hand, but being dominated and, in fact, controlled by the communists they refused to avail themselves of the means to put an end to the war of resistance, in accordance with the principles laid down by the Manifesto of the Emergency National Congress of the Kuomintang of April, 1938. So I had no alternative but to leave Chungking, in response to the real will of the people and at the request of many comrades, in order that I could freely express my views and be heard by the masses of the people. For a time I stayed in Hanoi, and then, after a visit to Tokyo, I went to various cities under occupation, such as Peking, Nanking and Canton. The purpose of my visiting Tokyo was to find out whether the Declaration of Prince Konoye of December 22 and my Peace Proposals of December 29, could be made a reality. I further wanted to bring about the moral unity between the masses and comrades at Chungking and those in the occupied areas. To achieve our task we must carry out two steps; the first is Party Renaissance; that is, to restore the original character of the Kuomintang and its liberty of action independent of outside influences. The second is to save China from destruction by putting an end to a futile and meaningless war and inaugurating an era of peace. The Sixth National Congress of the Kuomintang has just been held and its Manifesto and the various resolutions were passed by unanimous vote. Having accomplished the first step of my task I thus take this opportunity to meet you...

**〔此处转录不清〕**

of these inquiries can be answered collectively, others individually, while to some no answer can yet be given.

Some one asked how I, expelled by Chungking, can have still the authority to conduct activities in the name of the Party. This is indeed a very frank question, which I welcome and will answer in the same spirit.

The first point to remember is that the highest organ in the Kuomintang is its National Congress. Whosoever contravene the resolutions passed and adopted by that body, are committing illegal acts. Now, my Peace Proposals were actually based on the Manifesto issued by the Emergency National Congress. It is the Chungking Central Kuomintang and the Chungking Government which, in contravening that Manifesto, have committed illegal acts. It is they who are the guilty party, certainly not me.

Secondly, the Kuomintang is a revolutionary party. In the execution of its function in ordinary times, ordinary methods of procedure must be employed. But in times of emergency, a special procedure is called for, in accordance with the revolutionary spirit of a revolutionary Party. There are many such instances in the history of the Party.

Back In 1927
For instance, in 1927, when the Central Kuomintang and the National Government were still in Wuhan, General Chiang Kai-shek, who was then in Nanking, seceded from the National Government on the ground that that Government was completely dominated and controlled by the Communists. He therefore organized a new Government, and commenced a general Party purge. The Central Kuomintang in Wuhan decreed the expulsion of General Chiang Kai-shek and the National Government issued a warrant for his apprehension and arrest. But subsequently, the Central Kuomintang and the National Government found out that the Communists were carrying the Communist elements, and decided to co-operate with the Nationalist people...

1939年9月3日

汪精卫先生宴请
驻沪外国记者

国际集会听取和平运动说明；称其宗旨在于挽救中国免于民族灭亡

运动成功将不损害外侨权利与利益

昨日下午，汪精卫先生在其寓所设茶会，款待了大批外国记者，他们代表了上海的外文报纸、通讯社以及主要的海外期刊。

在聚会期间，汪先生发表讲话，解释其和平运动的缘由。他表示，主要宗旨在于挽救中国免于民族灭亡。他说，该运动的成功不应影响列强的利益，中国与日本合作以保卫东亚也不会损害外国的利益。

汪先生的讲话如下：
各位外国新闻界同仁——
今日在此与诸位会面，我深感荣幸。去年十二月，我离开重庆，因为我多次试图劝说重庆的国民党中央和国民政府抓住机会谈判一项体面的和平，但均告失败。他们清楚地知道和平近在咫尺，但由于受到共产党的支配，实际上受其控制，他们拒绝利用结束抗战的手段，尽管这符合1938年4月国民党临时全国代表大会宣言所制定的原则。因此，为了顺应人民的真实意愿，并应许多同志的请求，我别无选择，只能离开重庆，以便能够自由表达我的观点，并被广大民众所倾听。我在河内停留了一段时间，随后访问东京，之后前往北平、南京和广州等各占领区城市。我访问东京的目的是为了查明近卫公爵于12月22日发表的声明和我于12月29日提出的和平建议能否成为现实。我还希望促成重庆的民众和同志与占领区的民众和同志在道义上的统一。为了完成我们的任务，我们必须采取两个步骤；第一步是党的复兴；即恢复国民党的本来面目，使其行动自由不受外界影响。第二步是通过结束一场徒劳且无意义的战争，开启和平时代，从而挽救中国免于毁灭。国民党第六次全国代表大会刚刚召开，其宣言和各项决议均以全票通过。既然我已经完成了任务的第一步，我便借此机会与诸位见面……

**〔此处转录不清〕**

有些询问可以集体回答，有些则需个别回答，而有些问题目前尚无法作答。

有人问，我既已被重庆方面开除，何以仍有权以党的名义开展活动。这确实是一个非常直率的问题，我对此表示欢迎，并将以同样的坦诚精神予以回答。

首先要记住的一点是，国民党的最高机构是其全国代表大会。任何违背该机构通过和采纳的决议的人，都是在从事非法行为。现在，我的和平建议实际上是依据临时全国代表大会发布的宣言提出的。正是重庆的国民党中央和重庆政府违背了该宣言，从事了非法行为。有罪的一方是他们，肯定不是我。

其次，国民党是一个革命政党。在平时履行其职能时，必须采用常规的程序方法。但在紧急时期，根据革命政党的革命精神，需要采取特殊程序。党的历史上有很多这样的例子。

回到1927年
例如，1927年，当国民党中央和国民政府仍在武汉时，当时在南京的蒋介石将军以该政府完全被共产党支配和控制为由，脱离国民政府。因此，他组织了一个新政府，并开始进行全面的党内清洗。武汉的国民党中央下令开除蒋介石将军，国民政府发布了通缉令逮捕他。但随后，国民党中央和国民政府发现共产党正在推行共产主义元素，并决定与国民党人士合作……

Personal Statement
The following year, in 1925, I strongly opposed the personal dictatorship of General Chiang Kai-shek at Nanking, which had led to internal strifes and rudely shaken the foundations of the nation. The Central Kuomintang and the National Government in Nanking, thereupon, decreed my expulsion from the party, and issued an order for my arrest. In 1930 and 1931, I successively organised the Enlarged Party Convention in Peking and the Extraordinary Party Convention in Canton, to oppose General Chiang's Dictatorship. Then the "Manchurian Incident" took place on September 18, 1931. General Chiang sent representatives to Canton to negotiate with us for co-operation, and a conference was subsequently called in Shanghai to settle our differences in the interests of national unity. I then assumed office as President of the Executive Yuan of the National Government in Nanking. Such are the instances in the past. The present developments in the Party are clearly indicated in the Manifesto issued and the measures adopted by the Sixth National Congress which are available to the general public.

Visit To Tokyo
Now let me tell you something of my visit to Tokyo. Shortly after the Emergency National Congress of the Kuomintang in April last year, General Chiang relieved Mr. Kao Chung-wu of his post as the director of the Asiatic Department in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and entrusted him with the important mission to go to Hongkong to arrange peace negotiations with Japan. The allegation that Mr. Kao Chung-wu acted on his own and was without authority is therefore absolutely untrue. During the negotiations there had been many opportunities for both parties to come closely together, but they always stumbled on the question of General Chiang, which caused him frequently to change his mind on the question of peace. My visit to Tokyo was not along a new line of approach; it was only to prevent the negotiations started Mr. Kao Chung-Wu from breaking down. And the results of my negotiations with the Japanese authorities during my visit to Tokyo gave a concrete basis to my belief that Prince Konoye's Declaration and my Peace Proposals can be made a reality.

False Rumours
With regard to my various visits to the occupied areas, I regret to say that wherever I went, rumours immediately circulated to the effect that I was establishing a Government in that locality. And on my departure, the rumours had it that I had failed in my efforts. All this, of course, is part of the Chungking campaign of malicious misrepresentation of my activities. The fact was that I was merely carrying out my task of discussing with my comrades and those non-Party patriots who have the same views, how best to save the situation and carry out our responsibilities. In addition, I met, and discussed with, the competent Japanese military authorities with a view to secure the proper realisation of certain concrete measures to save the situation.
Our first step, Party Renaissance, has been accomplished. Our second step, the realization of the concrete plans for saving the situation, is now undertaken. But it has at the present moment not yet reached the stage of organising the national Government, and I am therefore not yet in a position to answer any queries concerning the Chinese Customs revenues, the currency and other fiscal matters which are **〔此处转录不清〕**
pages.zh:
个人陈述

次年，即一九二五年，我强烈反对蒋介石将军在南京的个人独裁，该独裁导致内部纷争，并粗暴地动摇了国家根基。国民党中央及南京国民政府随即下令将我开除出党，并发布通缉令。一九三〇年及一九三一年，我先后在北京组织国民党扩大会议，在广州组织非常会议，以反对蒋介石将军的独裁统治。随后，一九三一年九月十八日发生“满洲事变”。蒋介石将军派遣代表前往广州与我们谈判合作事宜，随后在上海召开会议，为谋求国家统一而解决我们的分歧。我随后就任南京国民政府行政院院长。以上即为过往事例。目前党内之发展，已明确体现于已公开发布的宣言及第六次全国代表大会所采取的措施中。

访问东京

现在让我谈谈我访问东京的情况。去年四月国民党临时全国代表大会结束后不久，蒋介石将军免去了高宗武先生外交部亚洲司司长的职务，并委以其重任，前往香港安排与日本的和平谈判。因此，所谓高宗武先生擅自行动、未经授权的说法完全不实。在谈判期间，双方曾多次有机会拉近关系，但总是卡在关于蒋介石将军的问题上，这导致他在和平问题上经常改变主意。我访问东京并非采取新的途径；其目的仅仅是为了防止高宗武先生开启的谈判破裂。我在访问东京期间与日本当局谈判的结果，使我有具体依据相信，近卫文麿亲王的声明与我的和平提议能够成为现实。

虚假谣言

关于我多次访问沦陷区一事，遗憾地说，无论我去到哪里，立刻就有谣言流传，称我正在当地建立政府。而当我离开时，谣言又说我努力失败。当然，这一切都是重庆方面恶意歪曲我活动的宣传攻势的一部分。事实是，我只是在执行我的任务，与同志及持有相同观点的非党爱国人士讨论如何最好地挽救局势并履行我们的责任。此外，我还与日本军方主管当局会面并进行讨论，旨在确保某些挽救局势的具体措施得到适当落实。
我们的第一步，“党的复兴”，已经完成。我们的第二步，即实施挽救局势的具体计划，目前正在开展。但目前尚未达到组织国民政府的阶段，因此我尚无法回答有关中国关税收入、货币及其他财政事项的询问，这些事项**〔此处转录不清〕**

pages.en:
Japanese Troops
With regard to the withdrawal of
the Japanese troops from China, it
must be borne in mind that evacu-
ation is always the result of peace.
And while the Chungking Govern-
ment is still shouting Resistance, it
is obvious that no general evacua-
tion can be effected, which can only
take place after peace is re-
established and the nation unified
as a result of the downfall of the
present Chungking regime.
The question has been raised,
whether the Chinese forces are
adequate for taking over the evacu-
ated areas. The answer to this
question is, first, that any Chinese
army which publicly adheres to
the peace and anti-Communist
policy as laid down by the Mani-
festo of the Sixth National Con-
gress will be left intact and will
therefore be in a position to re-
occupy the areas evacuated.
Secondly, as a result of the depre-
dations of the guerrillas, the popu-
lace in the respective war areas
have now organized militia units
for their self-protection. They have
voiced their support for the peace
and anti-Communist movement and
will be able with their militia to
maintain local peace and order.
With regard to foreign policy,
the Manifesto of the Sixth National
Congress has clearly pointed out
that China will co-operate with
Japan in maintaining the peace in
East Asia, while at the same time
will co-operate with other foreign
Powers in furthering the cause of
world peace. China will accord
due respect and protection to legit-
imate foreign rights and interests
in China. Such a policy is not
only part of China's diplomacy, but
is a corrollary of China's policy of
promoting international economic
co-operation.
The question of recognition of the
National Government by the for-
eign Powers, will, in my view,
hardly arise. For our Government
is actually and legitimately the
National Government purged of its
Communist and Communist-domin-
ated elements who will be replaced
by peace-loving and anti-Commun-
ist elements. Therefore, whatever
changes brought about will be con-
fined to personal and policy; the
legal status of the Government,
internally and internationally, will
remain substantially unchanged.
And even if some of the foreign
Powers should propose the non-
recognition of the our National Gov-
ernment, the matter is of minor
importance.
Aim of Movement
For it may be recalled that when
we brought about the downfall of
the Manchu Dynasty in 1911, it took
two years for new Republican Gov-
ernment to be internationally re-
cognized. The National Govern-
ment was established in 1925 in
Canton, but it was not until 1927,
after the conclusion of Northern
Expedition which brought the
downfall of the Peiyang militarists,
that the formal recognition was
accorded. By way of contrast,
formal recognition by the Powers
did not save the Spanish Repub-
lican Government from extinction
after flight of the republican leaders
to Franco.
In short, our aim is to save China
from national extinction; our suc-
cess should not affect the interests
of the foreign Powers. Neither
will China's co-operation with
Japan to safeguard East Asia be
detrimental to foreign interests.
And it is hoped that the foreign
Governments and public leaders
will give a sympathetic under-
standing to our true aims and co-
operate with us for the common
welfare.

pages.zh:
日军

关于日军从中国撤军一事，必须铭记，撤军始终是和平的结果。既然重庆政府仍在高呼“抵抗”，显然无法实现全面撤军，只有待和平重建、现重庆政权垮台从而使国家统一之后，全面撤军方能进行。

有人提出，中国军队是否有足够能力接管撤军后的地区。对此问题的回答是：第一，任何公开拥护第六次全国代表大会宣言所制定的和平与反共政策的中国军队，都将保持建制完整，因此有能力重新占领撤军后的地区。第二，由于游击队的劫掠，各战区的民众现已组织民团以自保。他们已表示支持和平与反共运动，并能够凭借其民团力量维持地方治安与秩序。

在外交政策方面，第六次全国代表大会宣言明确指出，中国将与日本合作，以维护东亚和平，同时将与其他外国列强合作，以促进世界和平事业。中国将对在华合法的外国权益给予应有的尊重和保护。此项政策不仅是中国外交的一部分，也是中国促进国际经济合作政策的必然结果。

至于外国列强承认国民政府的问题，依我之见，几乎不会成为问题。因为我们的政府实际上且合法地乃是清除了共产党及受共产党支配分子的国民政府，这些分子将由爱好和平及反共分子所取代。因此，无论发生何种变化，都将局限于人事和政策层面；政府的法律地位，无论在国内还是国际上，都将基本保持不变。即便某些外国列强提议不承认我们的国民政府，此事也无关紧要。

运动的目标

不妨回顾，当我们于1911年推翻满清王朝时，新的共和政府花了两年时间才获得国际承认。国民政府于1925年在广州成立，但直到1927年北伐结束、北洋军阀垮台后，才获得正式承认。相比之下，尽管西班牙共和政府获得了列强的正式承认，但在共和派领导人逃往佛朗哥（Franco）处后，仍未能避免灭亡的命运。

总之，我们的目标是拯救中国免于亡国；我们的成功不应影响外国列强的利益。中国与日本合作保卫东亚，也不会损害外国利益。希望各国政府及公众领袖能同情并理解我们的真正目标，并与我们合作，以谋求共同福祉。

CHINA PRESS.
SEP 8 1939
24667

Wang Explains
Peace Plans To
Newsmen Here

Foreign Correspondents
Hear Views Of
Ousted Leader

The dark veil of secrecy which has surrounded Mr. Wang Ching-wei since his flight from Chungking last December was lifted momentarily for the benefit of Shanghai's foreign newsmen yesterday when the expelled Kuomintang Deputy Chief Executive made his first public personal appearance to explain his views on peace with Japan.

In his prepared statement read to the assembled foreign correspondents and staff members of the local foreign press, Mr. Wang openly confessed that he has visited Tokyo, kept in close touch with the Japanese military authorities in China and visited Japanese-occupied Nanking, Peiping and Canton in order to discuss with "my comrades and non-party patriots" the ways and means of carrying out "our responsibility."

Some 20 foreign newspapermen, including two Japanese, were present at the tea reception which was held at Mr. Wang's palatial and closely guarded residence at House 32 Lane 1136 Yu Yuen Road. A number of Chinese, all of whom are associates of the expelled Kuomintang leader, were also present at the party. These included among others, Dr. Chu Ming-i, formerly Secretary-General of the Executive Yuan during Mr. Wang's regime, and Mr. Tang Leang-li, editor of the People's Tribune.

House Guarded

Newsmen who attended the party found the immense brick house, which at one time belonged to Mr. Wang Pei-chuen, former Minister of Communications, guarded by scores of plainclothes men. In the lane from Yu Yuen Road, a number of Chinese guards kept a close watch, while at the main iron grill gate, two men armed with Mausers grimly scrutinized the guests entering the premises.

The newspapermen were asked to leave their hats at the gate house. One correspondent who was carrying a walking cane was asked to check his stick outside before he entered the house. Ushered into the main reception room of the residence, wherein every window was protected by wired, bomb-proof glass, the correspondents waited expectantly for the appearance of the host against whom the Chinese National Government had decreed arrest and punishment.

汪精卫向在沪记者
阐述和平计划

外国记者
聆听被黜领袖之观点

自去年十二月逃离重庆以来，一直笼罩在汪精卫先生身上的神秘面纱，昨日为上海的外国新闻界人士暂时揭开。这位被开除的国民党副总裁首次公开露面，以阐释其对日和平之观点。

在向聚集于此的外国通讯员及本地外文报刊工作人员宣读的预先准备好的声明中，汪先生坦承，他曾访问东京，与中国境内的日本军事当局保持密切联系，并走访了日军占领下的南京、北平和广州，以便与“我的同志及无党派爱国人士”商讨履行“我们的责任”之途径与方法。

约有二十名外国新闻记者（其中包括两名日本人）出席了在愚园路1136弄32号汪先生那座宫殿式且戒备森严的宅邸举行的茶会。多名中国人也参加了此次聚会，他们均为这位被黜国民党领导人的亲信。其中包括前汪伪政权时期行政院秘书长褚民谊博士，以及《人民论坛》编辑唐良礼（音译）等人。

宅邸戒备森严

参加聚会的记者发现，这座巨大的砖砌房屋（曾属前交通部部长王伯群所有）由数十名便衣人员把守。在从愚园路进入弄堂的通道上，数名中国警卫严密监视；而在主要的铁栅大门处，两名手持毛瑟枪的男子神情严峻地审视着进入宅邸的客人。

记者们被要求在门房处留下帽子。一名携带手杖的记者被要求在入屋前将手杖寄存在外面。记者们被引入宅邸的主接待室，该处每扇窗户均装有带铁丝网的防弹玻璃。他们在此殷切等待主人的出现，而中国政府已下令逮捕并惩办此人。

Speaks In Chinese
Rising during tea, Mr. Wang read his lengthy statement to a hushed assemblage. Apart from his associates, few understood what he said because his statement, read with little expression, was in Chinese. The statement was later translated into English by one of Mr. Wang's secretaries. Mimeographed copies of the speech were subsequently distributed to the correspondents together with other literature on Mr. Wang's peace movement.
The expelled Kuomintang official proclaimed that his mission at the present time lies in the accomplishment of two objectives: "Party renaissance," and the ending of the "futile and meaningless war" by inaugurating "an era of peace." He revealed that a so-called "Sixth National Congress of the Kuomintang" had been held recently under his auspices.
Referring to his secret trip to Tokyo, Mr. Wang said that his talks in the Japanese capital were conducted in order to find out whether the declaration of Prince Konoye on December 22 and his own peace proposal of December 31 could be made a reality.
"Shortly after the Emergency National Congress of Kuomintang in April last year," Mr. Wang said, "General Chiang relieved Mr. Kao Chung-wu of his posts as the director of the Asiatic Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and entrusted him with the important mission of going to Hongkong to arrange peace negotiations with Japan. The allegation that Mr. Kao Chung-wu acted on his own and was without authority is therefore absolutely untrue. During the negotiations there had been many opportunities for both parties to come closely together, but they always stumbled on the question of the personal position of General Chiang, which caused him frequently to change his mind on the question of peace. My visit to Tokyo was not along a new line of approach. It was to prevent the negotiations started by Mr. Kao Chung-wu from breaking down. And the result of my negotiations with Japanese authorities during my visit to Tokyo gave concrete basis to my belief that Prince Konoye's declaration and my peace proposal can be made a reality."

用中文发言

王先生在茶歇期间起身，向鸦雀无声的集会人群宣读了他的长篇声明。除了他的随从人员外，很少有人听懂他的话，因为他的声明是用中文宣读的，且语调平淡无奇。该声明随后由王先生的一位秘书翻译成英文。演讲的油印副本随后连同有关王先生和平运动的其他宣传材料一并分发给各位记者。

这位被开除的国民党官员宣称，他目前的使命在于实现两个目标：“党之复兴”，以及通过开启“和平时代”来结束“徒劳且无意义的战争”。他透露，近期在他的主持下召开了一次所谓的“国民党第六次全国代表大会”。

谈及他秘密访问东京一事，王先生表示，他在日本首都进行的会谈旨在探明近卫亲王于12月22日发表的声明以及他自己于12月31日提出的和平建议能否成为现实。

王先生说：“在去年4月召开的国民党临时全国代表大会之后不久，蒋将军免去了高宗武外交部亚洲司司长的职务，并委以重任，派其前往香港安排与日本的和平谈判。因此，所谓高宗武擅自行动、未经授权的指控纯属不实。在谈判过程中，双方曾多次有机会拉近立场，但总是因蒋将军的个人地位问题而受阻，这导致他在和平问题上经常改变主意。我访问东京并非采取新的途径，而是为了防止高宗武发起的谈判破裂。我在访问东京期间与日本当局谈判的结果，为我相信近卫亲王的声明和我的和平建议能够成为现实提供了具体依据。”

政府尚未准备就绪

汪先生告诉记者们，目前他尚未准备好组建自己的“国民政府”。他解释说，他目前无法回答有关中国海关收入、货币及其他财政事务的询问，他说，这些事项必须在其“政府”成立之后才能处理。

在谈及侵华日军撤离的问题时，汪先生对记者表示，只要中国政府“仍在高喊抵抗，显然就无法实现全面撤军”。他说，当“和平重建”且中国政府被推翻后，“任何公开拥护和平与反共政策的中国军队”都将保持完整，以接管撤军后的地区。

汪先生宣称，所谓“第六次全国代表大会”的“外交政策”是与日本合作以维持东亚和平，并“与列强合作以促进世界和平事业”。

汪先生表示，他有信心其“政府”最终将获得列强的承认。他呼吁各国政府对其“真实目标”给予“同情的理解”。

茶话会持续了一个多小时。在此期间，记者们不被允许提出任何问题。

THE 6TH CONGRESS OF THE CENTRAL EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
OF THE KUOMINTANG

The first meeting of the 6th Congress of the
Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang was held in
Shanghai yesterday at which 59 members of the Central
Executive and Supervisory Committees of the Kuomintang were
present. The meeting was presided over by Wang Ching-wei
who made a detailed report on the international situation
and Kuomintang affairs and the political situation in China.
During the meeting Chow Vai-hai (周佛海) and
eight others were elected to the Standing Committee of the
Central Executive Committee, while Dr. Chu Min-yi was
appointed Secretary-General of the Central Kuomintang, with
Mei Sze-ping (梅思平) as Director of the Organization
Department, Tao Hsi-sung (陶希聖) as Director of the
Publicity Department and Ting Mu-tsung (丁默村) as
Director of the Social Affairs Department.

Chu Min-yi's Telegram to Chungking

Dr. Chu Min-yi has, as Secretary-General of
the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, sent a
telegram to the Kuomintang members at Chungking, urging
them to effect an immediate conclusion of the hostilities,
because the conditions prevailing both within and without
this country are not favourable to war.
Two years ago, the telegram says, we were in
a position to avoid war, but now conditions have changed
and if peace can do no harm to our national existence and
independence and if the continuation of the war of
resistance will only lead the country to ruin, then why
should we not seek for peace.
It is in the interests of the nation and the
people that comrade Wang Ching-wei is suggesting peace to
Chungking, yet he is being accused of conspiring with the
enemy. Now if a person who advocates peace is a traitor,
then comrade Chiang Kai-shek is a traitor for he has on many
occasions carried out peace negotiations. Prior to Wang
Ching-wei's departure from Chungking, I had on many
occasions, in company with representatives of comrade H.H.
Kung in Shanghai, opened negotiations with the other party
for the conclusion of hostilities and withdrawal of armed
forces, because I consider that the sooner peace is realised,
the earlier will the people be delivered from their misery

中国国民党中央执行委员会第六次全体会议

中国国民党中央执行委员会第六次全体会议昨日在上海举行，国民党中执委及中监委委员共59人出席。会议由汪精卫主持，他就国际形势、国民党党务以及中国政治局势作了详细报告。会议期间，周佛海等九人当选为中央执行委员会常务委员会委员，朱民谊博士被任命为中国国民党中央秘书长，梅思平任组织部部长，陶希圣任宣传部部长，丁默村任社会部部长。

朱民谊致重庆电文

朱民谊博士以中国国民党中央执行委员会秘书长的身份，向在重庆的国民党成员发出电报，敦促他们立即实现停战，因为当前国内外的局势均不利于战争。
电文称，两年前我们本可避免战争，但如今形势已变；如果和平不会损害我们的国家生存与独立，而继续抗战只会导致国家毁灭，那么我们为何不寻求和平呢？
汪精卫同志向重庆提出和平建议，是出于国家和人民的利益，然而他却遭到与敌人勾结的指控。倘若主张和平者即为汉奸，那么蒋介石同志也是汉奸，因为他曾多次进行和平谈判。在汪精卫离开重庆之前，我曾多次偕同孔祥熙同志在上海的代表，与对方开启谈判，以求实现停战及撤军，因为我认为和平越早实现，人民就能越早从苦难中得到解脱

and sufferings. I never realized that I would be

Meeting of "Sixth Congress of the Chinese Kuomintang"
in Shanghai

According to reliable information from foreign
sources, a meeting, known as the Sixth Congress of the Chinese
Kuomintang, was held at the residence of Wang Ching-wei
