It is learned from Japanese sources that
Wang Ching-wei has incurred the displeasure of General
Ando on account of his broadcast in Kwangtung on
August 9. The following day, General Ando gravely
reproached Wang Ching-wei who pitifully asked his pardon.
According to the Osaka Mainichi of August 11,
in the course of a broadcast over a certain radio station,
Wang Ching-wei clearly stated that Japan would first
withdraw her forces from Kwangtung. In General Ando's
opinion, Wang Ching-wei had exceeded his promise to the
Japanese, for Japan has no intention to withdraw her
forces.
Thus has Wang Ching-wei's propaganda that
Japan is willing to withdraw her troops been refuted by
his master. It is only right that he should be severely
reproached

Telegram to Wang Ching-Wei on Peace Movement

The "Central China Daily News" publishes the
following telegram from the Peace Movement Acceleration
Association to Wang Ching-wei :-
"Our country is unfortunately involved in a
war. The war of resistance has lasted two years and vast
tracts of territory have been lost and a large number of
people have been killed. China will be ruined if this
continues.
"You are now promoting peace and your movement
is being heartily supported by the people throughout the
country. However, the men responsible for the war of
resistance are still stubborn and the red bandits are
becoming more ferocious. Unless they are immediately
eliminated, people in the south-west and the north-west
of China will suffer more heavily.
"We request you to continue the work of peace
as desired by the general public. A conference of
representatives of the people should be called to form
a supreme Kuomintang organ to exercise its authority.
Chiang Kai-shek, who is bringing misfortune to the people
and endangering the existence of the country and the
Party, should be immediately deprived of all his posts.
Those Kuomintang members against whom there is evidence
that they are conspiring with red bandits must be expelled.
A new central regime should be formed and economic
reconstruction should be commenced with our friendly
nation, Japan.
"The members of this Association who number
several thousand swear to follow you."

《中美日报》（香港电）：-

汪精卫招致安藤将军不满

据日方消息，汪精卫因8月9日在广东的广播讲话而招致安藤将军的不满。次日，安藤将军严厉斥责汪精卫，汪精卫可怜地请求原谅。据8月11日《大阪每日新闻》报道，汪精卫在某电台广播中明确表示，日本将首先从广东撤军。在安藤将军看来，汪精卫超出了对日方的承诺，因为日本无意撤军。
因此，汪精卫关于日本愿意撤军的宣传已被其主子驳斥。他受到严厉斥责是理所应当的。

致汪精卫关于和平运动的电报

《华中日报》刊登了和平运动促进会发给汪精卫的以下电报：-
“我国不幸卷入战争。抗战已持续两年，大片国土沦丧，大量民众伤亡。若此状况持续，中国必将毁灭。
“阁下目前倡导和平，此举深得全国民众衷心支持。然而，负责抗战之人仍然顽固，赤匪日益猖獗。若不立即将其铲除，中国西南和西北地区的民众将遭受更沉重的苦难。
“我们恳请阁下顺应公众意愿，继续推进和平工作。应召开人民代表会议，组建最高国民党机构以行使职权。蒋介石给民众带来灾难，危及国家与党的生存，应立即剥夺其一切职务。凡有证据表明与赤匪勾结的国民党成员，必须予以开除。应组建新的中央政权，并与友好邻邦日本开始经济重建。
“本会数千名成员誓愿追随阁下。”

CHINA PRESS.
AUG 22 1939

〔右上角手写及印章内容：23870 / 8986 / 22 8 39〕

Wang Returns
Here From
Canton Visit

Wang Ching-wei, the deposed Kuomintang leader, returned to Shanghai yesterday from the south, THE CHINA PRESS learned last night from reliable sources.

While Wang's place of residence here was not known yesterday, it was believed that he would live in his heavily fortified headquarters on Yu Yuen Road, in immediate proximity to the Japanese-controlled Hollywood gambling resort.

On Sunday, the pill-boxes atop the tall walls were manned by Chinese sentries. A number of Japanese soldiers were also seen entering the well-guarded estate. Other activity noted in the house was the presence of half a dozen well-dressed Chinese girls.

During the past week, the house adjoining the Wang headquarters on the east has also been fortified. A three-foot addition was made to the brick wall, while barbed wire was strung around the lot.

During his visit in Canton, Wang met Lieut.-Gen. Ando, Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese forces in South China, and made an attempt to win over leading Kwangtung officials. While his conference with Gen. Ando was hailed by Japanese papers as a "success," his efforts to woo Chinese leaders were reported to have ended in dismal failure.

Gen. Chang Fa-kwei, former associate of Wang, denounced the latter as "China's Franco or Henlein" and as a "mouthpiece of the Japanese Army."

Wang's so-called "peace broadcast," widely advertised over Japanese-operated stations in Canton, was reported to have been inaudible in Hongkong.

〔右下角手写签名：似为 "Lile" 及日期 "8/22"〕

1939年8月22日

汪精卫
自广州
访问归来

据《字林西报》昨晚从可靠消息来源获悉，被罢黜的国民党领袖汪精卫昨日已从南方返回上海。

虽然汪精卫在沪的寓所位置昨日尚不为人知，但据信他将居住在其位于愚园路、紧邻日军控制的好莱坞赌博游乐场的戒备森严的总部内。

周日，高墙顶部的碉堡由中方哨兵把守。也有人看到数名日本士兵进入这座守卫严密的宅邸。在该宅邸内观察到的其他活动是，有半打衣着考究的中国女孩在场。

在过去的一周里，汪精卫总部东侧相邻的房屋也进行了加固。砖墙加高了三尺，场地周围拉起了铁丝网。

在广州访问期间，汪精卫会见了日本华南派遣军司令官安藤利吉中将，并试图拉拢广东主要官员。虽然日本报纸将汪与安藤将军的会谈称为“成功”，但据报道，他拉拢中国领导人的努力以惨败告终。

汪精卫的前同僚张发奎将军谴责后者为“中国的贝当或亨莱因”，并称其为“日本军队的传声筒”。

汪精卫所谓的“和平广播”在广州由日本人经营的电台上广为宣传，但据报道在香港无法收听。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
AUG 22 1939

Kwangtung Generals Attack
Mr. Wang Ching-wei

Joint Telegram Denounces The Statesman For His
Peace Proposals And Expresses Belief In
Ultimate Victory Of Chiang Kai-shek

SHUCHOW, Aug. 20.—Leading
Chinese commanders in Kwangtung
have issued a joint circular tele-
gram to the people of this province,
sharply denouncing Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, expelled Deputy Gen-
eral Executive of the Kuomintang,
for his so-called "peace proposals."
The message is signed by Gen-
eral Chang Fa-kwei, Commander-
in-Chief of the Government forces
in the 4th (Kwangtung-Kwangsi)
War Zone, General Yu Han-mou,
Pacification Commissioner for
Kwangtung and concurrently Vice-
Commander-in-Chief of the Gov-
ernment Forces in the 4th War
War Zone, General Yu Han-mou,
Chairman of Kwangtung Provincial
Government.
"Concerted Struggle"
The telegram begins by pointing
out that the campaign of resistance
represents the concerted struggle
of the entire Chinese people against
the Japanese invasion, and that its
purpose is to preserve Chinese
national independence and freedom.
"The campaign of resistance is
not the business of any one party,
clique or individual," the message
adds.
Citing numerous instances of
alleged "insincerity" from the
political career of Mr. Wang Ching-
wei, the message denounces him as
a "political gambler" and charges
him with secretly plotting to "sell"
the country to Japan.
Under the pretext of concluding
a so-called "honourable peace" with
the Japanese, the message adds, he
is seeking to bring about the ex-
tinction of the country so as to
satisfy his personal ambitions.
The message then urges the peo-
ple of Kwangtung unanimously to
oppose Mr. Wang's so-called "peace
proposals" and continue to repose
confidence in the Three People's
Principles.
These Principles, the message
states, are the only means of sav-
ing the country and regenerating
the nation.
Tribute To Chiang
Paying tribute to the able leader-
ship of General Chiang Kai-shek,
President of the Military Affairs
Commission and General Executive
of the Kuomintang, the message
states that the ultimate victory for
China is now only a matter of time.
"Those who have money should
contribute their wealth, and those
who have strength should contribute
their energy, to the State for the
attainment of the common objec-
tive. The people in the rear should
especially redouble their efforts in
increasing production so as to aug-
ment the country's power of resist-
ance. Only when the ultimate vic-
tory is won can real peace be
realised," the message says in con-
clusion.—U.P.

1939年8月22日

广东将领抨击
汪精卫先生

联名通电谴责该政治人物的
和平提议，并表示相信
蒋介石的最终胜利

徐州，8月20日电。—广东地区的中国高级指挥官向本省民众发布了一份联合循环通电，严厉谴责被开除的国民党副总裁汪精卫先生及其所谓的“和平提议”。该电文由第四战区（粤桂）政府军总司令张发奎将军、广东省绥靖主任兼第四战区政府军副总司令余汉谋将军、以及广东省政府主席余汉谋将军署名。
“ concerted struggle ”（协同斗争）
通电首先指出，抗战代表了全体中国人民对抗日本侵略的协同斗争，其目的是维护中国的民族独立和自由。“抗战并非任何一党、一派或个人的私事，”电文补充道。
电文列举了汪精卫先生政治生涯中诸多所谓“不真诚”的事例，谴责他为“政治赌徒”，并指控他秘密策划将国家“出卖”给日本。电文补充说，他以与日本达成所谓“光荣和平”为借口，实则寻求导致国家灭亡，以满足其个人野心。
随后，电文敦促广东人民一致反对汪先生所谓的“和平提议”，并继续信奉三民主义。
电文称，三民主义是救国复兴的唯一途径。
致敬蒋介石
电文向军事委员会委员长兼国民党总裁蒋介石将军的卓越领导致以敬意，并表示中国的最终胜利现在只是时间问题。
“有钱者出钱，有力者出力，为国家实现共同目标。后方民众尤其应加倍努力增加生产，以增强国家的抵抗力。只有赢得最终胜利，才能实现真正的和平，”电文在结尾处说道。—合众社

Wang Ching-wei Makes New S. H.
Appeal for Peace Date ____
Uselessness of Resistance Pointed Out in
Broadcast From Occupied Canton.

IN a broadcast from Canton, in Japanese-occupied territory, Mr.
Wang Ching-wei, dismissed official of the Kuomintang, yes-
terday repeated his appeal for peace between China and Japan,
and for an end to the destruction of property and human lives
caused in the present hostilities. This destruction he put down to
the Chinese policy of leaving nothing to Japanese conquerors,
which policy he condemned as being the brain-child of the Gen-
Chiang Kai-shek regime and the Communists.
Apologizing for having to speak from a Japanese-occupied
area, Mr. Wang Ching-wei took credit to himself for having made
his two former broadcasts from districts not under Japanese con-
trol. The trend of his remarks was to the effect that his present
broadcast was made from Japanese territory because he had no
other choice but to seek the pacification of his country in such
associations, since the Chungking government had called him a
traitor. No one could live as a human being in any other territory,
he maintained. Since he was speaking from Kwangtung, he took
conditions in that province as his guide.

"Now what are the conditions in
Kwangtung? Last October, the peo-
ple were told by the Chinese au-
thorities, for their peace of mind,
that there was positively no pos-
sibility of Japanese forces coming to
this region. Even at the beginning
of October they were told so.
"When the time at last came for
Japanese forces to surge on Canton,
the Chinese authorities were the first
to flee, accompanied by their troops,
leaving the people to their own de-
vices. Moreover, when the troops
fled they set fire to the people's
houses and shops, destroying them.

Guerillas Criticised

"Indeed the pain and distress suf-
fered by the people of Canton, both
at the front and in the rear, were
quite beyond description. And as for
those who are still living and have
their houses unburned, the Chinese
authorities seem to ask them why
they did not die and why their houses
were not burned. Bandits are being
instigated to resort to incendiarism
and plundering under the name of
guerillas.
"So great are the sufferings of the
people of Kwangtung in the occupied
areas. Then the question arises as
to why the Chinese authorities are
taking such a course of action. The
answer is that Gen. Chiang Kai-shek
orders them to do so. Why is Gen.
Chiang Kai-shek doing that? Because
he is upholding the tenets of the
Communist Party.
"What compensation, then, is there
for all these sacrifices? Even if
entire cities are burnt, that does not
prevent Japanese forces from enter-
ing them. After they are burnt, there
is nothing to stop the Japanese forces
from garrisoning them.
"What has been gained by such in-
cendiarism, which has killed people
and destroyed the property upon
which they depended for their live-
lihood?
"The Chinese authorities did not
stop at burning the city of Canton;
they even ordered the destruction of
the triple cities of Wuhan. Because
those who received such orders could
not bear the thought, the cities were
saved from that fate. As if to make
up for their failure to burn the triple
cities of Wuhan, the Chinese authori-
ties laid waste Changsha, which was
not to be evacuated. It is to be ex-
pected that Chengtu and Chungking
will share the same fate."

（批：Liu A 98 C）

汪精卫在上海发出新的和平呼吁 日期 ____
在被占领的广州发表的广播中指出抵抗的无用性。

昨日，被国民党免职的官员汪精卫先生从日军占领下的广州发表广播讲话，再次呼吁中日之间实现和平，并结束当前敌对行动造成的财产和生命损失。他将这种破坏归咎于中国当局实行的“不给日本征服者留下任何东西”的政策，并谴责该政策是蒋介石将军政权和共产党的产物。
汪精卫先生为不得不从日军占领区发表讲话表示歉意，并自夸他之前的两次广播是从非日军控制的地区发出的。他的言论大意是，由于重庆政府称他为叛徒，他别无选择，只能在此类关联中寻求国家的平定，因此本次广播是从日本领土发出的。他声称，在其他任何领土上都无法像人一样生活。既然他是从广东发表讲话，他便以该省的情况作为依据。

“那么广东的情况如何呢？去年十月，中国当局为了安抚民心，告诉民众日军绝对不可能来到该地区。甚至在十月初，他们还是这样说的。
“当日军最终涌向广州时，中国当局及其军队率先逃跑，将民众弃之不顾。此外，军队在逃跑时放火烧毁了民众的房屋和商店，将其摧毁。

批评游击队

“的确，广州民众在前线和后方所遭受的痛苦和苦难简直无法形容。至于那些仍然活着且房屋未被烧毁的人，中国当局似乎要质问他们为什么没有死去，为什么他们的房屋没有被烧毁。匪徒正以游击队的名义被煽动进行纵火和抢劫。
“广东民众在被占领区所受的苦难如此深重。于是问题出现了，中国当局为何采取这样的行动方针？答案是蒋介石将军命令他们这样做。蒋介石将军为何要这样做？因为他正在维护共产党的信条。
“那么，所有这些牺牲有什么补偿呢？即使整个城市被烧毁，也无法阻止日军进入。城市被烧毁后，没有任何东西能阻止日军驻守其中。
“这种既杀人又摧毁民众赖以生存的财产的纵火行为，究竟得到了什么？
“中国当局并未止步于烧毁广州城；他们甚至下令摧毁武汉三镇。因为接受命令的人不忍心这样做，这些城市才幸免于难。仿佛是为了弥补未能烧毁武汉三镇的过失，中国当局洗劫了本不打算撤离的长沙。可以预料，成都和重庆也将遭遇同样的命运。”

（批：Liu A 98 C）

pages.en:
23103

Safety-dwellers Ask Question

“Why should the people of China hasten along the path to destruction? Those at the front and in the rear are unable to give vent to their complaint because they are muzzled, but those in the occupied areas are loudly asking that question.
“It is this voice of the people that has drawn me to the occupied areas. I felt it was my duty to serve as a connection between this cry and that which could not make itself heard in the rear and at the front.
“The second point I wish to raise is why should I have lost my freedom in Japanese-occupied areas? It goes without saying that Japan has done nothing to curtail my freedom. Even if I should die, I shall not lose my freedom. I am always prepared to offer my life for those of my countrymen and my freedom for theirs.
“How then can peace be achieved? It seems complicated but really it is very simple. If Gen. Chiang Kai-shek thinks more of the State than of himself, if he should follow the great Asiatic principles bequeathed by the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, and if he should accept the Japanese proposals for peace, a cessation of the hostilities will be brought about.
“In subsequent negotiations for peace, the question of the withdrawal of Japanese troops, for which the people throughout the country aspire, will be solved by negotiations of concrete problems upon the basis of the principles of good neighbourliness, joint anti-Communism and economic co-operation. Is this not extremely simple?

Gen. Chiang’s Own Interests

“Gen. Chiang Kai-shek, however, is paying more attention to the protection of his own interests than to that of the interests of the State and of the people. Rather he is sacrificing the interests of the State and of the people to the Communist Party, a creature of the Comintern, to pay a personal debt he incurred when his life was saved at the time of the Sian Incident.
“Therefore in spite of wishes for peace and in spite that such a peace would not prejudice the independence and the freedom of the state, Gen. Chiang Kai-shek still stubbornly and unreasonably continues to obstruct the realization of such a peace.
“There is a simple way to remove this great obstacle. Convinced that there is hope for peace that does not run counter to the independence or the freedom of the state, civil and military authorities, both at the front and in the rear, should crush the fraudulent propaganda of Gen. Chiang Kai-shek and rid themselves of his oppression.”
Mr. Wang Ching-wei supported this statement from his personal knowledge that the Japanese army would not attack any people anxious for peace and opposed to the Comintern. This, however, was being thwarted by Gen. Chiang Kai-shek. The solution of China’s problems which he offered was, therefore, that the people should overthrow the resistance of Gen. Chiang Kai-shek and so win through to the freedom offered by Sino-Japanese co-operation in the New Order in East Asia.
pages.zh:
23103

安全区居民提出问题

“中国人民为何要加速走向毁灭之路？前方和后方的民众因被钳制而无法发泄不满，但沦陷区的民众却在大声提出这一问题。
“正是这种民众的声音将我吸引到了沦陷区。我觉得我有责任充当这一呼声与后方及前方那些无法发出声音的呼声之间的纽带。
“我要提出的第二点是，为何我在日占区失去了自由？不言而喻，日本并未采取任何措施限制我的自由。即使我死去，我也不会失去自由。我随时准备为我的同胞献出生命，为他们的自由献出我的自由。
“那么，如何实现和平呢？这看似复杂，实则非常简单。如果蒋介石将军多考虑国家利益而非个人利益，如果他遵循已故孙中山博士遗留下的伟大亚洲原则，如果他接受日本的和平提议，敌对行动就会停止。
“在随后的和平谈判中，全国民众所渴望的日军撤军问题，将在睦邻友好、共同反共和经济合作原则的基础上，通过具体问题的谈判得到解决。这难道不是极其简单吗？

蒋介石的个人利益

“然而，蒋介石将军更关注保护其个人利益，而非国家和人民的利益。他反而为了偿还西安事变中获救时所欠下的个人债务，将国家和人民的利益牺牲给共产国际的傀儡——共产党。
“因此，尽管人们渴望和平，且此种和平不会损害国家的独立和自由，蒋介石将军仍顽固且无理地继续阻碍此种和平的实现。
“有一个简单的方法可以消除这一巨大障碍。既然确信存在一种不违背国家独立或自由的和平希望，前方和后方的文武官员应当粉碎蒋介石将军的欺诈性宣传，摆脱他的压迫。”
汪精卫先生以其亲身所知支持这一说法，即日军不会攻击任何渴望和平并反对共产国际的人。然而，这一点正受到蒋介石将军的阻挠。因此，他提出的解决中国问题的方案是，民众应当推翻蒋介石将军的抵抗，从而赢得通过东亚新秩序下的中日合作所提供的自由。

SHANGHAI TIMES,

AUG 10 1939

WANG CHING-WEI'S
LATEST MOVE

Reported Organizing
"National Party
Congress"

CHUNGKING, Aug. 9. — Mr.
Wang Ching-wei, deposed Deputy
Executive of the Kuomintang, is
organizing a so-called national
party congress for the formation of
the highest central party offices,
thereby paving the way for the

Recognition Of Nanking
Government Accorded By
Berlin And Rome Regimes

Exchange Of Ambassadors Is Likely To Take Place
Marquis Taliani Expected
To Present Credentials To Mr. Wang

HARD BLOW TO CHUNGKING GOVERNMENT
SEEN IN LATEST DIPLOMATIC MOVE

(Reuter)
LONDON, July 1.—The German Government announced today that it recognizes the Nanking Government and that it will shortly enter into diplomatic relations with it, according to the official German news agency. The Italian Government has made a similar announcement.

(Domei)
NANKING, July 1.—Germany and Italy today formally accorded de jure recognition to the National Government of China at Nanking. Colonel Joachim von Ribbentrop, Reichs Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Count Galeazzo Ciano, Italian Foreign Minister, today formally notified the Foreign Minister, Mr. Hsu Liang, of the National Government of the steps taken by their respective Governments.

Acting on instructions from his home Government, Herr M. Gipperich, First Secretary of the German Embassy at Nanking, called on Mr. Hsu Liang at 6.10 o'clock this afternoon to notify the latter that Germany has recognized the Nanking Government.

Also, Marquis Francesco Maria Taliani de Marchio, Italian Ambassador to China, flew to Nanking from Shanghai, to inform the Foreign Minister of Italy's recognition of the National Government.

Immediately after notifying the Foreign Minister, Herr Gipperich accompanied the former to President Wang Ching-wei's official residence at 5.30 o'clock, making known to the Nanking leader the messages sent by Chancellor Adolf Hitler and Foreign Minister von Ribbentrop. The German official also conveyed the German Government's felicitations regarding the recognition.

The Italian Ambassador was met at the Nanking airfield by Mr. Hsu Liang, and the two then motored to Mr. Wang's residence, where the President was handed personal messages from Premier Mussolini and the Italian Foreign Minister, Count Ciano.

Exchange Of Envoys

With mutual diplomatic recognition completed, it was expected that an exchange of Ambassadors will take place in the nearest future, thus bringing about the resumption of normal diplomatic relations between China, and Germany and Italy.

While no definite announcement has been made by either Berlin or Rome regarding the envoy likely to be accredited to Nanking, quarters close to the Nanking Foreign Ministry expected that the Marquis Francesco Maria Taliani de Marchio, Italian Ambassador, now staying in Shanghai, will present his credentials to President Wang Ching-wei in the near future.

Ambassador Marquis Taliani, it was recalled, has not yet presented his credentials to Mr. Lin Sen of the Chungking regime. The German envoy, it was expected, will be either Dr. F. Altenburg, or Mr. W. Stahmer, who recently returned from Japan.

Should France accord diplomatic recognition to Nanking, it was believed that the thousands of Chinese in French Indo-China will come to support the National Government.

Support of the Nanking Administration by these Chinese, it was pointed out, would cause a stoppage of large remittances to the Chungking regime causing a further weakening of the financial structure of the Chiang Kai-shek administration.

The National Government, authoritative sources here stressed, will continue in the future the closest co-operation with Japan for the establishment of a New Order in East Asia. All pressure possible will be exerted on the Chungking regime to effect the realization of peace in East Asia.

The "New Order"
(Domei)
TOKYO, July 1—Recognition of the National Government of China at Nanking by the Governments of Italy, Germany, Rumania, Slovakia, and Croatia, "is a telling blow to those who do not yet East Asia," Dr. Nobufumi Ito, President of the Information Board, declared in a statement issued at 6 o'clock this evening.

Dr. Ito's statement said that "It is a source of profound gratification on the part of the Japanese Government that the Governments of Germany, Italy, Rumania, Slovakia and Croatia have accorded recognition to the National Government of the Republic of China.

"Since its establishment on March 30, last year, the new National Government has steadily grown in strength. By the Basic Treaty concluded between Japan and China on November 30, last year, Japan took the initiative in recognizing the Government, which has been exerting itself to attain the objective of co-existence, co-prosperity, and reconstruction of East Asia."

"The fact that the leading European Powers—Germany, Italy, Rumania, Slovakia and Croatia—have now recognized the National Government is a clear indication that the new order in East Asia is being established on a firm basis."

"Any manifestation of such recognition, in whatever form or manner, would be a violation of international law treaties and would be considered as an act most unfriendly to the Chinese nation, for the consequences of which the recognising party would have to bear full responsibility."

Another manifesto issued on March 10, 1940, by the National Peoples' Political Council, declared: "If any government should support Japan against China, or recognise the puppet regime under Mr. Wang Ching-wei, we will regard such countries as enemies of China."

Wang Makes Statement
(Domei)
NANKING, July 1.—President Wang Ching-wei, in a statement tonight regarding the German and Italian recognition of the Nanking Government, declared the National Government's aims to contribute to world peace have taken a first step toward fulfilment.

At the time of the return to Nanking of the National Government, announcement was made of its basic domestic and foreign policies, one of the most important items being respect for the interests of all friendly countries, Mr. Wang said.

To this end the National Government during the past year has made repeated efforts to carry out its enunciated aims.

"At these times, co-operation among the Powers concerned, and mutual assistance, in surmounting difficulties, is the only way toward realizing ultimate world peace.

"The National Government is determined to continue all efforts to carry out its fixed policies, and will endeavour to enunciate clearly to the world its aims and intentions.

"With Germany and Italy having recognized the National Government, relations between these two countries and China have entered a new phase. The wishes of the National Government to contribute to world peace have now taken a step toward fulfilment," Mr. Wang declared.

柏林与罗马政权承认南京政府

互派大使之举料将实现
塔利亚尼侯爵预计将向汪先生递交国书

最新外交举动被视为对重庆政府的沉重打击

（路透社）
伦敦，7月1日电——据德国官方通讯社报道，德国政府今日宣布承认南京政府，并将于不久后与其建立外交关系。意大利政府亦发表了类似声明。

（同盟社）
南京，7月1日电——德国和意大利今日正式给予位于南京的中华民国国民政府法律上的承认。德国外交部长约阿希姆·冯·里宾特洛甫上校和意大利外交部长加莱亚佐·齐亚诺伯爵，今日正式通知国民政府外交部长徐良先生各自政府所采取的步骤。

德国驻南京大使馆一等秘书吉佩里希先生奉其本国政府指示，于今日下午6时10分拜访徐良先生，通知后者德国已承认南京政府。

此外，意大利驻华大使弗朗切斯科·玛丽亚·塔利亚尼·迪·马尔基奥侯爵从上海飞抵南京，向外交部长通报意大利对国民政府的承认。

在通知外交部长后，吉佩里希先生随即于5时30分陪同前者前往汪精卫主席的官邸，向这位南京领导人转达了阿道夫·希特勒总理和外交部长冯·里宾特洛甫发来的讯息。这位德国官员还传达了德国政府就承认一事所致的贺意。

徐良先生在南京机场迎接了意大利大使，随后两人乘车前往汪先生寓所，汪主席在那里收到了墨索里尼总理和意大利外交部长齐亚诺伯爵的个人信函。

互换使节

随着相互外交承认的完成，预计在不远的将来将互换大使，从而恢复中国与德国及意大利之间的正常外交关系。

虽然柏林或罗马方面均未就可能派驻南京的使节作出确切公告，但接近南京外交部的人士预计，目前滞留上海的意大利大使弗朗切斯科·玛丽亚·塔利亚尼·迪·马尔基奥侯爵将在不久的将来向汪精卫主席递交国书。

回顾过往，塔利亚尼大使尚未向重庆政权的林森先生递交国书。预计德国使节将是F·阿尔滕堡博士，或是近期从日本返回的W·斯塔默尔先生。

人们认为，如果法国给予南京外交承认，法属印度支那的数千名华人将会转而支持国民政府。

指出这些华人对南京行政当局的支持，将导致汇往重庆政权的大额汇款中断，从而进一步削弱蒋介石行政当局的财政结构。

此间权威人士强调，国民政府今后将继续与日本保持最密切的合作，以建立东亚新秩序。将对重庆政权施加一切可能的压力，以实现东亚和平。

“新秩序”
（同盟社）
东京，7月1日电——情报局总裁伊藤述史博士在今晚6时发表的声明中宣称，意大利、德国、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚政府承认位于南京的中华民国国民政府，“是对那些尚未……东亚的人的有力打击”。

伊藤博士的声明称：“德国、意大利、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚政府承认中华民国国民政府，令日本政府深感欣慰。

“自去年3月30日成立以来，新的国民政府实力稳步增长。通过去年11月30日中日缔结的基本条约，日本率先承认了该政府，该政府一直致力于实现东亚共存、共荣及重建的目标。”

“主要欧洲强国——德国、意大利、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚——如今承认国民政府这一事实，清楚地表明东亚新秩序正在稳固的基础上建立起来。”

承认日本在中国的傀儡组织。

“任何形式的此类承认表现，均将被视为违反国际法条约，并被视为对中华民族极不友好的行为，承认方须为此后果承担全部责任。”

国民参政会于1940年3月10日发布的另一份宣言宣称：“若有政府支持日本对抗中国，或承认汪精卫先生领导下的傀儡政权，我们将视此类国家为中国的敌人。”

汪发表声明
（同盟社）
南京，7月1日电——汪精卫主席今晚就德国和意大利承认南京政府发表声明，宣称国民政府为世界和平作贡献的目标已迈出实现的第一步。

汪先生称，在国民政府还都南京之际，曾宣布其基本的内外政策，其中最重要的一项便是尊重所有友好国家的利益。

为此，国民政府在过去一年中多次努力践行其既定目标。

“在此时刻，有关列强之间的合作以及克服困难时的互助，是实现最终世界和平的唯一途径。

“国民政府决心继续努力执行其既定政策，并将努力向世界阐明其目标和意图。

“随着德国和意大利承认国民政府，这两国与中国的关系已进入一个新阶段。国民政府为世界和平作贡献的愿望现已迈出实现的一步，”汪先生宣称。

It was pointed out that the Chiang
Kai-shek regime is now nothing

The Nanking Government, observers
said, is rapidly pushing itself for-
ward into the front ranks of the
world Powers.
With the Nanking Government
finding itself in a greatly strengthen-
ed position, not only in China, but
in the world, it was predicted here
that the Chungking regime would
lose all semblance of a sovereign
administration and be hopelessly
tied to Great Britain and the United
States.
Moreover, it was expected that
with the formal recognition accord-
ed by Germany and Italy, other
nations would closely follow in their
footsteps. The 300,000 Chinese now
residing in Europe, it was pre-
dicted here, will rally around the
Nanking Administration.

TOKYO, July 1.—Germany,
Italy, Rumania, Slovakia and
Croatia have officially recognized
Mr. Wang Ching-wei's Nanking
Government, the Cabinet Informa-
tion Board announced today.
The Information Board an-
nouncement stated that Japan was
profoundly grateful for the recogni-
tion of the "National Government
of China" by the Axis States.
The recognition, added the
announcement, was a "telling blow
to those who, having failed to
realise the great ideal of the
establishment of East Asia's New
Order, still continue the folly of
resistance against Japan."

**How Chungking Regards It**
(Reuter)
CHUNGKING, July 1.—German
and Italian recognition of the Nan-
king Government is likely to result
in China breaking off diplomatic
relations with Berlin and Rome and
in spreading of the war to the Far
East, according to Chinese circles
here.
These quarters are not surprised
at the development and express the
opinion that it may, after all, be
favourable to Chungking as it would
formally bring the Chungking Gov-
ernment into the same camp with
the United States, Great Britain and
Soviet Russia and would also make
it unnecessary for Chungking to
maintain half-hearted relations, as
hitherto existing, with Berlin and
Rome.
The development is arousing
speculation whether the Axis step
is one of the conditions for Japan's
entry into the war against Russia.
Therefore, Chinese circles are anxi-
ously awaiting Japan's next move
which may further clarify the inter-
national situation and Chungking's
position in the present war.
Germany never replaced Dr. Oscar
Trautmann, the German Ambassador,
after his recall in 1939, while the
Italian Ambassador remained in
Shanghai and never visited Chung-
king.
It is recalled here that the Chinese
Government delivered identical
notes on March 30, 1940, to the three
powers, stating: "The Chinese Gov-
ernment is convinced that the three
respecting states will not take any
step which might prejudice the exist-
ing cordial relations..."

**对重庆的打击**
有人着重指出，柏林和罗马对南京的正式承认将对重庆造成沉重打击，尤其是因为此举紧随汪精卫主席具有历史意义的访日之行，以及日本向南京政府慷慨提供总额达3亿日元的信贷之后。
此间的观察家宣称，德国和意大利对南京政府的完全外交承认，明确预示中国将加入三国同盟。
有人补充说，法理上的承认也意味着对已摇摇欲坠的重庆政权的致命一击。有人指出，蒋介石政权如今不过是一个权力不断缩小的地方小政府。
观察家称，南京政府正迅速跻身世界强国之列。
鉴于南京政府在中国乃至世界的地位大大增强，此处预测重庆政权将失去主权政府的所有表象，并无可救药地依附于英国和美国。
此外，人们预计，随着德国和意大利给予正式承认，其他国家也将紧随其后。此处预测，目前旅居欧洲的30万中国人将团结在南京政府周围。

东京，7月1日电——内阁情报局今日宣布，德国、意大利、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚已正式承认汪精卫先生的南京政府。
情报局的声明称，日本对轴心国各国承认“中华民国国民政府”深表感激。
声明补充说，这一承认是对那些未能认识到建立东亚新秩序的伟大理想、仍继续从事抗日蠢行的人的“有力打击”。

**重庆方面如何看待此事**
（路透社）
重庆，7月1日电——据此地中国方面人士称，德国和意大利承认南京政府可能导致中国与柏林和罗马断绝外交关系，并将战争蔓延至远东。
这些人士对事态发展并不感到意外，并表示认为这最终可能对重庆有利，因为它将使重庆政府在形式上与美国、英国和苏联处于同一阵营，同时也使重庆无需再维持迄今为止与柏林和罗马那种半心半意的关系。
这一事态发展引发了人们的猜测：轴心国的这一步骤是否为日本参加对俄战争的条件之一。因此，中国各界正焦急等待日本的下一步行动，这可能进一步澄清国际局势以及重庆在当前战争中的地位。
德国在1939年召回奥斯卡·特劳特曼博士（Dr. Oscar Trautmann）这位德国大使后，从未再派人接替，而意大利大使则留在上海，从未访问过重庆。
此处有人回顾，中国政府曾于1940年3月30日向这三个国家递交了内容相同的照会，声明：“中国政府深信，这三个尊重中国的国家不会采取任何可能损害现有友好关系的步骤……”

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
JUL 2 1941.

RECOGNITION OF NANKING

The announcement that Germany, Italy and Rumania have decided to recognize the Government at Nanking as from July 1 means that the Axis Powers have taken a step which Japan had every reason to expect would have been taken long before this. The device is an obvious one. The sudden attack by Germany upon Russia, the breaching of the Russo-German non-aggression pact in that manner, has aroused very considerable concern in Tokyo, and during the past week many conferences have been held by the Japanese Government to consider its policy in view of the great change which has been brought about by Hitler's treachery. There can be little doubt that great anxiety has been caused in Japan by this latest development, and no small amount of question as to the sincerity of Hitler with regard to his relationships with the Japanese Government. This belated recognition coming as it does at such a moment, is clearly designed to allay Japanese anxieties, and it is but another piece of trickery.

It is not to be assumed that Hitler is animated by any greater degree of sincerity towards Tokyo than he has been with regard to other countries. To believe that he would honour his commitments to Japan is to believe something which every act of his since he came into power proves not to be true, and if there are any in Tokyo who fancy that this last-hour recognition can be accepted as evidence of German bona fides they will in the long run find themselves sadly disillusioned. The attitude of Germany and Italy towards the Sino-Japanese conflict has been equivocal throughout. When hostilities first broke out, German experts were assisting the armies on the National Government. Following Japanese representations these were eventually withdrawn, though the Germans maintained diplomatic relations with Chiang Kai-shek's Government. When there was a change in the Italian diplomatic representation at Chungking a new ambassador was appointed who since his arrival in this country has presented his credentials **〔此处转录不清〕**

There has been throughout the past four years an endeavour on the part of these two members of the Tri-Partite Pact to run with the hare and hunt with the hounds, chiefly because they were by no means sure of what would be the ultimate outcome of the struggle, and because they wished to avoid any step which might at some later stage create embarrassment. The conclusion to be drawn is that they delayed making any definite step until the last possible moment, and it is quite apparent that this declaration of the recognition of the Nanking Government, coming as it does at a time such as this, is no more than a sop offered to Japan, putting up a pretence of solidarity with her which the German invasion of Russia clearly shows does not and never can exist. It must be apparent that Japan plays a very secondary role in Hitler's eyes. If not why was Tokyo not informed of his intention to invade Russia? Why was an equal member of the Tri-Partite Pact so completely and so humiliatingly ignored?

The emptiness of the gesture is the clearest possible indication of the insincerity with which it has been made. Neither Germany nor Italy can lose anything by making it, for they have no interests capable of advancement in China because of their complete isolation from the Asiatic continent. They are making no sacrifice in Japan's favour because they have nothing to sacrifice. It is to be believed that the realists in Japan will accept that view. If recognition such as is now declared could have been worth anything at all it would most certainly been valuable if it had come earlier. This belated demonstration of a solidarity which has been so rudely shaken by the treachery of Hitler will it is hoped convince no one in Japan. The moderate elements are coming to understand that no reliance can be placed in Hitler or his policies. There is still much in the old saying Timeo Danaos et dona ferentes. The recognition of the Nanking Government is indeed a very small gift, a mere valueless trifle which should certainly not serve to satisfy those Japanese who have been brought to a full recognition of the inevitable results of both Germany and Italy.

《字林西报》。
1941年7月2日。

承认南京政府

德国、意大利和罗马尼亚决定自7月1日起承认南京政府，这一宣布意味着轴心国采取了一步日本完全有理由预期早已会采取的行动。这一手段显而易见。德国突然袭击俄国，以这种方式撕毁《苏德互不侵犯条约》，已在东京引起相当大的担忧；在过去的一周里，日本政府举行了多次会议，鉴于希特勒的背信弃义所带来的巨大变化，审议其政策。毫无疑问，这一最新事态发展在日本引起了极大的焦虑，并且人们对希特勒在与日本政府关系上的诚意产生了不小的疑问。在此时刻姗姗来迟的承认，显然是为了缓解日本的焦虑，这不过是另一种欺骗伎俩。

不应认为希特勒对东京抱有比他对其他国家更大的诚意。相信他会履行对日本的承诺，就是相信一件被他掌权以来的每一个行动证明为不真实的事情；如果东京有任何人幻想可以将这最后一刻的承认视为德国诚意的证据，他们最终将感到痛苦的幻灭。德国和意大利在整个中日冲突期间的态度一直是模棱两可的。当敌对行动最初爆发时，德国专家正在协助国民政府的军队。在日本提出交涉后，这些专家最终被撤回，尽管德国仍与蒋介石政府保持外交关系。当意大利在重庆的外交代表机构发生变动时，任命了一位新大使，他自抵达本国以来已递交了国书**〔此处转录不清〕**

在过去四年中，作为三国同盟成员的这两个国家一直试图两面讨好，主要是因为它们对于斗争的最终结果毫无把握，并且希望避免任何可能在后期阶段造成尴尬的步骤。由此得出的结论是，它们将任何明确的步骤推迟到了最后一刻；而且很明显，此时发表承认南京政府的声明，不过是向日本提供的一点安抚，假装与其团结一致，而德国入侵俄国清楚地表明这种团结并不存在，也永远不可能存在。显然，在希特勒眼中，日本扮演着非常次要的角色。否则，为何不将其入侵俄国的意图通知东京？为何三国同盟中一个平等的成员被如此彻底且屈辱地忽视？

这一姿态的空洞性最清楚地表明了其作出时的不诚意。德国和意大利都不会因此遭受任何损失，因为它们由于与亚洲大陆完全隔绝，在中国没有任何可以推进的利益。它们并没有为了日本的利益做出牺牲，因为它们没有什么可牺牲的。相信日本的现实主义者会接受这一观点。如果像现在所宣布的这种承认有任何价值的话，它若早些时候出现肯定会有价值。希望这种在被希特勒的背信弃义粗暴动摇的团结之后姗姗来迟的表现，不会说服日本的任何人。温和派人士开始认识到，不能信赖希特勒或其政策。那句古谚“Timeo Danaos et dona ferentes”（我害怕带着礼物的希腊人）中仍有许多道理。承认南京政府确实是一份非常微小的礼物，仅仅是一件毫无价值的琐事，当然不足以让那些充分认识到德意两国必然结果的日本人感到满意。

Minister Perplexed
(United Press)
ROME, July 2.—Mr. Hsu Dau-lin,
Chinese Minister to Italy and
Charge d'Affairs in Rome, told the
United Press yesterday that it was
too soon to say what his plans

Chinese Press Indignant
(Reuter)
CHUNGKING, July 2.—The Chi-
nese press this morning unanimous-
ly expressed the greatest indigna-
tion over the German and Italian
recognition of the Nanking Govern-
ment under Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
The official "Central Daily News,"
in a leading article, describes the
action as an "insult to the Chinese
people."
The daily declares: "The Hitler
and Mussolini Governments have
always adopted an unfriendly
attitude towards China, pursuing a
pro-Japanese policy. Newspapers
and periodicals under their control
make malicious attacks on the Chi-
nese Government and people.
"The Chinese Government had
hitherto refrained from taking any
action, as the Chinese and German
peoples had a history of sincere
friendship and mutual assistance in
cultural and technical relations. We
were unwilling to sacrifice the
friendship of the Chinese and Ger-
man peoples because of the actions
of the Nazi regime.
"At the same time we hoped that
the German people would be able
to induce their government to
change their mistaken policy. This
hope, however, has now totally
gone with the German recognition
of the puppet regime. We are con-
fident, however, that this does not
represent the wishes of the Ger-
man people. But it is noteworthy
that Germany and Italy waited 14
months before extending recogni-
tion, showing that there
was a motive behind the move."

八国现已完全承认南京政府

重庆中国政府召回驻罗马和柏林公使；西班牙、保加利亚和匈牙利承认南京政府

美日关系无变化；东京方面评论

（同盟社）
南京，7月2日电——继德国、意大利、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚之后，保加利亚、西班牙和匈牙利也效仿其例，至此，已有八个欧洲国家承认位于南京的中华民国国民政府。

保加利亚、西班牙和匈牙利正式承认汪精卫政府为中华民国国民政府，这三国驻东京公使已通过中国驻东京大使褚民谊将此意传达给南京政府。

（同盟社）
东京，7月2日电——祝贺轴心国承认南京政府的贺电继续纷至沓来，汇聚于麻布区中国大使馆，现场呈现出一片欢腾景象。

该报进一步警告敌对列强，若它们希望保障其在南京控制区域内的利益，至少必须与中华民国国民政府保持正常的外交关系。

公使感到困惑
（合众社）
罗马，7月2日电——中国驻意大利公使兼驻罗马代办徐道林先生昨日告诉合众社，鉴于轴心国承认南京政府，现在谈论他的计划安排为何还为时过早。徐先生表示，他并不确切知道自己的地位如何，也不清楚轴心国是否已正式与重庆断绝关系。
（由于轴心国承认南京政府，重庆政府昨日召回了驻轴心国的中国外交官）。

中国报界愤慨
（路透社）
重庆，7月2日电——今晨，中国报界一致对德意两国承认汪精卫先生领导下的南京政府表示极大愤慨。官方报纸《中央日报》在一篇社论中将此举描述为“对中国人民的侮辱”。
该报宣称：“希特勒和墨索里尼政府一直对中国采取不友好态度，推行亲日政策。在其控制下的报刊杂志对中国政府和人民进行恶意攻击。
“此前，中国政府一直克制未采取任何行动，因为中德两国人民在文化和技术关系方面有着真诚友谊和互助的历史。我们不愿因纳粹政权的行径而牺牲中德两国人民的友谊。
“同时，我们希望德国人民能够促使他们的政府改变这一错误政策。然而，随着德国承认傀儡政权，这一希望现已彻底破灭。不过，我们要坚信，这并不代表德国人民的意愿。但值得注意的是，德国和意大利在给予承认之前等待了14个月，这表明此举背后是有动机的。”

Eight Countries Have
Now Fully Recognized
Government At Nanking

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JUL 3 1941.

Chinese Government In Chungking Recalls Envoys
From Rome And Berlin; Spain, Bulgaria And
Hungary Recognize Nanking Government

NO CHANGE IN U.S. RELATIONS WITH
CHINA, JAPAN; TOKYO COMMENT

(Domet)
NANKING, July 2.—With Bulgaria, Spain, and Hungary, following the examples of Germany, Italy, Rumania, Slovakia, and Croatia, the National Government of China at Nanking has now been recognized by eight European countries.

Formal recognition of the Wang Ching-wei Government as the National Government of China by Bulgaria, Spain, and Hungary, was communicated to the Nanking Government through Chinese Ambassador Chu Min-yi at Tokyo by the envoys of these three countries.

(Domet)
TOKYO, July 2.—Messages of congratulation on the recognition of the Nanking Government by the Axis powers, continued to arrive at the Chinese Embassy, Azabu, Ward, which presented a scene of great rejoicing.

Among the numerous visitors to the Embassy was Baron Mario Indelli, Italian Ambassador, who called on Dr. Chu this morning to extend his best wishes for strengthening of ties of friendship between the Nanking and the Italian Governments.

In the afternoon, Dr. Chu returned the courtesy calls of the Italian envoy, as well as German Ambassador Major-General Eugen Ott, at their respective Embassies.

Chungking Relations
(Reuters)
STOCKHOLM, July 2.—As an appeasement towards Japan, the Berlin correspondent of the "Tidningens" expects Germany and Italy shortly to sever relations with the Chungking Government.

A statement on this point is expected to be made in Japan imminently, but it is expected that Japan, for the present, will remain neutral.

(Reuters)
CHUNGKING, July 2.—The Foreign Office has cabled Chen Chieh, Chinese Ambassador to Berlin, and Hsu Tao-lin, Chinese Charge d'Affaires in Rome, instructing the Chinese diplomatic representatives in Germany and Italy to return to China.

The Foreign Minister, Mr. Quo Tai-chi, will issue a statement today announcing the severance of relations with Germany and Italy, and the withdrawal of diplomatic and Consular representatives.

Spain Gives Recognition
(Domet)
MADRID, July 1.—The Foreign Ministry announced today that Spain has recognized the Nanking Government as the National Government of China, and said that a Spanish envoy would be sent to Nanking very soon.

Bulgaria, Hungary Follow Suit
(Reuters)
LONDON, July 2.—Bulgaria and Hungary have decided to recognise the Nanking Government, according to the German Radio.

No Change In U.S. Relations
(Reuters)
WASHINGTON, July 2.—Formal recognition by Germany and Italy of the Nanking regime has not affected the attitude of the United States towards China and Japan, Mr. Sumner Welles, Under-Secretary of State, declared last evening.

New York Press Astir
(Domet)
NEW YORK, July 1.—News of the formal recognition of the Chinese National Government in Nanking by the Axis Powers made the front pages of all evening papers. However, apparently expecting some such move sooner or later, the papers evinced no surprise. On the contrary, they emphasised the delay in recognition until the Axis became involved in hostilities with the Soviet Union, describing the step as a master stroke of timing. Some papers said that if the recognition by other Powers may be expected.

"The National Government can now go forward to further heights of achievement," the editorial declared, "knowing that it is being accorded the fullest sympathy and support, and admitted in equality to the task of worldwide reconstruction on what it is hoped will prove an enduring condition of amity and concord."

Diplomatic Poverty
Pointing out the fact that Italy and Germany have severed diplomatic relations with the Chungking regime as a result of their recognition of the Nanking government, the "Times and Advertiser" declared: "No longer having association with these European Governments, Chungking must still further feel the pinch of diplomatic poverty, and its supporters cannot but realize its waning influence in the world just as they discover the increasing strength of President Wang Ching-wei's authority."

Slow and difficult, but sure and inevitable is the building of a New Order in the Far East, the paper opined, "with past trials justified and the future heralded by this important joint action which will bring further spontaneous jubilation throughout Japan and China."

Stating that China has now become an important part of the great Axis movement for world consolidation, the "Times" concluded, "There is more than a recognition of China in this act. There also is a recognition of the Far Eastern co-prosperity sphere as an integrated force which is destined to do much for the service of all people in the Pacific and Asia."

Recognition of the Nanking Government by Germany, Italy and three other Axis partners, will accelerate disposal of the China conflict, Mr. Chou Fo-hai, Finance Minister of the Nanking Government, declared in an interview yesterday.

Referring to the significance of the recognition of the Nanking Government by the Axis Powers, Mr. Chou declared, "This recognition will further strengthen the Nanking Government's international position and will undoubtedly be a heavy blow to Chungking."

"I believe that the other Axis nations will follow suit and the Chungking officials who are still hesitant in recognizing the Nanking Government will realize sooner or later that it would be in the interest of China that China and Nanking join hands in the construction of a New Order in East Asia."

New Epoch In East Asia Opens
Recognition of the Nanking Government as the National Government of China by five European nations, including Germany and Italy, metropolitan morning dailies agreed, is an event which marks a new epoch in the disposal of the China hostilities and the creation of a prosperity sphere in East Asia.

The "Yomiuri" declared that recognition will have a worldwide repercussion, because it indicates that the creation of a New Order in East Asia is not merely a theory or ideals, but an actuality.

The paper further warned hostile Powers that if they are desirous of safeguarding their interests in the Nanking controlled areas, they will at least have to maintain normal diplomatic relations with the National Government of China.

Minister Perplexed
(United Press)
ROME, July 2.—Mr. Hsu Dau-lin, Chinese Minister to Italy and Charge d'Affairs in Rome, told the United Press yesterday that it was too soon to say what his plans might be as result of Axis recognition of the Nanking government.

Mr. Hsu indicated he did not exactly know what his position was, or whether the Axis had yet officially severed relations with Chungking.

(The Chungking Government yesterday recalled Chinese diplomats from Axis countries as result of Axis recognition of Nanking).

Chinese Press Indignant
(Reuters)
CHUNGKING, July 2.—The Chinese press this morning unanimously expressed the greatest indignation over the German and Italian recognition of the Nanking Government under Mr. Wang Ching-wei.

The official "Central Daily News," in a leading article, describes the action as an "insult to the Chinese people."

The daily declares: "The Hitler and Mussolini Governments have always adopted an unfriendly attitude towards China, pursuing a pro-Japanese policy. Newspapers and periodicals under their control make malicious attacks on the Chinese Government and people.

"The Chinese Government had hitherto refrained from taking any action, as the Chinese and German peoples had a history of sincere friendship and mutual assistance in cultural and technical relations. We were unwilling to sacrifice the friendship of the Chinese and German peoples because of the actions of the Nazi regime.

"At the same time we hoped that the German people would be able to induce their government to change their mistaken policy. 八国现已完全承认南京政府

《上海泰晤士报》。
1941年7月3日。

重庆中国政府召回驻罗马和柏林使节；西班牙、保加利亚和匈牙利承认南京政府

美日关系无变化；东京评论

（多梅特通讯社）
南京，7月2日电——继德国、意大利、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克和克罗地亚之后，保加利亚、西班牙和匈牙利也效仿其例，至此，位于南京的中华民国国民政府已获得八个欧洲国家的承认。

保加利亚、西班牙和匈牙利正式承认汪精卫政府为中华民国国民政府，这三国使节已通过中国驻东京大使褚民谊将此意传达给南京政府。

（多梅特通讯社）
东京，7月2日电——祝贺轴心国承认南京政府的贺电继续纷至沓来，位于麻布区的中国大使馆内呈现出一片欢腾景象。

在众多拜访大使馆的访客中，有意大利大使马里奥·因德利男爵（Baron Mario Indelli），他于今晨拜访褚博士，以表达其对加强南京政府与意大利政府之间友好纽带的最良好祝愿。

下午，褚博士分别前往意大利和德国大使馆，回访了意大利使节以及德国大使欧根·奥特少将（Major-General Eugen Ott）。

重庆方面关系
（路透社）
斯德哥尔摩，7月2日电——据《Tidningens》报柏林记者预测，作为对日本的安抚，德国和意大利不久将与重庆政府断绝关系。

预计日本方面即将就此发表声明，但预料日本目前将保持中立。

（路透社）
重庆，7月2日电——外交部已致电中国驻柏林大使陈介和中国驻罗马代办徐道林，指令中国在德国和意大利的外交代表返回中国。

外交部长郭泰祺先生将于今日发表声明，宣布与德国和意大利断绝关系，并撤回外交及领事代表。

西班牙给予承认
（多梅特通讯社）
马德里，7月1日电——外交部今日宣布，西班牙已承认南京政府为中华民国国民政府，并称西班牙使节将很快派往南京。

保加利亚、匈牙利紧随其后
（路透社）
伦敦，7月2日电——据德国广播电台消息，保加利亚和匈牙利已决定承认南京政府。

美国关系无变化
（路透社）
华盛顿，7月2日电——国务卿助理萨姆纳·韦尔斯先生昨晚宣称，德国和意大利对南京政权的正式承认并未影响美国对中国和日本的态度。

纽约报界骚动
（多梅特通讯社）
纽约，7月1日电——轴心国正式承认南京中华民国国民政府的消息登上了所有晚报的头版。然而，各报似乎早已预料到迟早会有此举，因此并未表现出惊讶。相反，它们强调承认之举一直拖延至轴心国卷入与苏联的敌对行动之后，称这一步骤在时机把握上堪称妙着。一些报纸表示，其他列强的承认或许也可期待。

社论宣称：“国民政府如今可以迈向更高的成就巅峰，因为它知道自身正获得充分的同情与支持，并被平等地接纳参与世界重建工作，而这有望证明是一种持久的和睦与协调状态。”

外交困境
《字林西报》指出，意大利和德国因承认南京政府而与重庆政权断绝外交关系这一事实，并宣称：“重庆不再与这些欧洲政府有任何关联，必将进一步感受到外交匮乏的窘迫，其支持者也不得不意识到其在世界上的影响力正在减弱，正如他们发现汪精卫主席的权威日益增强一样。”

该报认为，东亚新秩序的建立虽然缓慢且艰难，但确凿且不可避免，“过去的考验由此得到正当化，而这一重要的联合行动预示着未来，将在日本和中国引发更多自发的欢庆。”

《字林西报》在陈述中国现已成为轴心国为世界整合而进行的伟大运动的重要组成部分后总结道：“这一举动不仅仅是对中国的承认。这也是对大东亚共荣圈作为一个整体力量的承认，该力量注定将为太平洋和亚洲所有人民的服务做出巨大贡献。”

南京政府财政部长周佛海先生在昨日的一次采访中表示，德国、意大利及其他三个轴心国伙伴对南京政府的承认，将加速解决中国冲突。

谈及轴心国承认南京政府的意义时，周先生宣称：“这一承认将进一步巩固南京政府的国际地位，并无疑将对重庆造成沉重打击。”

“我相信其他轴心国也将效仿，而那些在承认南京政府问题上仍犹豫不决的重庆官员迟早会意识到，中国与南京携手建设东亚新秩序符合中国的利益。”

东亚开启新纪元
包括晨报在内的都市日报一致认为，德国和意大利等五个欧洲国家承认南京政府为中华民国国民政府，是标志着解决中国敌对行动及创建东亚繁荣 sphere 新纪元的事件。

《读卖新闻》宣称，这一承认将产生世界性的反响，因为它表明东亚新秩序的建立不仅仅是一种理论或理想，而是现实。

该报宣称，预计保加利亚、西班牙、匈牙利和法国在不久的将来也会给予承认。祝贺……尊重其控制区域内的利益。

该报进一步警告敌对列强，如果它们希望保障在南京控制区域内的利益，至少必须与中华民国国民政府保持正常的外交关系。

公使困惑
（合众社）
罗马，7月2日电——中国驻意大利公使兼驻罗马代办徐道林先生昨日告诉合众社，鉴于轴心国承认南京政府，现在谈论他的计划还为时过早。

徐先生表示，他并不确切知道自己的地位如何，也不清楚轴心国是否已正式与重庆断绝关系。

（由于轴心国承认南京政府，重庆政府昨日召回了驻轴心国的中国外交官）。

中国报界愤慨
（路透社）
重庆，7月2日电——中国报界今晨一致对德国和意大利承认汪精卫先生领导下的南京政府表示极大愤慨。

官方报纸《中央日报》在一篇社论中将此行动描述为“对中国人民的侮辱”。

该报宣称：“希特勒和墨索里尼政府一直对中国采取不友好态度，推行亲日政策。受其控制的报刊杂志对中国政府和人民进行恶意攻击。

“中国政府此前一直克制未采取任何行动，因为中德两国人民在文化和技术关系方面有着真诚友谊和互助的历史。我们不愿因纳粹政权的行动而牺牲中德两国人民的友谊。

“同时，我们希望德国人民能够促使他们的政府改变其错误政策。然而，随着德国承认傀儡政权，这一希望现已彻底破灭。不过，我们要确信，这并不代表德国人民的意愿。但值得注意的是，德国和意大利在给予承认之前等待了如此之久，其动机现在已……”

一些报纸称，如果德国的举动并非旨在将日本拖入对俄战争，那么至少也是旨在通过展示威胁苏联前后方的坚固轴心国阵线来遏制苏联。
观察家认为，日本不会因这一承认而采取任何积极步骤，并强调重庆政权与轴心国之间的关系已发生变化。

新秩序的持久性
（同盟社）
东京，7月2日电——《日本时报暨广告人报》在今早发表的一篇社论中评论德国、意大利、斯洛伐克、克罗地亚和罗马尼亚对南京政府的外交承认时宣称，对南京中华民国国民政府的法律承认将“向世界强调中国新秩序的力量和持久性”。
该社论宣称：“日本人民希望借此机会向地位日益提升的南京表示祝贺，并向意大利、德国及其他列强对其承认表示感谢。”
该日报称，此举紧随汪精卫主席访日以及向南京政府提供用于建设和扩展目的的大额贷款之后，“这种承认状态将向世界强调中国新秩序的力量和持久性。这将导致____

《读卖新闻》宣称，承认将产生世界性的反响，因为它表明东亚新秩序的创建不仅仅是一种理论或理想，而是现实。
该日报宣称，预计保加利亚、西班牙、匈牙利和法国在不久的将来也会予以承认。社论祝贺南京政府在成立后短时间内赢得国际承认，并断言：
“日满华集团现在被国际公认为创建新东亚的轴心。”
《国民新闻》断言，国民政府在获得欧洲国家承认后的任务是“在日本的帮助下废除南京控制下的中国境内的外国租界”。
该社论回顾近卫文麿首相多次表示日本愿意将租界归还中国的事实，宣称：“日本政府宣布协同措施以彻底解决租界问题的时机已经成熟。”

租界将被废除
《国民新闻》补充说，废除作为“颠覆活动温床”的租界，将加强南京政府的政治权力并改善南京控制区的状况。
《报知新闻》与其他晨报一致，宣称欧洲列强承认国民政府是对重庆国际地位的重大打击。然而，该报警告说，英国、美国和苏联将继续保持与重庆的现有关系。
《报知新闻》称，如果这三国继续拒绝承认中华民国国民政府，后者此后将“坚决对付与其敌对的列强，因为它没有义务____

SHANGHAI TIMES,
JUL 3 1941.

Nanking Said Preparing
To Take Over Settlement
Tribunal In Near Future

Municipal Reaction To Attempt Seen Depending
On Method Used; No Talks Underway Over
Issue Heightened By Recognitions

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE “QUITE CERTAIN”
NANKING TO MAKE BID FOR COURTS

The Nanking Government is “definitely known” to be preparing an imminent attempt to take over the Chinese courts in the International Settlement, at present under the jurisdiction of the government in Chungking, a highly authoritative foreign source told “The Shanghai Times” yesterday. This decision was reached without any negotiations being started, he disclosed.

The stand of the Shanghai Municipal Council in the face of a resolute bid for the cession of the Settlement courts would be “difficult to predict,” he declared, but would probably depend on the method used by the Nanking Government. Should its representatives take over the premises with the backing of Japanese armed forces, there would be little that local municipal and consular authorities could do under the present circumstances, he said.

“Quite Certain”

It was not known to him, he continued, whether the Nanking Government would attempt to take over the Settlement courts by force or through negotiations. The one thing of which he was “quite certain,” he declared, was that the Nanking Government has decided to take such a step and intended to put its decision into force in the near future. “It may come quite suddenly,” he added.

A strong possibility, he continued, would be that the Nanking Government would use the recognition granted it by Germany and other Axis-dominated countries as one reason for claiming jurisdiction over the Settlement courts. Since countries like Germany, Hungary and Bulgaria do not enjoy extra-territorial rights in China, their nationals were, so far, tried in the Settlement courts with regard to criminal or civil offences committed in the Settlement.

Since their countries have withdrawn their recognition from the Chinese Government in Chungking, the Nanking Government may now claim that these nationals can no longer be tried in a Chungking court. This, the informant said, is cited as one of the principal reasons for the cession of the courts to the Nanking Government.

Legal Tangle Belittled

The reliable source foresaw little actual difficulty in suits involving foreign residents not enjoying extra-territoriality. The number of cases who have appeared before the Chinese courts within the last decade has been comparatively insignificant, while it is “highly improbable” that German refugees would demand being tried before a Nanking in preference to a Chungking tribunal.

The Japanese authorities, he recalled, have long been expressing their desire for the Nanking Government to control the First Special District Court and other Chinese tribunals in the Settlement, but no actual negotiations on the score ever took place.

In December, 1940, after a brief flurry of rumours which the French authorities steadfastly refused to confirm, Japanese and Nanking officials rolled up in their limousines to the premises of the Kiangsu High Court, Third Branch, on Route des Sieyes, for a conference that stretched into the afternoon.

At 5 p.m. the same day, at the Broadway Mansions, the Japanese Embassy Spokesman announced that the Kiangsu High Court, Third Branch, and the Second Special District Court, had been ceded to the Nanking Government through the good offices of the Japanese authorities. In the evening the French authorities confirmed the cession by a special communique through Havas news agency.

The Japanese authorities at that time said they would not be satisfied until the Settlement courts were also ceded to the Nanking Government. They added, however, that no immediate steps on the matter were planned. Since then speculation continued on whether the Japanese and Nanking authorities still planned to take over the Settlement courts, or had shelved the matter for the time being.

（批：3/7）

《上海泰晤士报》，
1941年7月3日。

据称南京方面正筹备
于近期接管租界法院

工部局对此次尝试的反应视乎所用手段；因承认问题而加剧的此事尚无谈判进行

权威消息源称南京方面“十分确定”将谋求接管法院

一位极具权威的外国消息人士昨日告诉《上海泰晤士报》，已知南京政府“确凿无疑”地正在筹备一项迫在眉睫的尝试，旨在接管目前受重庆政府管辖的国际公共租界内的中国法院。他透露，这一决定是在未启动任何谈判的情况下作出的。

他宣称，面对坚决要求割让租界法院的举动，上海工部局的立场将“难以预测”，但可能取决于南京政府所采用的方法。他说，如果其代表在日本武装力量的支持下接管办公场所，那么在当前局势下，当地市政和领事当局能做的寥寥无几。

“十分确定”

他继续说道，他并不知晓南京政府是会试图通过武力还是通过谈判来接管租界法院。他宣称，他“十分确定”的一点是，南京政府已决定采取这一步骤，并打算在不久的将来实施该决定。“它可能会来得非常突然，”他补充道。

他继续说，一种很大的可能性是，南京政府将利用德国及其他轴心国主导国家给予它的承认，作为声称对租界法院拥有管辖权的理由之一。由于德国、匈牙利和保加利亚等国在中国不享有治外法权，迄今为止，这些国家的国民若在租界内犯下刑事或民事罪行，均在租界法院受审。

既然这些国家已撤回对重庆中国政府的承认，南京政府现在可能会声称，这些国家的国民不能再由重庆的法院审判。这位消息人士称，这被列为将法院移交给南京政府的主要原因之一。

法律纠葛被轻视

该可靠消息源预见，在涉及不享有治外法权的外侨的诉讼中，实际困难甚微。过去十年间出现在中国法院的案件数量相对微不足道，而且德国难民要求优先在南京而非重庆的法庭受审是“极不可能的”。

他回顾道，日本当局长期以来一直表示希望南京政府控制第一特区法院及租界内的其他中国法庭，但就此从未进行过实质性的谈判。

1940年12月，在经历了一阵法国当局坚决拒绝证实的短暂谣言风波后，日本和南京官员乘坐豪华轿车前往西爱咸斯路（Route des Sieyes）的江苏高等法院第三分院办公地点，参加了一场持续至下午的会议。

同日下午5时，日本大使馆发言人在百老汇大厦宣布，经日本当局斡旋，江苏高等法院第三分院和第二特区法院已移交给南京政府。当晚，法国当局通过哈瓦斯通讯社发布特别公报，确认了此次移交。

日本当局当时表示，除非租界法院也移交给南京政府，否则他们不会满意。然而，他们补充说，目前尚未计划就此采取立即行动。此后，人们一直猜测日本和南京当局是仍计划接管租界法院，还是暂时搁置了此事。

（批：3/7）

CHINA PRESS.
12 1 3 1940

I.N.S. Man Rapped
Wang Is Not
A Prisoner,
Say Japanese

Accusing Chester S. Holcombe, Shanghai representative of the International News Service, of having “disregarded the courtesy and hospitality extended to him by the Chinese and Japanese authorities,” the Embassy spokesman at the Japanese press conference last night added that the interview with Mr. Wang Ching-wei published by Mr. Holcombe in the China Weekly Review does harm not only to China but also to the relations between Japan and the United States of America.

Mr. Holcombe had described Mr. Wang as a “prisoner of the Japanese” in Nanking, and the Embassy spokesman said the fact that the city of Nanking was garrisoned by Japanese forces, who also gave their protection to the person of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, was not sufficient grounds for such a statement.

The Japanese authorities had sympathized with the lofty ideals expressed by Mr. Wang in December, 1938, and had decided to assist him to strive for the resurrection and reconstruction of a new China. It is not the aim of Japan to leave the Chinese people in miserable circumstances, and the Japanese authorities are therefore co-operating with Mr. Wang Ching-wei in his work, stated the Embassy spokesman.

The article in question, complained the spokesman, is full of malice from beginning to end, and there is good reason to suppose that Mr. Holcombe has become a slave of journalism in its worst sense.

（批：S. 1/3 (1-3)6）

1940年1月12日

国际新闻社人员遭斥责
日方称汪氏并非囚犯

在昨夜的日本记者招待会上，大使馆发言人指责国际新闻社（International News Service）上海代表切斯特·S. 霍尔科姆（Chester S. Holcombe）“无视中日当局给予他的礼遇和款待”，并补充说，霍尔科姆先生在《密勒氏评论报》上发表的与汪精卫先生的谈话，不仅损害中国，也损害日本与美利坚合众国之间的关系。

霍尔科姆先生曾将汪先生描述为在南京的“日本人的囚徒”，大使馆发言人表示，南京城由日军驻防，且日军也对汪精卫先生的人身提供保护，这一事实并不足以成为作出此种陈述的理由。

日本当局对汪先生在1938年12月所表达的崇高理想表示同情，并决定协助他为实现新中国的复兴与重建而努力。大使馆发言人称，日本的宗旨并非让中国人民处于悲惨境地，因此日本当局正在与汪精卫先生合作开展其工作。

该发言人抱怨说，涉事文章从头到尾充满恶意，有充分理由推测，霍尔科姆先生已沦为最恶劣意义上的新闻奴仆。

Important Steps Taken
In The Realization Of
Peace, Declares Mr. Wang

Momentous Resolutions Passed During Three-Day
Session Of Central Political Conference;
Principle Of Good Neighbourliness

NEW FOREIGN AFFAIRS APPOINTEE
TO CIRCULATE STATEMENT

NANKING, March 23.—Important resolutions were passed during the three-day session of the Central Political Conference concerning the realization of peace and the enforcement of constitutional Government, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Acting President of the reorganized National Government, declared at the final session of the Conference on Friday.

“In regard to the realization of peace, resolutions were passed to readjust Sino-Japanese relations on the fundamental principles of good neighbourliness, a common anti-Comintern front, and economic co-operation, aiming at attaining independence and liberty as to our sovereignty and equality and reciprocity as to economic affairs. Now peace and order in East Asia can be solidly established,” Mr. Wang said.

“With reference to the enforcement of the Constitutional Government, a resolution has been passed to establish a Committee for enforcement of Constitutional Government. To this end, the Committee shall, within the shortest possible period, convene the National Assembly to draft, promulgate and enforce the Constitution.

Seat At Nanking

“A resolution has also been passed to the effect that the National Government shall return to its capital at Nanking with a view to carrying out simultaneously these two important policies. This is indeed great progress in the movement for peace and national reconstruction,” he continued.

“The members of this Conference had unanimously adopted these resolutions in a spirit of sincere solidarity, then I feel they will strive all the more in concert to put these resolutions into practice. The movement for peace and national reconstruction will thus progress further by virtue of the unification now achieved and will eventually become nationwide. With the attainment of peace and national reconstruction, not only the liberty and equality of China will be secured, but that of East Asia will be safeguarded. So I wish success to the future of China as well as to East Asia,” Mr. Wang said in conclusion.

Foreign Affairs Appointee

East Asiatic and international peace, international justice, respect for foreign powers’ rights and interests, reciprocal trade, and the open door policy were expected to be contained in a statement to be made soon by Dr. Chu Min-i, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the reorganized National Government of China.

It was also understood that the statement would formally notify foreign Powers of the reorganization of the National Government and its return to the former capital.

up a three-day session during which the fundamental problems for reorganization of the National Government of China were deliberated by 30 members drawn from many parts of the country under the chairmanship of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, the Central Political Conference adjourned at 10:30 o’clock this morning.

1940年4月15日

汪先生宣称
为实现和平
已采取重要步骤

中央政治会议三日会期通过重大决议；
确立善邻原则

新任外交部长
将发表声明

南京，3月23日电——改组后的国民政府代理主席汪精卫先生于周五会议闭幕式上宣布，在为期三天的中央政治会议期间，通过了关于实现和平及实施宪政的重要决议。

“关于实现和平，会议通过决议，以善邻、共同防共及经济合作为基本原则，调整中日关系，旨在实现主权独立自由以及经济事务上的平等互惠。如今，东亚的和平与秩序得以稳固建立，”汪先生说。

“关于实施宪政，已通过决议成立实施宪政委员会。为此，该委员会将在尽可能短的时期内召集国民大会，起草、颁布并实施宪法。

定都南京

“会议还通过决议，国民政府将还都南京，以便同时推行这两项重要政策。这确实是和平运动与国家重建运动的巨大进步，”他继续说道。

“本次会议成员本着真诚团结的精神一致通过了这些决议，因此我相信他们将更加齐心协力，将这些决议付诸实践。凭借现已实现的统一，和平与国家重建运动将进一步推进，并最终遍及全国。随着和平与国家重建的实现，不仅中国的自由与平等将获得保障，东亚的自由与平等也将得到维护。因此，我祝愿中国及东亚的未来取得成功，”汪先生在结尾时说道。

外交部长人选

预计东亚与国际和平、国际正义、尊重外国列强权益、互惠贸易以及门户开放政策等内容，将包含在中华民国改组国民政府外交部长褚民谊博士即将发表的声明中。

另据悉，该声明将正式通知外国列强关于国民政府的改组及其还都旧都事宜。

中央政治会议在汪精卫先生主持下，由来自全国各地的30名成员组成，经过为期三天的会议，审议了改组中华民国国民政府的基本问题，于今天上午10时30分休会。

Economic Reconstruction
NANKING, March 28.—Economic
reconstruction constituted the main
task of the reorganized National
Government which will be
inaugurated here on March 30,
Mr. Lin Pai-sheng, spokesman for
the Central Political Conference,
which concluded its sessions on
Friday, told 100 Japanese, Chinese
and foreign correspondents on the
eve of the last session.
The main political significance of
the reorganization, however, lies
in the clear distinction that was
made between Government and
Party to eliminate abuses and con-
flicts prevalent under Kuomintang
one-party rule, he said.
In order to expend “more
effort” in rebuilding the Chinese
nation economically “after two
years of destruction,” Mr. Lin de-
clared, the Ministries of Industry
and Commerce and of Agriculture
and Mining, formerly grouped
under the Ministry of Industries,
have been re-established, while the
Department of Publicity, the De-
partment of Social Affairs, and the
Political Training Department for
troops, formerly dependent upon
the Central Kuomintang, have
been respectively established as
the Ministry of Publicity and the
Ministry of Social Affairs, of the
Executive Yuan, and the Director-
ate of Political Training of the
Military Commission.
The Ministries of Railways and
of Communications were also re-
constituted, he stated.

A Series of Conflicts
Speaking in Chinese from the
centre of a U-shaped press table in
the dining room of the Metropolitan
Hotel, Mr. Lin described at length
various conflicts which prevailed
under the former Kuomintang one-
party rule. His remarks were
translated first into Japanese, and
then into English.
Referring to the formerly exist-
ing conflicts of authority between
the Government and the Party,
Mr. Lin cited as an example the
difficulties that could be encounter-
ed by persons intending to publish
a newspaper.
Their application for registration,
he said, first had to be filed with
the local administration, which re-
ferred it to the Ministry of In-
terior for approval. Another ap-
plication had to be made to the
local branch or branch of the Kuo-
mintang, which, in turn, passed it
on to the Kuomintang Headquarters
for sanction. Besides the delay in-
volved by this procedure, the Gov-
ernment and the Party frequently
did not see eye to eye on some sub-
jects with the result that an ap-
plication approved by the Govern-
ment was rejected by the Party, or
vice versa. The public was the
main sufferer in such cases, he as-
serted.
Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Mr. Lin con-
tinued, had pointed out these de-
fects in 1929-30. The party, Mr.
Wang had stated, should not stand
side by side with the Government
as a “ruling class” but should re-
main among the people, to lead
them, Mr. Lin recalled.
“Under the dictatorship of Chiang
Kai-shek, however, no change could
be expected,” Mr. Lin stated. The
situation only deteriorated, he said.
A “radical correction” of such
basic conflicts was necessary, Mr.
Lin said, explaining the steps taken
by Mr. Wang and his associates in
drawing up the organization of the
National Government of China for
its impending “return” to Nanking.
—Domel.

Chungking Paper On Motives
CHUNGKING, March 22.—In a
leading article on the forthcoming
establishment of the new Central
Government at Nanking, the “Sao
Tang Pao,” organ of the Chinese
Army, to-day declares: “The in-
tention of the Japanese in making
use of Wang Ching-wei is to use
Chinese against Chinese, attempting
to create internal dissension, there-
by weakening China’s resistance.”
Furthermore, the paper declares,
Japanese support for Wang Ching-
wei is for the purpose of exerting
pressure on Third Powers, forcing
them to recognize the results of
Japanese aggression and to nego-
tiate with a puppet regime, in order
to protect their interests and rights
in China.
The “Sao Tang Pao” adds: “But
the speech by United States’ Am-
bassador, Mr. Joseph Grew, last
October, also the abrogation of the
Japanese-American commercial trea-
ty, in January, proved that the
Japanese use of Wang Ching-wei is
producing no effect on Third
Powers’ policy in China.
“The prolonged war is already
resulting in an economic strain on
Japan. Therefore, the Japanese
have concluded an agreement with
Wang Chin-wei for economic ex-
ploitation in China, hoping to finance
the war in China with Chinese re-
sources.
“The failure of the Japanese in-
vasion, as well as the collapse of the
puppet regime, will be inevitable,”
the paper concludes.—Reuter.

9,670 Telegrams Sent
During the three-day Central
Political Conference which was
brought to an end on Friday, the
Nanking Telegram Office was kept
busy day and night as Japanese,
Chinese and foreign correspondents
sent altogether 9,670 telegrams to
relay the historic events, the
“Tohoku Shimpo” reported yester-
day.
Of the 9,670 telegrams, 4,500
were written in Japanese, 3,000 in
Chinese and the rest in western
languages, the paper reported.
Brief messages were transmitted
in one minute and longer ones in
35 minutes at the most, the paper
said.
The busy was the Nanking Tele-
gram Office, which handled 3,000
telegrams during the three days. Most of
the calls were made to Shanghai
and the daily number of telegrams
was three times more than the usual daily
average, it was reported.

经济重建
南京，3月28日电。——中央政治会议发言人林柏生先生在上周五会议结束前夕，向100名日本、中国及外国记者表示，经济重建构成了将于3月30日在此就职的改组后的国民政府的主要任务。该中央政治会议已于周五结束其议程。
然而，他表示，此次改组的主要政治意义在于明确区分政府与党，以消除国民党一党专政下普遍存在的弊端和冲突。
林先生宣称，为了在“经过两年破坏”后“更加用力”地重建中华民族的经济，原隶属于实业部的工商部和农矿部已重新设立；而原依附于国民党中央的宣传处、社会处以及军队政治训练处，则分别改组为行政院属下的宣传部和社会部，以及军事委员会属下的政治训练总监部。
他还 stated，铁道部和交通部也已重组。

一系列冲突
林先生在大都会酒店（Metropolitan Hotel）餐厅内呈U形的记者席中央用中文发言，详细描述了前国民党一党专政下普遍存在的各种冲突。他的讲话先被译成日语，随后译成英语。
谈及此前政府与党之间存在的权限冲突，林先生以有意创办报纸者所遇到的困难为例。
他说，他们的注册申请首先必须提交给地方行政机关，由其转呈内政部批准。另外还需向国民党地方分部或支部提出申请，后者再将其转呈国民党中央总部核准。除了这一程序带来的延误外，政府和党在某些问题上经常意见不一，导致政府批准的申请被党驳回，反之亦然。他断言，在这种情况下，公众是主要的受害者。
林先生继续说道，汪精卫先生曾在1929-30年指出这些缺陷。林先生回忆说，汪先生曾指出，党不应作为“统治阶级”与政府并列，而应留在民众之中，领导民众。
“然而，在蒋介石的独裁统治下，不可能期待任何改变，”林先生表示。他说，局势只是进一步恶化。
林先生说，有必要对这类基本冲突进行“彻底纠正”，并解释了汪先生及其同僚在为即将“还都”南京的中国国民政府拟定组织架构时所采取的步骤。——多梅尔（Domel）。

重庆报纸论动机
重庆，3月22日电。——中国军队机关报《扫荡报》今日就即将在南京成立的新中央政府发表社论称：“日本人利用汪精卫的意图是以华制华，企图制造内部纷争，从而削弱中国的抵抗。”
该报还宣称，日本支持汪精卫的目的是向第三国施压，迫使它们承认日本侵略的成果，并与傀儡政权进行谈判，以保护其在华利益和权利。
《扫荡报》补充道：“但是，去年十月美国大使约瑟夫·格鲁（Joseph Grew）的讲话，以及今年一月废止《美日商约》，都证明日本利用汪精卫并未对第三国在华政策产生任何影响。”
“长期的战争已经给日本造成经济压力。因此，日本人与汪精卫达成了在华进行经济掠夺的协议，希望利用中国资源来资助在华战争。”
该报总结道：“日本入侵的失败以及傀儡政权的垮台将是不可避免的。”——路透社。

发出9,670封电报
据《东北新报》（Tohoku Shimpo）昨日报道，在周五结束的为期三天的中央政治会议期间，南京电报局日夜忙碌，日本、中国及外国记者共发出9,670封电报，以报道这一历史性事件。
该报报道，在这9,670封电报中，4,500封用日文撰写，3,000封用中文撰写，其余用西方语言撰写。
该报称，简短的电报在一分钟内发出，较长的电报最多需时35分钟。
南京电报局在这三天内处理了3,000封电报，工作十分繁忙。据报道，大多数电话打往上海，每日电报数量是平日平均水平的三倍。

MAR 24 1940

All Free China
Said Ignoring
Wang Regime

(United Press)
CHUNGKING, Mar. 23.—Official Chinese Government quarters and the local press yesterday unanimously declared that the rump "Kuomintang" regime at Nanking, headed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, was "doomed to failure" and said that "as a matter of course, all free China would ignore the decisions orders of the Nanking regime."

"Wang Ching-wei is only fooling himself," they said, "and China will completely ignore his order to cease hostilities."

Mr. Lin Sen, President of the National Government, speaking before the Central Party Headquarters, charged that the Nanking regime represented a Japanese effort to deceive the Japanese people and divide the Chinese people.

See Exhaustion

"The present plots of the enemy merely indicate his exhaustion and are perfectly harmless to us. All our loyal people and our army can realize the enemy's intrigue and they are determined to fight and shatter the enemy's ambitions," President Lin Sen declared.

The official Chinese Government spokesman pointed out that the National Government had repeatedly "announced to the world that all actions, contracts, treaties and orders issued by any puppet regimes" would be null and void.

"There is no need at the present to stress this point again," the spokesman said.

Mr. Kuo Mo-juo, chief of the National Military Council's propaganda bureau declared that "Nanking is Wang-Ching-wei's grave."

"Monkey Show"

Meanwhile, the Chinese press yesterday criticized the "government" of Mr. Wang, characterizing it as a "monkey show with the Japanese holding the rope and beating the gong."

The official newspaper Hankow Herald said the Nanking regime was "a farce which is doomed to failure and will not affect China's war of resistance in the least."

The official Chinese Army organ Sao Tang Pao said the Nanking regime of Mr. Wang was "a monkey show designed by the Japanese to make further bargainings with the Western Powers and force the European and American Powers into starting diplomatic negotiations advantageous to the Japanese."

"Lost Sense Of Shame"

The influential newspaper Ta Kung Pao said, "All members of the Wang Ching-wei regime have lost their sense of shame . . . they have all forgotten they are still Chinese."

"Nanking is the place where the enemy killed 300,000 of our brothers and raped thousands of our sisters. How can Chinese forget such bloody enmity? We should all attack Nanking immediately and kill all of these people," the Ta Kung Pao declared.

Meanwhile, it was officially announced that March 30, the date chosen by Mr. Wang Ching-wei for the inauguration of his Nanking Government, would be celebrated in Chungking as the second anniversary of the 1938 Taierchwang victory, described as the "Tannenburg victory of the Orient."

DEMANDS STATUS
QUO ADMINISTRATION

(United Press)
FEIPING, Mar 23.—The North China Political Council has agreed to cede Honan Province and part of Kiangsu Province to Mr. Wang Ching-wei's new "Central Government" on the condition "that the status quo of the local administration of those Provinces remains unchanged," according to the Chinese news agency Chunghwa yesterday.

Meanwhile, the news agency disclosed that Mr. Chi Hsieh-yuan will head the "North China Pacification Commission." This was the organization which Marshal Wu Pei-fu, late war lord, refused to accept.

The currency of North China and Mongolia will remain unchanged, the agency reported, while the "Hsin Min Hui" (New Life Party) will continue with Japanese military advisers.

Members of the "Provisional Government," however, expected a large personnel change in the new government, it was said.

1940年3月24日

全自由中国
称将无视
汪伪政权

（合众社）
重庆，3月23日电。——中国政府官方人士及当地报刊昨日一致宣称，由汪精卫先生领导的南京残余“国民党”政权“注定失败”，并称“理所当然，全自由中国将无视南京政权的决定与命令”。

他们说：“汪精卫只是在自欺欺人，中国将完全无视其停止敌对行动的命令。”

国民政府主席林森先生在中央党部讲话时指责称，南京政权是日本为欺骗日本人民和分裂中国人民而做出的努力。

预见其穷途末路

“敌人目前的阴谋仅表明其已筋疲力尽，对我们毫无危害。所有忠诚的民众和我军均能识破敌人的诡计，并决心战斗以粉碎敌人的野心，”林森主席宣称。

中国政府发言人指出，国民政府已多次“向全世界宣布，任何傀儡政权所发布的一切行动、合同、条约和命令”均属无效。

发言人称：“目前无需再次强调这一点。”

国民政府军事委员会政治部部长郭沫若先生宣称，“南京是汪精卫的坟墓”。

“猴子戏”

与此同时，中国报刊昨日批评汪先生的“政府”，将其形容为“一场由日本人牵绳敲锣的猴子戏”。

官方报纸《汉口日报》称，南京政权是“一场注定失败的闹剧，绝不会对中国的抗战产生丝毫影响”。

中国军方官方报纸《扫荡报》称，汪先生的南京政权是“日本人为进一步与西方列强讨价还价，并迫使欧美列强开启有利于日本的外交谈判而设计的猴子戏”。

“丧失羞耻心”

有影响力的报纸《大公报》称：“汪精卫政权的所有成员都已丧失羞耻心……他们都忘记了自己仍然是中国人。”

《大公报》宣称：“南京是敌人杀害我们三十万同胞、强奸我们数千姐妹的地方。中国人怎能忘记如此血海深仇？我们都应立即进攻南京，杀光这些人。”

与此同时，官方宣布，汪精卫选定的南京政府就职日期3月30日，将在重庆作为1938年台儿庄大捷两周年纪念日进行庆祝，该胜利被描述为“东方的坦嫩贝格胜利”。

要求维持
现状行政

（合众社）
北平，3月23日电。——据中华通讯社昨日报道，华北政务委员会已同意将河南省及江苏省部分地区割让给汪精卫的新“中央政府”，条件是“这些省份的地方行政现状保持不变”。

与此同时，该通讯社披露，齐燮元先生将领导“华北绥靖委员会”。这正是已故军阀吴佩孚元帅拒绝接受的机构。

该社报道称，华北及蒙疆的货币将保持不变，而“新民会”将继续在日本军事顾问的指导下运作。

据说，“临时政府”的成员预计新政府将出现大规模的人事变动。

MAR 27 1940

（印：S. J. HEGARTY / No. S. B. D. 8986 / Date 15 H 40）

Depends On Japan
U. S., Soviet
Press Spurn
Wang Regime

(Tass)
MOSCOW, Mar. 25.—"The Japanese militarists strive to accelerate the formation of the 'new government' because with their position in Japan becoming less stable, they need Wang Ching-wei's 'successes'," writes Pravda, commenting on the conference in Nanking which had adopted a decision on the formation of a new "central government" on March 30.

"The 75th session of the Japanese Parliament has reflected the growing dissatisfaction by the policy pursued by the military circles. This dissatisfaction is directed chiefly against the China policy of the military circles. The split in the Shakai Taishu-to (Socialist People's Party) is fresh evidence of the growing opposition against the policy of the military circles vis-a-vis China. Thus the expulsion of Saito did not stop the growing dissatisfaction in the country.

"According to the opinion of the militarist circles the forced preparation for the formation of Wang Ching-wei's "government" must calm the uneasiness in the Parliament and beyond it.

"Consequently, the Nanking staging and clamor about the 'successes' of Wang Ching-wei's movement represent nothing but an ineffective smoke barrage behind which the growing weakness of the Japanese internal situation is hidden."

WANG CANNOT STAND
WITHOUT JAPANESE ARMY

(United Press)
NEW YORK, Mar. 26.—The new Nanking "Government" under Mr. Wang Ching-wei, leader of the Nanking "Kuomintang," can exist only as long as it is protected by the Japanese Army, the New York Daily News stated in an editorial today.

The editorial, entitled "The Traitor, Wang Ching-wei—Japan's Puppet in China," stated:

"The Government of China's Benedict Arnold can last only so long as it is upheld by Japanese bayonets. That is why the United States may write the next chapter in the story of Wang. The United States could give the Japanese invasion a terrific blow by clapping on an embargo."

1940年3月27日

依赖日本
美苏报刊
唾弃汪伪政权

（塔斯社）
莫斯科，3月25日电。——《真理报》在评论南京会议通过于3月30日成立新的“中央政府”的决定时写道：“日本军国主义者竭力加速组建‘新政府’，因为随着他们在日本的地位变得日益不稳，他们需要汪精卫的‘成功’。”

“日本议会第七十五届会议反映了军方所推行政策引发的日益增长的不满。这种不满主要针对军方的对华政策。社会大众党（Shakai Taishu-to）的分裂是反对军方对华政策的力量日益壮大的最新证据。因此，斋藤（Saito）的被开除并未平息国内日益增长的不满情绪。

“据军国主义圈子认为，强行筹备组建汪精卫‘政府’必须能够平息议会内外的不安。

“因此，南京方面的 staged staging（原文不清，意指 staged performance/作秀）以及对汪精卫运动‘成功’的大肆宣扬，不过是一道无效的烟幕弹，其背后掩盖的是日本国内局势日益严重的虚弱。”

若无日军支持
汪精卫无法立足

（合众社）
纽约，3月26日电。——《纽约每日新闻》今日在一篇社论中指出，由南京“国民党”领袖汪精卫先生领导的新南京“政府”，只有在日本军队的保护下才能存在。

这篇题为《叛徒汪精卫——日本在华傀儡》的社论称：

“中国本尼迪克特·阿诺德（Benedict Arnold，美国独立战争时期的叛将，此处喻指汉奸）的政府只有在日本刺刀的支持下才能维持。这就是为什么美国可以书写汪精卫故事的下一章。美国可以通过实施禁运，给日本侵略以沉重打击。”

MAY 27 1940

Britain Not Recognizing Wang Regime

(United Press)
LONDON, Mar. 26.—On the eve of the inauguration of the new “Chinese Central Government” at Nanking under Mr. Wang Ching-wei, the British Government will clearly indicate to Japan that Great Britain continues to regard Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek’s Chungking Government as the only legal Chinese national administration, reliable quarters said today.

The memorandum to Japan will also state that there will be no prospect of a change in such a British attitude in the immediate future, they added.

WANG KEH-MIN TO CONVENE MEETING
(Reuters)
PEIPING, Mar. 26.—Mr. Wang Keh-min, after his return to Peiping from Nanking, is expected to convene a meeting at which he will make a report on the “Central Political Conference,” and important matters relating to the North China “Political Council”—the body which is to take the place of the Peiping “Provisional Government.”

The dissolution of the Peiping “Provisional Government” is expected to be formally announced on March 30, and the “North China Political Council, it is expected, will come into existence on April 1.

Sources in close contract with the “Provisional Government” state it was decided at the Central Political Conference that Mr. Wang Keh-min, Chairman of the executive commission of the “Provisional Government,” should be appointed Chairman of the North China “Political Council,” and concurrently superintendent of the department of the interior. It had previously repeatedly been rumored locally that Mr. Wang Keh-min was to resign on the inauguration of the new “Central” regime.

Made Standing Member
Mr. Chu Shen, present minister of justice of the “Provisional Government,” will, it is further learned, be appointed a standing member of the North China “Political Council” and concurrently superintendent of the political affairs department.

Mr. Wang Shih-ching is expected to be appointed superintendent of the department of finance; General Chi Hsieh-yuan, superintendent of the Department of Pacification; Mr. Tang Erh-ho head of the department of education; Mr. Wang Yin-tai head of the department of industry; and Mr. Yin Tung head of the department of reconstruction.

The above-mentioned personnel, the same sources forecast, will be standing members of the North China “Political Council.”

General Chi Hsieh-yuan, it is also reported, will be commander-in-chief of the North China garrison headquarters, to be established in Peiping.

Other Names Given
Other members of the North China “Political Council,” it is stated, will be: Mr. Tung Kang, Mr. Wang I-tang, Mr. Su Ti-jen, Mr. Yu Ching-ho (the Mayor of Peiping), Mr. Chao Chi, Mr. Kiang Chao-tsung, Mr. Ma Liang and Mr. Fan Yu-kuei.

The Peiping office of the “United Council” of the “Provisional” and “Reformed Governments” was officially dissolved on March 22.

Direct telephone and wireless communication is to be established between Peiping and Nanking. A wireless office was opened in Peiping on March 22, and the telephone service, it is learned, will be put into operation in April.

PEIPING TO SEE OLD FLAG AGAIN
(Reuters)
PEIPING, Mar. 26.—The local police are reported to have notified various shops and stores in Peiping to have a “Sun in Blue Sky” flag made for use on April 1 on the occasion of the inauguration of the new “central government” at Nanking.

The new flag is similar to that used in Chungking, except for a small pennant at the top bearing four Chinese characters in red signifying anti-communism and peace.

All preparations have been completed in Peiping and Tientsin to celebrate the inauguration.

In Peiping, according to Chinese reports, posters will be placarded throughout the city, floral “Pai Lous” will be erected at different thoroughfares, and there will be a mass celebration.

In Tientsin, the same reports state, there will be a three-day program of festivities, which will include lantern and flag processions, mass celebrations in the auditorium of the Tientsin municipality, placarding of posters all over the city, and the holding of a reception for foreign Consuls.

1940年5月27日

英国不承认汪伪政权

（合众社）
伦敦，3月26日电。——据可靠方面今日称，在汪精卫先生于南京就任新的“中华民国中央政府”主席的前夕，英国政府将向日本明确表示，大不列颠继续视蒋介石委员长的重庆政府为唯一合法的中国国家行政机构。

他们补充说，致日本的备忘录还将声明，英国的这一态度在近期不会有任何改变的前景。

王克敏将召开会议
（路透社）
北平，3月26日电。——王克敏先生从南京返回北平后，预计将召开一次会议，在会上他将报告“中央政治会议”的情况，以及有关华北“政务委员会”的重要事项——该机构将取代北平“临时政府”。

预计将于3月30日正式宣布解散北平“临时政府”，而华北“政务委员会”预计将于4月1日成立。

与“临时政府”有密切联系的 sources 称，中央政治会议决定任命“临时政府”执行委员会主席王克敏先生为华北“政务委员会”委员长，并兼任内务总署督办。此前当地曾屡次传闻，王克敏先生将在新“中央”政权成立时辞职。

被任命为常务委员

另获悉，“临时政府”现任司法部长朱深先生将被任命为华北“政务委员会”常务委员，并兼任政务总署督办。

预计王士珍先生将被任命为财政总署督办；齐燮元将军被任命为绥靖总署督办；唐尔和被任命为教育总署督办；王荫泰被任命为实业总署督办；殷同被任命为建设总署督办。

同一消息来源预测，上述人员将成为华北“政务委员会”的常务委员。

另有报道指，齐燮元将军将担任将在北平设立的华北治安军总司令部司令官。

公布其他名单

据悉，华北“政务委员会”的其他成员包括：董康先生、王揖唐先生、苏体仁先生、余晋和先生（北平市市长）、赵琪先生、江朝宗先生、马良先生和范毓桂先生。

“临时政府”与“维新政府”的“联合委员会”北平办事处已于3月22日正式解散。

北平与南京之间将建立直接的电话和无线电通信。北平已于3月22日开设了一处无线电台，据悉，电话服务将于4月投入运营。

北平将再次见到旧旗帜
（路透社）
北平，3月26日电。——据报道，当地警方已通知北平各家商铺制作一面“青天白日”旗，以便在4月1日南京新“中央政府”成立之际使用。

新旗帜与重庆使用的旗帜相似，不同之处在于顶部有一面小三角旗，上面用红色写着四个汉字，象征“反共和平”。

北平和天津为庆祝成立仪式所做的各项准备工作均已就绪。

据中文报道称，在北平，全市将张贴海报，各主要街道将搭建花牌楼，并将举行群众庆祝活动。

同样的报道指出，在天津，将举行为期三天的庆祝活动，包括灯笼和旗帜游行、在天津市礼堂举行群众庆祝大会、在全市张贴海报，以及举行招待外国领事的活动。

二十八个同业公会
否认支持汪精卫

上海又有二十八个中国同业公会今日否认曾发表宣言支持汪精卫先生的“和平运动”。此前，汪精卫方面的《华中日报》声称，这些公会均已发出宣言，向新的中央政府效忠。

pages.en:
New Regime to Be
Installed Today

Ceremonies in Nanking
Prepared; Japanese Will
Issue Policy Statement

Nanking, Mar. 29.
Opening a new chapter in the
history of East Asia, the "National
Government of China" will be in-
augurated here tomorrow morning
when Mr. Wang Ching-wei and other
leading officials of the new administra-
tion will formally be installed at
elaborate ceremonies.
Ceremonies will get under way at
a special ceremony ground at 9
o'clock tomorrow morning with the
attendance of Mr. Wang Ching-wei
acting president of the "National
Government"; Mr. Chen Kung-po,
president of the Legislative Yuan,
Mr. Wen Chung-yao, president of the
Judicial Yuan, Mr. Liang Hung-chih,
president of the Control Yuan, Mr.
Wang I-tang, president of the
Examination Yuan, and 200 other
officials concerned.
Following the ceremonies, the new
central régime will issue a statement
declaring that it will henceforth re-
present the sovereignty of China,
taking the place of the China régime
and at the same time announcing its
political programme in which the
domestic and foreign policies of the
new administration will be clarified.
The dissolution of the Nanking
"Reformed Government," the Peiping
"Provisional Government" and their
liaison commission will also be an-
nounced tomorrow.—Domei.

Japanese Statement Prepared

Tokyo, Mar. 29.
A draft of a statement to be issued
by the Japanese Government clarify-
ing its fundamental policy towards
the reorganized "National Govern-
ment of China" under Mr. Wang
Ching-wei was approved today at a
meeting of the Cabinet.
The statement was expected to be
issued tomorrow night by Admiral
Mitsumasa Yonai, the Premier.
The Japanese Government will,
the statement, observers here said,
express its immutable decision to co-
operate with the new administration
and give positive assistance for its
sound development.
The statement will also request
the realization by third party Powers
of the new situation in East Asia,
observers believed.—Domei.

Precautions Intensified

Nanking, Mar. 29.
Mr. Fu Siao-en, "Mayor" of the
City Government of Greater Shang-
hai, is among the many Chinese and
Japanese officials who have arrived
here from Shanghai to attend the
inauguration of the new National
Government.
The inauguration ceremony, it is
understood, will comprise only of
oath-taking, after which Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, head of the new régime,
will make a speech to foreign cor-
respondents.
Meanwhile, there is not the slightest
sign of public excitement or en-
thusiasm here. This, however, may
be partially due to a steady down-
pour of rain.
Precautionary measures have been
intensified throughout the city, and
armed marching guards are stationed at
the city gates.
