pages.zh:
新政权将于今日成立

南京筹备典礼；日本将发表政策声明

南京，3月29日。
东亚历史翻开新篇章，“中华民国国民政府”将于明晨在此正式成立，汪精卫先生及新政府其他主要官员将在隆重的典礼上正式就职。
典礼将于明日上午9时在特设的典礼场地开始，出席者包括“国民政府”代主席汪精卫先生、立法院院长陈公博先生、司法院院长温宗尧先生、监察院院长梁鸿志先生、考试院院长王揖唐先生以及其他200名相关官员。
典礼结束后，新的中央政权将发表声明，宣称其从此代表中国主权，取代原有的中国政权，同时公布其政治纲领，阐明新政府的内外政策。
南京“维新政府”、北平“临时政府”及其联络委员会的解散也将于明日宣布。——同盟社

日本准备发表声明

东京，3月29日。
日本政府澄清其对汪精卫领导下改组后的“中华民国国民政府”基本政策的声明草案，于今日在内阁会议上获得批准。
据预计，该声明将由首相米内光政海军大将于明晚发表。
此间的观察家称，日本政府将在声明中表达其与新政权的合作决心不可动摇，并给予积极协助以促其健全发展。
观察家认为，该声明还将要求第三方列强承认东亚的新局势。——同盟社

加强戒备措施

南京，3月29日。
上海特别市“市长”傅筱庵先生是众多从上海抵达此处参加新国民政府成立典礼的中日官员之一。
据悉，成立典礼仅包括宣誓仪式，随后新政权首脑汪精卫先生将向外国记者发表讲话。
与此同时，此地公众情绪毫无激动或热情之迹象。不过，这在一定程度上可能是由于持续的大雨所致。
全市范围内的警戒措施已加强，武装巡逻卫兵驻守在各城门。

归档

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.

MAR 20 1940

Nanking Shows No Signs Of
Public Enthusiasm For Event

(Reuters)
NANKING, Mar. 29.—Mr. Fu
Siao-en, "Mayor" of the "City
Government of Greater Shanghai,"
is among the many Chinese and
Japanese officials who have arrived
here from Shanghai to attend the
inauguration of the new "National
Government."

The inauguration ceremony, it is
understood, will comprise only of
oath-taking, after which Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, head of the new regime,
will make a speech to foreign cor-
respondents.

Meanwhile, there is not the slight-
est sign of public excitement or
enthusiasm here. This, however,
may be partially due to a steady
downpour of rain.

Precautionary measures have been
intensified throughout the city, and
strict searching is being enforced
at the city gates.

WANG, YONAI TO
BROADCAST SPEECHES
(China News Agency)
NANKING, Mar. 29.—On the
occasion of the return of the Na-
tional Government to its capital,
Mr. Wang Ching-wei will broadcast
a speech at 6.30 p.m. tomorrow and
this will be immediately followed by
another broadcast by Admiral Yonai,
Japanese Premier. Later in the
evening, at 9 p.m., Mr. Chen Kung-
po will also speak over the radio.

《字林西报》。

1940年3月20日

南京未显现出民众对该事件的热情

（路透社）
南京，3月29日电——“大上海市政府”“市长”傅筱庵先生，是众多从上海抵达此处参加新“国民政府”就职典礼的中日官员之一。

据悉，就职典礼仅包括宣誓仪式，随后新政权的头目汪精卫先生将向外国记者发表讲话。

与此同时，此地丝毫未见公众的兴奋或热情。不过，这可能部分归因于持续的倾盆大雨。

全市已加强预防措施，并在城门实施严格搜查。

汪精卫、米内将发表广播演说
（中国新闻社）
南京，3月29日电——值此国民政府还都之际，汪精卫先生将于明日下午6时30分发表广播演说，随后日本首相米内光政海军上将也将立即发表广播演说。当晚稍后，即晚上9时，陈公博先生亦将通过无线电发表讲话。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

O 1040

Fireworks Display in
Pootung Tonight

Celebration of New Nanking
Regime by Ta Min Hui

A fireworks display will be staged
between 4 o'clock this afternoon and
9 o'clock tonight by the Ta Min Hui
on the Pootung side of the Whangpoo
in celebration of the reorganized
National Government at Nanking,
local Chinese authorities announced
yesterday.

Foreigners and others will be able
to witness the display from the Bund,
it was stated. The exhibition will
reach a climax about 8 o'clock tonight
when fireworks depicting six Chinese
characters "Kuo Min Cheng Fu Huan
Tu," meaning "Celebrating the return
of the National Government to its
capital," will egnited.

Similar fireworks displays will be
staged in Hangchow and Soochow to-
night under the auspices of the Ta
Min Hui in those places.

《字林西报》。

O 1040

浦东今晚燃放烟花

大民会庆祝南京新政权

据当地中国当局昨日宣布，为庆祝南京改组后的国民政府，大民会将于今日下午4时至晚间9时，在黄浦江浦东一侧举行烟花表演。

据悉，外国人及其他人士可从外滩观看此次表演。今晚8时许，表演将达到高潮，届时将点燃拼出六个汉字“国民政府还都”（意为“庆祝国民政府返回首都”）的烟花。

今晚，在杭州和苏州，也将由当地的大民会主办类似的烟花表演。

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS
1940

Inauguration
Train Derailed
Near Nanking

(United Press)
NANKING, Mar. 29.—The inauguration of the new Government here tomorrow was almost marred tonight when the “inauguration express,” packed with high Japanese and Chinese officials and foreign correspondents, was derailed at 7.20 o’clock within sight of the lights of Nanking.
The last express from Shanghai for the inauguration was slowing down near Nanking when suddenly the locomotive and three third class coaches, which were jammed with Chinese who even stood in the aisles, jumped the rails. The locomotive and the three coaches were partially overturned, but no one was injured seriously. Numerous Chinese were shaken and bruised, but none required hospital attention.

Faulty Repairs
The derailing of the train was blamed on faulty repairs to a portion of the tracks. Railway officials said that the accident occurred at a point at which repair gangs worked this morning. The defective tracks apparently were not fully repaired, the officials said.
The six remaining upright coaches, which carried the Japanese and Chinese officials and the foreign correspondents, were shunted to another track. A new locomotive was pressed into service and the express reached Nanking at 9 p.m., 80 minutes late. It was raining as the train drew into the station.

NEWSMEN LEAVE
FOR INAUGURATION
“Mayor” Fu Siao-en of the ‘City Government of Shanghai’ departed from the North Station yesterday morning aboard the same train taken by a number of foreign newspaper correspondents who will view the inauguration ceremonies of the new Nanking regime today.
The “Mayor” will return to his bailiwick this evening or tomorrow morning, according to his office staff here.
Among the newsmen making the train trip were Messrs: Eric Mayell of Fox Movietone, Douglas Robertson, the New York Times, V. Galimberti, Steffani News Service and Mrs. George Lacks, news photographer. Other American correspondents traveled to Nanking by plane.

pages.zh:
《字林西报》
1940年

就职典礼前夕
南京附近发生列车脱轨事故

（合众社）
南京，3月29日电——明日在此间举行的新政府就职典礼险些因今晚发生的意外而蒙上阴影。载满日本和中国高官以及外国记者的“就职典礼专列”于7时20分在南京灯火可见的范围内发生脱轨。

这班从上海开往南京参加就职典礼的末班特快列车在接近南京时正在减速，突然，机车和三节挤满了中国乘客（甚至过道上都站满了人）的三等车厢冲出轨道。机车和三节车厢部分倾覆，但无人受重伤。许多中国人受到惊吓并出现挫伤，但均无需送医治疗。

维修不当
此次列车脱轨事故被归咎于部分铁轨维修不当。铁路官员称，事故发生在今天上午维修班组作业过的地点。官员们表示，受损铁轨显然未得到彻底修复。

载有日本和中国官员及外国记者的其余六节直立车厢被转辙至另一条轨道。一辆新的机车被紧急投入使用，该特快列车于晚上9点抵达南京，晚点80分钟。列车进站时正下着雨。

记者启程
前往参加就职典礼

“上海市政府”“市长”傅筱庵昨晨在北火车站登上同一列火车，同行的还有数名外国报社记者，他们将观摩今日南京新政权的就职典礼仪式。

据其在此间的办公人员称，“市长”将于今晚或明晨返回其管辖区域。

乘坐此次列车前往的记者包括：福克斯电影新闻片的埃里克·梅耶尔（Eric Mayell）先生、《纽约时报》的道格拉斯·罗伯逊（Douglas Robertson）、斯特法尼新闻社的V. 加利姆贝蒂（V. Galimberti）以及新闻摄影师乔治·拉克斯（George Lacks）夫人。其他美国记者则乘飞机前往南京。

归档

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS
MAR 30 1940

City Guarded
As Wang
Regime Due

Barbed wire barricades were erected on S.M.P. orders at all important street exits of the International Settlement last night to forestall possible public disturbances in connection with the inauguration of the Wang Ching-wei regime in Nanking today.

Police authorities, interviewed by The CHINA PRESS last night stated that the precautionary measures would continue possibly for two or three days and would be discontinued whenever the situation so justified.

In addition to the barbed wire barricades, Settlement police, aided by foreign defense forces here and the Russian Regiment of the S.V.C., will conduct searches of pedestrians at the exits as well as the busier sections of the city.

French Concession authorities last night also put up barriers along Avenue Edward VII and Avenue Foch. The French Police Force will conduct rigid searches throughout today.

Trouble Not Expected

Police did not believe there would be any extensive trouble as the city was very quiet yesterday.

While authorities here last night were taking full precautions against terrorist outbreaks on the occasion of the "inauguration" Chinese quarters in the foreign-controlled areas continued to manifest contempt for the new regime.

"Just another so-called 'government' being brought into being" was the consensus of responsible business and cultural leaders in Shanghai who for obvious reasons preferred to remain anonymous.

In direct response to "threatening" appeals of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's clique in Shanghai that classes be suspended today when the new regime will be inaugurated, school authorities loyal to the National Government decided that the spring vacation of schools here would begin yesterday and continue until the "crisis" is over.

Strike Not Confirmed

Reports that students in local school would declare a "go-slow" strike tomorrow could not be confirmed in local educational quarters. It was pointed out that while remaining loyal to the government, schools here wish to avoid all dealings with the Wang regime either by observing its instructions or disobeying them.

The same quarters stated that despite the puppet official's ambitious program of winning the students in Shanghai to his cause, by far the majority of the Chinese youth here may well be branded "loyalists." "Money means very little to them," a veteran teacher...

fevor stated, "although 80 per cent of them may be classified as destitute."

"Professors" Act

It was reported yesterday that for several days this week, a self-styled "College Professors' Association," consisting of a handful of men who had once taught school in Shanghai, had been active among student circles in a last-minute effort to get them to stage demonstrations on "inauguration day." Responsible quarters predicted last night no such gatherings would take place in the Settlement or Concession.

Wang's agents here were reported to have fared no better in their solicitation of the support of the Shanghai businessmen. Even backers of Mr. Wang's "peace" move will hesitate to show their sympathies to the new regime in the foreign controlled area, it was stated.

A loyalist businessman pointed out that even if Mr. Wang's agents had been successful, they would be unable to circumvent the S.M.C. and F.M.C. regulations against unlicensed large gatherings and the modus operandi governing the hoisting of the Chinese flag.

Leaflets Distributed

Although no mass meetings were reported to have been held yesterday, thousands of loyalist leaflets were showered on the pedestrians from the roof gardens of the department stores in the downtown district. Printed in many colors, the leaflets urged the public to "Strike down the traitors; remain loyal to the government."

Several trucks were seen yesterday cruising around the main thoroughfares distributing leaflets in support of Mr. Wang's "government." "Peace and construction," some of the leaflets said, "will be the foundation stone of the government."

Mass gatherings, however, were scheduled to be held in many parts of Hongkew, Chapel, Pootung and the surrounding districts under Japanese occupation. Large detachments of Japanese gendarmes and "Special Municipality" police were said to have been mobilized to protect the demonstrators. All schools in those areas will close today while business establishments were "requested" to buy and display Chinese banners together with their yellow pennants as adopted by Mr. Wang's "Central Political Council."

Japanese To Hoist Flag

Japanese authorities in Shanghai, according to the Mainichi, have ordered the hoisting of the Japanese flag today to mark the "return of the national government to Nanking." This move was decided upon at a conference between representatives of the Foreign Office, War Office, Navy Office and the Asia Development Board "for the sake of the establishment of the new order in East Asia and the promotion of friendship between Japan and China."

Dancing partners in the employ of a cabaret in Hongkew were reported by the Tairoku Shimpo busily engaged in preparing to hoist a balloon over the Joint Savings Bank godown near the Yu Ya Ching Road bridge. The balloon will bear the inscription "Celebration of the return of the National Government to Nanking," it was stated.

FILED
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》
1940年3月30日

因汪伪政权即将成立
全市加强警戒

昨夜，为防范今日南京汪精卫政权“就职”可能引发的公众骚乱，工部局下令在国际租界所有主要街道出口处架设铁丝网路障。

《大美晚报》记者昨晚采访警方当局时获悉，这些预防措施可能会持续两三天，一旦局势允许即行撤销。

除铁丝网路障外，租界巡捕将在本地外国防卫部队及上海万国商团俄籍支队的协助下，在各出口及市内较繁忙地段对行人进行搜查。

法租界当局昨晚也在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）和福煦路（Avenue Foch）沿线设置了路障。法国巡捕房将于今日全天进行严格搜查。

预计不会发生骚乱

警方认为不会发生大规模骚乱，因为昨日全市非常平静。

尽管本地当局昨晚针对此次“就职”期间可能发生的恐怖活动采取了充分预防措施，但外国控制区域内的华人社区继续表现出对新政权的蔑视。

上海一些负责任的商界和文化界领袖（出于显而易见的原因要求匿名）普遍认为，这不过是又一个所谓的“政府”粉墨登场而已。

针对汪精卫集团在上海发出的“威胁性”呼吁——要求在今日新政权“就职”时停课——忠于国民政府的学校当局决定，本地学校的春假从昨日开始，直至“危机”结束。

罢工消息未经证实

本地教育界人士无法证实有关本地学校学生将于明日举行“怠工”罢课的报道。有人指出，虽然学校方面保持对政府的忠诚，但希望避免通过遵守或违抗其指令的方式与汪伪政权发生任何关联。

同一消息来源表示，尽管这名傀儡官员野心勃勃地试图争取上海学生支持其事业，但绝大多数本地中国青年仍可被标记为“忠义之士”。一位资深教师……

表示：“金钱对他们来说意义不大，尽管其中80%的人可被归类为贫困阶层。”

“教授们”的行动

据昨日报道，本周数日以来，一个自称为“大学教授协会”的组织（由少数曾在上海任教的人员组成）在学生圈中积极活动，做最后努力企图煽动学生在“就职日”举行示威。负责任的消息来源昨晚预测，在租界或法租界内不会发生此类集会。

据报道，汪氏代理人在此间争取上海商人支持的努力也未获成功。据悉，即使是支持汪先生“和平”运动的人士，在外国控制区域内也会犹豫是否公开表达对新政权的同情。

一位忠义商界人士指出，即使汪氏代理人取得成功，他们也无法绕过工部局和公董局关于禁止未经许可的大型集会以及悬挂中国国旗相关操作规定的条例。

散发传单

虽然昨日未报告举行大规模集会，但在市中心百货公司的屋顶花园，成千上万份忠义传单如雨点般撒向行人。这些传单彩色印刷，呼吁公众“打倒汉奸；忠于政府”。

昨日可见数辆卡车在主要干道巡游，分发支持汪氏“政府”的传单。部分传单称，“和平与建设”将是该政府的基石。

然而，在虹口、闸北、浦东及周边日军占领区的许多地方，计划举行大规模集会。据悉，大批日本宪兵和“特别市”警察已动员起来保护示威者。这些地区的所有学校今日将停课，商家则被“要求”购买并展示中国旗帜，以及汪氏“中央政治委员会”采用的黄色三角旗。

日本人将悬挂旗帜

据《每日新闻》报道，上海日本当局已下令今日悬挂日本国旗，以纪念“国民政府还都南京”。此举是在外务省、陆军省、海军省和兴亚院代表之间的会议上决定的，目的是“为了建立东亚新秩序及促进日中友好”。

据《泰罗克辛报》（Tairoku Shimpo）报道，虹口一家歌舞厅雇佣的舞伴们正忙于准备在靠近虞洽卿路桥的联合储蓄银行仓库上空升起一只气球。据悉，气球上将印有“庆祝国民政府还都南京”的字样。

归档

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES

MAR 20 1940

Authorities
Plan Local
Precautions

Barricades To Be Placed
On Boundaries; Troops
To Aid The Police

Having commenced with special
searches all over the International
Settlement and the French Conces-
sion from 6 o'clock yesterday
evening the police of the two for-
eign areas will remain on stand-by
orders all day to-day to prevent any
untoward incidents in connection
with the inauguration at Nanking to-
day of the Reorganized National
Government of China.

Precautions in the city to-day will
be the same as carried out on Jan-
uary 28, the anniversary of the out-
break of the 1932 hostilities. Barb-
ed wire barricades were erected at
all boundaries as from midnight last
night and intensive police searches
at intersections will be carried out
throughout the day.

As on former occasions the vari-
ous foreign military forces in
Shanghai will co-operate with the
police in maintaining law and order
in the city. Sentries will be placed
at various intersections and patrols
of Seaforth Highlanders, East Sur-
reys, U.S. Marines and the Italian
Marines will operate in their respec-

1940年3月20日

当局
筹划本地
防范措施

边界将设置路障；军队
将协助警察

自昨晚6时起，公共租界与法租界这两个外侨区域已在全境展开特别搜查，两地警方今日全天处于待命状态，以防因今日在南京成立的中国国民政府（改组）而引发任何意外事件。

今日市内的防范措施将与1月28日（即1932年战事爆发周年纪念日）所采取的措施相同。自昨夜午夜起，所有边界均已架设铁丝网路障，全天将在各十字路口进行密集的警察搜查。

与以往一样，驻沪各外国军队将与警方合作，维持市内治安。哨兵将部署于各个十字路口，海福尔高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）、东萨里郡团（East Surreys）、美国海军陆战队以及意大利海军陆战队的巡逻队将在各自防区内执行任务。

上海公共租界工部局警务处特务队（S.M.P. Specials）与上海义勇队（S.V.C.）也将配合此次动员。上海义勇队俄国分队的成员将提供特别警卫，并将乘坐卡车进行巡逻。

上海公共租界工部局警务处全体警员自昨日下午6时起即处于待命状态。

Political Platform
Of New Regime

Forecast of Proposed New
Government Policies Made
By Japanese Agency

Nanking, Mar. 28.
A political programme, believed to embrace seven major points, of the reorganized "National Government of China" will be announced on Saturday, it was learned here today.
The reorganized "National Government" will officially come into existence on that day and the formal appointment of the presidents of the five yuans as well as state ministers will be officially announced.
Later in the day the inaugural meeting of the Cabinet will be held at which a draft of the platform will be discussed and approved.
Although the nature of the platform had not been revealed, observers here predicted today that it would emphasize seven major points:

Seven Principle Points

1. To place the right men in the right places in the organization of the reorganized government.
2. The achievement of national unity by abolishing the one-party dictatorship.
3. The speedy enforcement of Constitutional Government and the Convocation of the National Assembly.
4. To assure the lessening of the burden of the people and granting of relief to sufferers.
5. To insure the independence of China, everlasting peace in East Asia and to share in the responsibility for the establishment of a new order in East Asia.
6. To respect the legitimate interests and rights of third party Powers and to cement friendly relations with Foreign countries.
7. To invite to China Foreign capital necessary for the economic reconstruction of China.—Domei.

Tokyo Support Pledged

Tokyo, Mar. 28.
The Japanese Government will issue a statement either on Saturday or Sunday clarifying its fundamental policy vis-à-vis the reorganized "National Government of China."
The Japanese Government will in the statement, observers here said, pledge its wholehearted support to the new administration and emphasize its fundamental policy of co-operating with the Nanking administration in establishing a new order in East Asia to ensure everlasting peace.

Foreign Relations

The statement was expected to refer to the international position of the reorganized "National Government" and its relations with the third-party nations.
The Premier, Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai, yesterday conferred with Gen. Shunroku Hata, War Minister, on the matter, while Mr. Hisatada Hirose, director of the Cabinet's Legislative Bureau, Mr. Sotaro Ishiwata, chief secretary of the Cabinet, and Maj.-Gen. Teiichi Suzuki, director of the Political Affairs Bureau of the Asia Development Board, worked on a draft of the statement at the Premier's official residence.—Domei.

新政权的政治纲领

日本机构对拟议中的新政府政策的预测

南京，3月28日。
据今日在此间获悉，改组后的“中华民国国民政府”的政治纲领（据悉包含七大要点）将于星期六公布。
改组后的“国民政府”将于当日正式成立，五院院长及国务大臣的正式任命也将同时官方宣布。
当日晚些时候将举行内阁就职会议，讨论并批准纲领草案。
尽管纲领的具体性质尚未披露，但此间的观察家今日预测，它将强调以下七个主要方面：

七项原则要点

1. 在改组政府的组织架构中，做到人尽其才、任人唯贤。
2. 通过废除一党专政，实现国家统一。
3. 迅速实施宪政，并召开国民大会。
4. 确保减轻民众负担，并对受灾者提供救济。
5. 保障中国独立、东亚永久和平，并分担建立东亚新秩序的责任。
6. 尊重第三国列强的合法利益与权利，并巩固与外国的友好关系。
7. 邀请对中国之经济重建所必需的外国资本进入中国。——同盟社

东京承诺支持

东京，3月28日。
日本政府将于星期六或星期日发表声明，阐明其对改组后的“中华民国国民政府”的基本政策。
此间的观察家称，日本政府将在该声明中承诺全力支持新政府，并强调其与南京政府在建立东亚新秩序以确保永久和平方面进行合作的基本政策。

对外关系

预计该声明将提及改组后的“国民政府”的国际地位及其与第三国之间的关系。
米内光政海军大将首相昨日就此事与陆军大臣畑俊六将军进行了磋商，而内阁法制局长广濑久忠先生、内阁官房长官石渡宗太郎先生以及兴亚院政务部长铃木贞一少将则在首相官邸起草该声明。——同盟社

CHINA PRESS
1940

Lin Sen Flays Wang
In Broadcast
President Declares
China To Fight On
Until Goal Reached

(United Press)
CHUNGKING, Mar. 29.—Branding Mr. Wang Ching-wei, head of the Kuomintang at Nanking, a “traitor under death sentence” and urging all responsible Government organizations to arrest the leader of the Nanking regime, Mr. Lin Sen, President of the Chinese National Government, tonight told the Chinese nation and overseas Chinese that China would continue to struggle to protect her national integrity.

Broadcasting over Chungking’s powerful short-wave station at 7 o’clock tonight, Mr. Lin said he was “decidedly” going to continue leading all Chinese, civil and military, to “ultimate victory.”

President Lin Sen’s speech was his first personal public rejection of his election to the Presidency of the “New” Government at Nanking. Official quarters pointed out that during the Central Political Conference at Nanking last week, Mr. Wang Ching-wei was elected acting President of the Nanking regime pending Mr. Lin Sen’s return to Nanking.

“As long as our goal is not reached,” President Lin declared, “our struggle will not cease. Wang Ching-wei has violated the second article of the Kuomintang’s regulations governing the punishment of traitors (death). His is a regular criminal case and all responsible organizations under the National Government must do their utmost to arrest Wang and have him taken to Chungking for strict punishment in accordance with the fixed rules.”

Pointing out that the present status of the Sino-Japanese conflict was extremely important to China, Mr. Lin Sen said that “unfortunately a few traitors, including Wang Ching-wei, have emerged and are being utilized by the Japanese.”

“Under Cover Of Peace”
“Under the cover of peace,” the National leader said, “these traitors have surrendered and are carrying on a large scale rebellion. Wang Ching-wei is illegally using all the original titles of the party and the government in executing his dangerous designs. He is even attempting to succeed the legitimate government in order to mislead the world.

“The Japanese are merely using Wang as a temporary tool to conduct continual aggression in a different style.

“The facts show that the enemy’s military forces are reaching a point of exhaustion. The utilization of traitors signifies Japan’s plan to get help in her final struggles.

“I am chairman of the National Government and I am entrusted by the entire Kuomintang and nation to carry out my duties. I am absolutely consistent in my mind.

“From beginning to end, I have one heart and one determination and act in accordance with the Kuomintang’s General Chiang Kai-shek.

“I am decidedly going to lead the entire nation in our struggle for the protection of our integral independence and the freedom of our national state. As long as this goal is not reached we will not halt our fight.”

China’s Ability Stressed
President Lin Sen told the nation, overseas Chinese and all “friendly powers” that China had the ability to secure her self-existence and self-prosperity.

“China,” he said, “also has the ability to secure her co-existence and co-prosperity with all nations treating her on an equal basis.

“For the past 30 months we have struggled under extreme hardships. I hope friendly powers will give us their sympathy and assistance. We always reciprocate these powers with interest and mutual benefits in order to achieve equality and freedom for all the human race.

“Our eventual victory is not distant, because of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek’s exploits.

“Every citizen must fulfill his duties and guard his post. We must unite with one single mind and strongly stick to our stand of resistance and destroy all traitors.”

The National Government’s President warned all Chinese “never to forget the territories that have fallen into Japanese hands.”

“We must struggle for their early recovery,” Mr. Lin declared, “and we must do our utmost to save our brothers and sisters suffering in hot fire and deep water in the occupied zones.

“This great task does not allow the slightest hesitation. All of us must fight onward hand in hand,” President Lin Sen concluded.

Lin Addresses Kuomintang

林森在广播中痛斥汪精卫
总统宣布中国将战斗直至达成目标

（合众社）
重庆，3月29日电。——中华民国国民政府主席林森先生今晚向全国同胞及海外华侨表示，中国将继续奋斗以维护国家完整。林森主席称南京国民党头目汪精卫先生为“判处死刑之叛徒”，并敦促所有负责的政府机构逮捕南京政权领导人。

林森先生今晚七时通过重庆强力短波电台发表广播讲话，称他“坚决”将继续领导全体文武同胞，直至取得“最后胜利”。

林森主席的此次讲话，是他首次以个人身份公开拒绝接受在南京“新”政府当选主席一事。官方人士指出，在上周南京召开的中央政治会议上，汪精卫先生被选为南京政权代主席，以待林森先生返回南京。

林森主席宣称：“只要我们的目标尚未达成，我们的斗争就不会停止。汪精卫违反了国民党惩治汉奸条例第二条（死刑）。这是一起普通的刑事案件，国民政府下属各负责机构必须竭尽全力逮捕汪精卫，并将其押解至重庆，依照既定规章严加惩办。”

林森主席指出，目前中日冲突的局势对中国极为重要，他说：“不幸的是，包括汪精卫在内的一小撮叛徒已经出现，并正被日本人所利用。”

“和平掩护下”
这位国家领袖说：“在‘和平’的掩护下，这些叛徒已投降并进行大规模叛乱。汪精卫非法使用党与政府的所有原有头衔，以实施其危险图谋。他甚至企图取代合法政府，以迷惑世界舆论。

“日本人 merely 将汪精卫作为临时工具，以不同形式继续进行侵略。

“事实表明，敌军的军事力量已接近枯竭。利用叛徒意味着日本计划在其最后挣扎中寻求援助。

“我是国民政府主席，受整个国民党及国民托付以履行职责。我的意志绝对坚定。

“自始至终，我同心同德，遵循国民党总裁蒋介石将军的行动方针。

“我决心领导全国同胞，为保护我们完整的独立和国家自由而斗争。只要这一目标尚未达成，我们就不会停止战斗。”

强调中国之能力
林森主席向全国同胞、海外华侨及所有“友好列强”表示，中国有能力确保自身的生存与繁荣。

他说：“中国也有能力确保与所有以平等地位对待中国的国家共存共荣。

“在过去三十个月里，我们在极端艰难困苦中奋斗。我希望友好列强能给予我们同情与援助。我们始终以互利互惠回报这些国家，以实现全人类的平等与自由。

“由于蒋中正总司令的功绩，我们的最终胜利为期不远。

“每位公民必须恪尽职守，坚守岗位。我们必须万众一心， firmly 坚持抵抗立场，消灭所有叛徒。”

国民政府主席警告全体中国人“切勿忘记已沦入日寇手中的领土”。

林森宣称：“我们必须为早日收复这些领土而奋斗，必须竭尽全力拯救在占领区水深火热中受苦的兄弟姐妹。

“这项伟大任务不容丝毫犹豫。我们所有人都必须携手并肩，继续战斗，”林森主席最后说道。

林森对国民党发表讲话
与此同时，林森主席在今早于本地国民党总部举行的纪念仪式上，面对与会的政府领导人发表了讲话，随后才进行了上述广播。

the 72 martyrs killed in action in Canton prior to the founding of the Chinese Republic.

In his first speech today, Mr. Lin said that China "must continue the holy task left us by our martyrs—the revolution for China's freedom and independence.

"We must employ the same perseverance and the same determination the martyrs used in routing the Imperial Manchus," he declared.

"We must rout the Imperial Japanese and create a real, free and prosperous China. All of us must do our best to destroy the enemy's political intrigues, and recover lost territory," the Chinese President stated.

Broadcast Considered Important
National Government circles considered Mr. Lin Sen's second speech today over the shortwave radio as an "important" historic document unfolding Chungking's exact stand regarding Wang Ching-wei."

Official quarters interpreted the President's broadcast as a "manifesto to the world telling all nations what free China's masses and political parties think of the Wang Ching-wei regime."

"President Lin Sen's second speech represented China's permanent mind, which is unalterable by any circumstances," these circles said.

CHINESE LEADERS
TO DENOUNCE WANG

(Reuters)
CHUNGKING, Mar. 29.—For two weeks, commencing today, the Central Broadcasting Station here will feature speeches by prominent leaders of the Chinese Government, denouncing Mr. Wang Ching-wei's new government.

The speakers will include, Mr. Lin Sen, Chairman of the National Government, Mr. Sun Fo, President of the Legislative Yuan, Mr. Tai Chi-tao, President of the Examina-

tion Yuan, Mr. Yu Yu-jen, President of the Control Yuan, Mr. Chi Cheng, President of the Judicial Yuan, Mr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance, General Ho Ying-ch'in, Minister of War, and Madame Feng Yu-hsiang, the wife of General Feng Yu-hsiang, the "Christian General."

PAI SAYS JAPANESE
BOUND TO FAIL

(United Press)
CHUNGKING, Mar. 29.—General Pai Chung-hsi, leader of China's southwest forces, in an article today in memory of the 1910 Canton uprising, urged strict adherence to "China's strategy of prolonged resistance" and scored the "Japanese policy of making Chinese fight Chinese."

"The enemy's policy of making Chinese fight Chinese and force occupied areas to finance their war of aggression is bound to fail," General Pai declared.

EFFIGIES OF WANG
AND WIFE BURNED

(United Press)
CHUNGKING, Mar. 29.—Kneeling effigies of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, leader of the Nanking "Kuomintang," and his wife were burned here this morning before a mass meeting of 2,000 persons.

Mr. Chang Chi, veteran Kuomintang leader, presided over the "Traitor burning ceremony." Barrels of kerosene were poured over the wood and straw figures after which they were set afire. Mr. Chang smiled when the crowd clapped their hands as the fire destroyed the effigies.

The meeting, commemorating the death of the 72 martyrs of the Canton uprising, was held in the square which was formerly the site of Chungking's business center, but which was reduced to the ground during Japanese bombing raids last May.

在中华民国成立之前于广州阵亡的七十二烈士。

林森先生在今日的首次演讲中表示，中国“必须继续先烈留给我们的神圣任务——为中国的自由与独立而革命。

“我们必须运用先烈在驱逐满清帝制时所用的同样毅力和决心，”他宣称。

“我们必须驱逐日本帝国主义，建立一个真正、自由且繁荣的中国。我们所有人都必须竭尽全力破坏敌人的政治阴谋，并收复失地，”这位中国国家主席 stated。

广播被视为重要事项

国民政府人士认为，林森先生今日通过短波无线电发表的第二篇演讲是一份“重要的”历史文件，阐明了重庆方面关于汪精卫的确切立场。”

官方人士将总统的广播解读为“一份向全世界发表的宣言，告知各国自由中国的民众和各政党如何看待汪精卫政权。”

这些人士称：“林森主席的第二篇演讲代表了中国不可动摇的永久意志，任何情况都无法改变。”

中国领导人
将谴责汪精卫

（路透社）
重庆，3月29日。—从今天起的两周内，这里的中央广播电台将播发中国政府著名领导人的演讲，谴责汪精卫先生的新政府。

演讲者包括：国民政府主席林森先生、立法院院长孙科先生、考试院院长戴季陶先生、监察院院长于右任先生、司法院院长居正先生、财政部长孔祥熙先生、军政部长何应钦将军，以及“基督将军”冯玉祥将军的夫人冯玉祥夫人。

白崇禧称日本
注定失败

（合众社）
重庆，3月29日。—中国西南部队领导人白崇禧将军在今日纪念1910年广州起义的一篇文章中，敦促严格坚持“中国的持久抵抗战略”，并抨击“日本人让中国人打中国人的政策”。

白将军宣称：“敌人让中国人打中国人、并强迫占领区为其侵略战争提供资金的政策注定要失败。”

汪精卫及其夫人
的偶像被焚毁

（合众社）
重庆，3月29日。—今天上午，在南京“国民党”领导人汪精卫先生及其夫人的跪姿偶像在2000人的群众大会前被焚毁。

资深国民党领导人张继先生主持了“焚烧汉奸仪式”。在向木制和草扎的人像倾倒数桶煤油后，将其点燃。当人群在火焰吞噬偶像时鼓掌，张先生露出了微笑。

这次纪念广州起义七十二烈士殉难的集会，是在一个广场上举行的，该广场曾是重庆的商业中心所在地，但在去年五月的日本轰炸袭击中被夷为平地。

Anti-Wang Papers
Distributed Here

But Stringent Measures
Are Taken by Authorities
To Prevent Trouble

As a reaction to the widely-pub-
licized official establishment of a new
central régime under the guidance
of Mr. Wang Ching-wei at Nanking
today, slips printed in Chinese at-
tacking the scheme were distributed
in Shanghai yesterday afternoon and
evening, asking shops and factories
to close today. The rain last night
was credited with helping to prevent
overt demonstrations against the
Nanking project.

Yesterday, national flags were half-
masted generally in the Internation-
al Settlement, south of the Soochow
Creek, and the French Concession in
commemoration of the 72 Kuomintang
revolutionary martyrs of Canton, a
memorial day observed by the Chung-
king Government.

Elaborate Precautions

Special precautions are being taken
today by the police and military
throughout Shanghai. The Settle-
ment and the French Police will con-
duct innumerable searches for arms,
visit places suspected of harbouring
criminals and trouble-makers, and
strictly enforce the curfew law. The
precautions are similar to those taken
on all the important political an-
niversaries in Shanghai.

The Settlement Police were stand-
ing-by from 6 o'clock yesterday
evening. At the same time the
elaborate machinery of control
started to function, with many streets
and lanes being closed and barbed-
wire barricades being erected gen-
erally at strategic points. Search
parties started to function at import-
ant crossings, particularly along
Avenue Edward VII, and on the
bridges over the Soochow Creek.
Special patrols, in cars and on foot,

were seen in the streets, and many
houses were visited by detectives
who rounded-up scores of suspects
for investigation and finger-printing.
The red vans of the Reserve Unit
were standing-by at Lotza and
Gordon Road Stations.

Besides patrols provided by the
Russian Regiment, S.V.C., there will
be "stand-by" today for some of the
volunteer units of the Corps as well
as the Police Specials.

It is reported in Chinese quarters
that a Chinese aeroplane is expected
to fly from Nanking to Shanghai
today to distribute coloured leaflets
in celebration of the establishment
of the new central government at
Nanking by Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
Elaborate preparations are reported
to have been made by Mr. Wang's
supporters in Shanghai for celebrat-
ing the occasion.

Public Bodies Invited

A local celebration meeting will be
held in the morning in the western
district under the auspices of Kuo-
mintang officials under Mr. Wang.
It is reported that public bodies have
been asked to send representatives
to the meeting and that many shops
have been urged to display celebra-
tion posters in their show windows.
Handbills are expected to be dis-
tributed in streets and from the
plane.

Mr. Wang's organ, the "Central
China Daily News," reports that
Chinese factories will sound sirens
and foreign war vessels on the
Whangpoo will fire salutes." The
report adds that all Chinese schools
will be closed for the day and that
the pupils will attend meetings cele-
brating the beginning of the new
régime. The pro-Government section
of the Chinese press, however, re-
ports an entirely different spirit
amongst the majority of the local
students. It announces that a "tai-
kung" ("go slow") strike is contem-
plated by the young men in protest
against the Wang movement. Which-
ever may be the case, it remains a
fact that many Chinese schools here
are already closed for spring vaca-
tion and that, therefore, it would be
difficult to consider the student issue
a live one at this moment.

反汪传单
在此分发

但当局采取严厉措施
以防生乱

作为对今日在南京于汪精卫先生指导下正式成立新中央政权的广泛报道的反应，昨天下午和晚间，上海分发了印有中文的攻击该计划的传单，呼吁商店和工厂今日停业。昨夜的雨水被认为有助于防止针对南京计划的公开示威活动。

昨日，为纪念广州七十二位国民党革命烈士——这是重庆政府遵守的纪念日——苏州河以南的国际公共租界及法租界普遍下半旗致哀。

周密预防措施

今日，上海各地的警察和军队正在采取特别预防措施。公共租界巡捕房和法租界巡捕房将进行无数次武器搜查，走访涉嫌窝藏罪犯和滋事分子的场所，并严格执行宵禁法。这些预防措施与上海在所有重要政治纪念日所采取的措施类似。

公共租界巡捕房从昨晚六点起便处于待命状态。与此同时，严密的管控机制开始运作，许多街道和弄堂被封闭，并在战略要点普遍架设铁丝网路障。搜查队开始在主要路口展开行动，特别是沿着爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）以及苏州河上的桥梁。街上可见汽车和步行的特别巡逻队，许多住宅遭到侦探探访，他们逮捕了数十名嫌疑人进行调查和采集指纹。后备队的红色厢式车在罗塔路（Lotza Road）和戈登路（Gordon Road）巡捕房待命。

除了由俄国团和上海义勇队（S.V.C.）提供的巡逻外，今日义勇队的一些志愿分队以及警察特别队也将处于“待命”状态。

据中方人士报告，预计今日将有一架中国飞机从南京飞抵上海，散发彩色传单，以庆祝汪精卫先生在南京建立新中央政府。据报道，汪先生的支持者在上海已为庆祝这一场合做了周密准备。

邀请公共团体参加

上午，将在西区举行当地庆祝集会，由汪先生属下的国民党官员主持。据报道，已要求公共团体派代表参加会议，并敦促许多商店在橱窗展示庆祝海报。预计将在街头和从飞机上散发传单。

汪先生的机关报《华中日报》报道称，中国工厂将鸣响汽笛，黄浦江上的外国军舰将鸣放礼炮。该报道还称，所有中国学校今日停课，学生将参加庆祝新政权开始的集会。然而，亲政府阵营的中国媒体报道称，当地大多数学生的情绪截然不同。该报宣布，年轻人正考虑发动“怠工”（"tai-kung"，“慢干”）罢工，以抗议汪伪运动。无论情况如何，事实是，这里的许多中国学校已经因春假而关闭，因此，目前很难将学生问题视为一个活跃的问题。

FIRST MEETING OF CENTRAL POLITICAL COUNCIL

The Central Political Council of the orthodox
Kuomintang held its first meeting at 9.15 a.m. March 20 in
Nanking at which representatives of the China (orthodox)
Kuomintang, the "Reformed" and the Provisional Governments,
the Mongolian Autonomous Government, the National Socialist
Party and the China Youths' Party were present. Wang Ching-

government to be known as the "National Government" take
place on March 30 at Nanking and that the blue-sky-white-sun

of the new government.

adoption of a policy for the adjustment of relations between
China and Japan.
(3) That the general principles for the
establishment of a central government be passed.

MAR 20 1940

Organisation
Of New China
Gov't Outlined

With the inauguration of the new central regime for China which is expected to take place in Nanking sometime early next month, political interest is centred around the organisation of the Central Political Conference to be headed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Chairman of the Kuomintang Party, according to observations made by the Evening Echo.
Following is the outline of the Conference released by the Secretariat of the Central Political Conference yesterday:

Article 1. In accordance with the resolutions of the National Congress of the Kuo-Min Tang, the Central Political Conference shall be organised by President Wang Ching-wei, assisted by existing administrative Governments, in co-operation with the various lawful political parties other than the Kuo-Min Tang as well as the non-Party national leaders; the system of one-party dictatorship is hereby renounced in favour of an all-Party co-operation.

Party Participation

Article 2. The representatives of the existing Administrations and of the various lawful political parties who will participate in the Central Political Conference shall be determined by President Wang Ching-wei in consultation with the authorities of the existing Administration and the various lawful political parties other than the Kuo-Min Tang. The non-Party national leaders shall be invited by President Wang Ching-wei.

Article 3. The members of the Kuo-Min Tang who will participate in the Central Political Conference shall be designated by President Wang.

Article 4. President Wang Ching-wei shall be the Chairman of the Central Political Conference which shall be composed of thirty members as follows:—
(i) Ten members of the Central Executive and Central Supervisory Committees of the Kuo-Min Tang.
(ii) Five representatives of the Provisional Government.
(iii) Five representatives of the Reformed Government.
(iv) Two representatives of the Inner-Mongolia Federal Autonomous Government.
(v) Four representatives from the various lawful political parties outside the Kuo-Min Tang.
(vi) Four non-Party national leaders.

To Pass Resolutions

Article 5. The Central Political Conference shall pass resolutions on:—
(i) Empowering President Wang Ching-wei to determine the policy for readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations, and to draw up the outline for the establishment of the Central Government.
(ii) Matters concerning the establishment of the Central Government; with reference to (a) the name, capital and flag of the Central Government; (b) the date of the establishment of the Central Government; (c) the structure of the Central Government; and (d) the abolition and liquidation of the Provisional and Reformed Governments.
(iii) The political programme of the Central Government.
(iv) The policy vis-a-vis the Chungking regime and the question of its liquidation.
(v) Matters concerning the convocation of the National Assembly and questions of enforcing Constitutional Government.

Article 6. The resolution of the Central Political Conference shall be decided by agreement of either over one-half or three-fourths of the members according to the nature of the subject matter.

CONSTITUTION

Article 1. The Constitution of the Central Political Conference is based on the Outline of the organisation of the Central Political Conference.

Article 2. The Central Political Conference shall be composed of the President and thirty members who shall be designated or invited by the President.

Article 3. The Central Political Conference shall decide on:—
(i) The policy for the readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations entrusting full powers to the President for its determination and for drawing up the outline of the establishment of the Central Government.
(ii) Matters concerning the establishment of the Central Government with reference to: (a) the name, capital and flag of the Central Government; (b) the date of the establishment of the Central Government; (c) the structure of the Central Government; and (d) the abolition and liquidation of the Provisional and Reformed Governments.
(iii) The political programme of the Central Government.
(iv) The policy vis-a-vis the Chungking regime and the question of its liquidation.
(v) Matters concerning the convocation of the National Assembly and questions of enforcing Constitutional Government.

Article 4. The resolutions of the Central Political Conference shall be decided by agreement of either over one-half or three-fourths of the members according to the nature of the subject matter.

Article 5. The Central Political Conference shall be concluded and dissolved when all the resolutions under Article 3 above have been passed.

Article 6. The resolutions passed by the Central Political Conference shall be executed by the Central Government and referred to the Central Political Council for future reference.

Article 7. These rules shall come into force as from date of promulgation.

1940年3月20日

新中国政府组织大纲概要

据《晚声报》观察，随着预计将于下月初在南京成立的中国新中央政权的 inaugurated（就职/启动），政治关注的焦点集中在由国民党主席汪精卫先生主持的中央政治会议的组织工作上。
以下是中央政治会议秘书处昨日发布的会议大纲概要：

第一条. 根据国民党全国代表大会的决议，中央政治会议由汪精卫总裁组织，在现有行政政府的协助下，并与国民党以外的各合法政党及无党派国家领袖合作；特此放弃一党专政制度，转而实行全党派合作。

政党参与

第二条. 将参加中央政治会议的现有行政机构代表及各合法政党代表，由汪精卫总裁与现有行政机构当局及国民党以外的各合法政党协商确定。无党派国家领袖由汪精卫总裁邀请。

第三条. 将参加中央政治会议的国民党党员由汪总裁指定。

第四条. 汪精卫总裁担任中央政治会议主席，该会议共由三十名成员组成，如下：—
(i) 国民党中央执行委员会和中央监察委员会成员十名。
(ii) 临时政府代表五名。
(iii) 维新政府代表五名。
(iv) 蒙古联盟自治政府代表两名。
(v) 国民党以外的各合法政党代表四名。
(vi) 无党派国家领袖四名。

通过决议

第五条. 中央政治会议应就以下事项通过决议：—
(i) 授权汪精卫总裁决定调整中日关系的政策，并起草建立中央政府的纲领。
(ii) 关于建立中央政府的事项；涉及 (a) 中央政府的名称、首都和国旗；(b) 中央政府的成立日期；(c) 中央政府的结构；以及 (d) 临时政府和维新政府的废除与清算。
(iii) 中央政府的政治纲领。
(iv) 对重庆政权的政策及其清算问题。
(v) 关于召开国民大会及实施宪政的问题。

第六条. 中央政治会议的决议应根据事项性质，由过半数或四分之三以上成员同意决定。

章程

第一条. 中央政治会议的章程以中央政治会议组织大纲为基础。

第二条. 中央政治会议由总裁及三十名成员组成，成员由总裁指定或邀请。

第三条. 中央政治会议应决定：—
(i) 调整中日关系的政策，授予总裁全权以确定该政策并起草建立中央政府的纲领。
(ii) 关于建立中央政府的事项，涉及：(a) 中央政府的名称、首都和国旗；(b) 中央政府的成立日期；(c) 中央政府的结构；以及 (d) 临时政府和维新政府的废除与清算。
(iii) 中央政府的政治纲领。
(iv) 对重庆政权的政策及其清算问题。
(v) 关于召开国民大会及实施宪政的问题。

第四条. 中央政治会议的决议应根据事项性质，由过半数或四分之三以上成员同意决定。

第五条. 当上述第三条下的所有决议均通过后，中央政治会议即告结束并解散。

第六条. 中央政治会议通过的决议应由中央政府执行，并提交中央政治委员会以备将来参考。

第七条. 本规则自公布之日起生效。

April 4, 1940.

National Herald, Sin Wan Pao and Shun Pao :-

LOCAL STUDENTS ISSUE CIRCULAR TELEGRAM

Yesterday the 8,000 students of local
universities and colleges, such as the Kwang Hwa, Chinan,
Futan, Soochow College, University of Shanghai, Utopia,
Great China, Chiaotung, Aurora, Tse Kiang, Shanghai Law
College, Tung Tuh Medical College, Institut Technique
Franco-Chinois, East Asia, Cheng Feng, Nantung, and New
China, issued the following circular telegram addressed
to the public bodies throughout the country :-
"We were much surprised to read a report
appearing in a certain local newspaper on March 30 to the
effect that the China Youths' Educational Association
as well as the branches of our universities, had issued
circular telegrams supporting the return of the 'National
Government' to Nanking. The National Government is now
in Chungking and has not yet returned to the Capital.
Moreover, we have never formed amongst ourselves any
organization known as the Branch of the China Youths'
Educational Association.
"We students of all universities and
colleges have always supported the Government's policy
for national reconstruction by means of the war of
resistance and are strongly opposed to illegitimate
organizations; we refuse to recognize all humiliating
treaties concluded to the detriment of the nation.
"In addition to requesting the authorities
of our colleges and universities to ascertain the source
of the report, we issue this circular telegram for the
information of the public lest they should be misled."

Unauthorized Use of Names by Wang Clique Terrifies Local

the peace movement is terrifying many commercial leaders
in Shanghai. Although most of them have never participated
in political circles, and have firmly refused the temptation

to-day clearing their names. There are still several trade

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. E. R.
No. S. B. D 8986

WANG SEEN
TAKING OVER
HIGH POSTS

Pro-Nipponese Leader
To Hold Premier,
Foreign Jobs

FU BACKS REGIME

(Reuter's Agency)
PEIPING, Mar. 19.—Mr. Wang Ching-wei will assume the posts of Chairman of the Executive Yuan and Minister of Foreign Affairs when the new central government of China is inaugurated in Nanking, according to Provisional Government circles in close touch with the present political situation.

The new government, it is stated, will be organized on the same basis as the present Chungking Government, and will comprise an Executive Yuan, a Legislative Yuan, a Judicial Yuan, an Examination Yuan and a Control Yuan.

To Have Forces
It is expected to have its own military and naval forces because a Military Affairs Committee and a Minister of Navy are to be appointed.

The probable constitution and membership of the new government, it is forecast by informed circles here, will be as follows:
Chairman of the Executive Yuan; Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
Secretary-General of the Executive Yuan; Mr. Chu Min-yi.
Minister for Foreign Affairs; Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
Vice-Ministers for Foreign Affairs; Mr. Chu Ho-hsiao and Mr. Li Sheng-wu.
Minister of Finance; Mr. Chou Fu-hai.
Minister of Military Affairs; Major-General Pao Wen-yueh.
Minister of Navy; Mr. Hsu Tso-ping.
Minister of Education; Mr. Chao Cheng-ping.
Minister of Labor, Industry and Commerce; Mr. Mei Ssu-ping.
Minister of Agriculture, and Forestry; Mr. Lin Po-sheng.
Minister of Communications; Mr. Chu Tsing-lai.
Minister of Railways; Mr. Chen Chun-nu.
Minister of Police; Mr. Ting Mo-chun.
Minister of Social Affairs; Mr. Fu Shin-shuo.
Minister of Judicial Administration; Mr. Chang Shiao-yi.

Two Ministries
It is reported that, under the direct control of the Examination Yuan, there will be a Ministry of Public Safety, while the Control Yuan will have as its subsidiary body the Ministry of Audit.

The Judicial Yuan, it is stated, will be composed of the Commission for the Disciplining of Officials, the Administrative Court, the Supreme Court and the Ministry of Judicial Administration. The last also is subordinate to the Executive Yuan.

In addition to the five Yuans and their subsidiary organs, but directly subordinate also to the new Central Government, will be a Military Affairs Committee, which will be composed of the General Staff, the Military Council and the Directorate-General of Military Training.

Fu Pledges Loyalty
"Representing the five million people of Shanghai, I hereby express to you my congratulations and pledge our loyalty for the future," Mr. Fu Siao-en, Mayor of the Shanghai Special Municipality said in a telegram sent Monday to Mr. Wang Ching-wei, leader of the forthcoming Central Government, according to the Talriku Shimpo today.

"For the past three years since the outbreak of the current China affair, you and your colleagues have forgotten everything else in ceaseless devotion to peace and national salvation", the telegram added.

March 20. 1940. Afternoon Translation.
Sin Shin Pao (Japanese owned Chinese Language newspaper)

Short Biographies.

Chen Kung-po, a most influential member
of Wang Ching-wei's political clique, was born in Kwangtung
51 years ago. He is a graduate of Columbia University.
He held various important positions in the Kuomintang
including that of leader of the Reorganization Clique. He
is now a member of the C.E.C. of the Orthodox Kuomintang.
Chrv Fu-hai, 44, native of Hunan, studied
in the Imperial University in Tokyo, Japan. After teaching
in Canton University, he became Chief of the Political
Training Department of the Central Military Officers
Academy and Chief of the Educational Department of the
Kiangsu Provincial Government. After becoming a member
of the C.E.C., he held the post of Chief of the People's
Training Department of the Kuomintang in 1935. Following
the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities he was appointed
Chief of the Central Publicity Department of the Kuomintang.
In March, 1938, he supported Wang Ching-wei and Mei Sze-ping
in the peace movement. He came to Shanghai in May, 1939,
and was given the post of Chief of Staff to the Wang Ching-
wei Clique.

《新申日报》（日资中文报纸）

人物小传。

陈公博，汪精卫政治派系中最具影响力的成员之一，51年前出生于广东。他是哥伦比亚大学的毕业生。他曾在国民党内担任各种重要职务，包括改组派领袖。他现任正统国民党中央执行委员会委员。
褚民谊，44岁，湖南人，曾就读于日本东京帝国大学。他在广州中山大学任教后，出任中央军官学校政治训练部主任及江苏省政府教育厅厅长。在成为中央执行委员会委员后，他于1935年担任国民党民众训练部部长。中日敌对行动爆发后，他被任命为国民党中央宣传部部长。1938年3月，他支持汪精卫和梅思平发起的和平运动。他于1939年5月来到上海，并被授予汪精卫派系参谋长一职。

March 20, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Dr. Chu Min-nyi, aged 57, native of
Wushing (吳興), Chekiang, is a graduate of Japan
University and Strasbourg University in France. He is
a veteran Kuomintang member. In 1931 he was Chief
Secretary of the Executive Yuan of the National
Government. At present he is Chief Secretary of the
Orthodox Kuomintang and member of the C.E.C. of the
Orthodox Kuomintang, and Chief of the Secretariat of the
Central Political Council.

Mei Sze-ping, age 43, native of
Chekiang, was a graduate of the Law College of Peking
University. After teaching in the Central University
and the Central Political College in Nanking, he was
appointed Magistrate of Klangnin Hsien (江寧縣).
Since the commencement of the peace movement, he has
been travelling between Shanghai, Hongkong and Chungking
as a liaison officer. He is now Chief of the Organization
Department and a C.E.C. member of the Orthodox Kuomintang.

Ling Pah-sung, age 40, native of
Kwangtung, is a graduate of Chungshan University in Moscow.
In his early days he was very active among newspaper circles.
He adopted an anti-Chiang Kai-shek policy when he was Chief
editor of the "Central China Daily News". In 1938, when he
was editor of the "South China Daily News," he was
seriously wounded when an attempt on his life was made by
people detailed by the Chungking authorities. He is now
Chief of the Central Publicity Department and a member of
the C.E.C. of the Orthodox Kuomintang.

Liu Yoch-fung, age 59, native of Tsing
Hoen (清苑), Hopei Province, is a graduate of the
Paoting Military Academy (Infantry). He served under
Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang as Commander of the Second Army and
was a member of the National Military Commission, Chairman
of the Kansu Provincial Government and Counsellor to the
Commander-in-Chief of the Army, Navy and Air Forces in
1930. He joined Wang Ching-wei recently and attended the
Tsingtao Conference.

Yih Boon, age 47, native of Huang Pi
(黃陂), Hupeh Province, is a graduate of the Paoting
Military Academy. Prior to the outbreak of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities, he was Garrison Commissioner of
Wuhan Area. He is at present the Dean of the Central
Military Officers Training Corps.

Li Sung-wu, age 52, native of Tai An
(泰安), Shantung Province, graduated from Peking
University, later he studied law in Tokyo University,
Japan. After teaching in Chinan and Futan Universities,
he was appointed Chief of the General Affairs Dept.
of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1933 and Special
Secretary of the Central Political Council. In 1936
he was advisor to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
After leaving Chungking, where he was a member of the
People's Assembly, he was appointed member of the C.E.C.

Tseng Sin is the elder sister of the late

attached to the Third Department of the National Military
Commission of the Chiang regime. After joining Wang Ching-

梅思平，43岁，浙江人，毕业于北京大学法学院。在南京中央大学及中央政治学院任教后，被任命为江宁县县长。自和平运动开始以来，他作为联络官员往返于上海、香港和重庆之间。现任正统国民党组织部部长及中央执行委员会委员。

林柏生，40岁，广东人，毕业于莫斯科中山大学。早年他在新闻界非常活跃。在担任《华中日报》总编辑期间，他采取反蒋介石政策。1938年，他在担任《华南日报》编辑时，遭重庆当局派遣的人员刺杀，身受重伤。现任正统国民党中央宣传部部长及中央执行委员会委员。

刘郁芬，59岁，河北清苑人，毕业于保定军校（步兵科）。他曾效力于冯玉祥元帅，任第二军军长，并于1930年任全国军事委员会委员、甘肃省人民政府主席及陆海空军总司令顾问。他最近加入汪精卫阵营，并参加了青岛会议。

叶蓬，47岁，湖北黄陂人，毕业于保定军校。在中日敌对行动爆发前，他任武汉地区卫戍司令。现任中央军官训练团教育长。

李圣五，52岁，山东泰安人，毕业于北京大学，后在日本东京大学研习法律。在济南大学和复旦大学任教后，于1933年被任命为外交部总务司司长及中央政治委员会专门委员。1936年任外交部顾问。离开重庆（他曾是国民参政会成员）后，被任命为正统国民党中央执行委员会委员。

Wang Keh-min, age 65, native of Hangchow, Chekiang, had held many high governmental positions. He is at present Chairman of the Political Council of the Provisional Government and Chairman of the Hsin Min Hui Association (新民會).
Wong Ih-tang, native of Huh Fei, Anhwei, is a graduate of the Japan Law College. He was a prominent member of the Anfu Clique. He was at one time Civil Governor of Anhwei Province. He is now Minister of Interior of the Provisional Government and concurrently Vice Chairman of the Hsin Min Hui Association.
Ying Dong (榮 德), age 52, native of Kiangyin, Kiangsu Province, is a graduate of the Military Communications School in Japan. Following the conclusion of the North China Truce, he was appointed Director of the Pei Ping Railway Administration. He is now Director of the Construction Bureau of the Provisional Government.
Chu Seng, age 70, native of Yung Tsing (永 清), Hopei Province. He was Premier of China in 1922 when the Anfu Clique was in power. He is at present Minister of Justice of the Provisional Government.
General Chi Hsi-yuan, age 60, native of Hopei Province, is at present Minister of Public Security and Principal of the Military Academy of the Provisional Government.
Liang Hung-tse, age 52, native of Fokien, is at present Chairman of the Executive Yuan of the "Reformed Government".
Wen Chung-yao, age 65, native of Kwangtung, is at present Chairman of the Legislative Yuan of the "Reformed Government".
Chen Chun, age 51, native of Fokien, is at present Minister of Interior of the "Reformed Government".
Lieut.-General Jen Yuan-tao, age 50, native of Ishing, Kiangsu, is a graduate of the Paoting Military Academy. He was Brigadier of the 15th Mixed Brigade, Garrison Commander of the Pinghan Railway and a-member of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council in 1938. He is now Minister of Pacification of the "Reformed Government".
Kao Kwen-ngoo was appointed Vice Minister of Pacification shortly after the inauguration of the "Reformed Government". He subsequently became the first Mayor of Nanking Municipality which post he still holds.
Tso Da Yoch Po Tsa Pu, age 65, is a native of Charhar, and member of the Ming An Banner (明 安 旗). He is at present Chief of the Political Council of the Mongolian Federal Autonomous Government which was inaugurated in September last year.
Chen Nyoh-min, age 47, native of Mukden, is a law college graduate. He is at present Chief of the Political Department of South Charhar.

王揖唐，安徽合肥人，毕业于日本法政大学。曾是安福俱乐部的显要成员。曾任安徽省民政长。现任临时政府内政部长，并兼任新民会副会长。

荣德（榮 德），52岁，江苏江阴人，毕业于日本陆军通信学校。华北停战协定签订后，被任命为北平铁路管理局局长。现任临时政府建设总署督办。

朱深，70岁，河北永清（永 清）人。1922年安福俱乐部掌权时，曾任中国国务总理。现任临时政府司法部长。

齐燮元将军，60岁，河北人，现任临时政府治安部部长兼军官学校校长。

梁鸿志，52岁，福建人，现任“维新政府”行政院院长。

温宗尧，65岁，广东人，现任“维新政府”立法院院长。

陈群，51岁，福建人，现任“维新政府”内政部长。

任援道中将，50岁，江苏宜兴人，毕业于保定军校。曾任第十五混成旅旅长、平汉铁路警备司令，并于1938年担任冀察政务委员会外交委员会委员。现任“维新政府”绥靖部长。

左达约布扎（Tso Da Yoch Po Tsa Pu），65岁，察哈尔人，明安旗（明 安 旗）成员。现任去年九月成立的蒙古联盟自治政府政务委员会主任委员。

陈耀民，47岁，沈阳人，法学院毕业。现任察南政务厅厅长。

李祖虞（Li Tsoo-yu），57岁，江苏常州人，毕业于日本早稻田大学。1934年曾任福建省政府民政厅厅长。辞职后来到上海，被任命为上海律师公会会长。

张英华（Chang Ying-hwa），55岁，河北衡水人，毕业于北洋大学和英国曼彻斯特大学。他曾任四川、山东和河北的盐运使，并在唐绍仪内阁期间担任财政部长。

赵承平（Chao Cheng-ping），64岁，江苏常山人，毕业于日本早稻田大学。他曾任暨南大学校长、北平特别市社会局局长、青岛特别市教育局局长。他在文化界颇有名气。

臧土光（Zang Tuh-kwang），46岁，广西人，是臧宗銮（Zang Tsung-shuan）之子。他曾任梧州海关监督及广西外交专员。

杨耀星（Yang Yoch-sing），46岁，安徽泗县人，毕业于北京陆军军官学校。他曾在潘复内阁期间担任陆军次长，并担任过其他军职。

赵曾鄂（Chao Tseng-ngoh），别名赵叔雍（Chao Soh-yung），前《申报》记者。现任《华中日报》代经理。他是上海资深的文化工作者。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 18986
15- 3 1/c

Admiral Yonai Pledges
Support, Recognition To
New Central Government

Japanese Prime Minister's Statement On Coming
Session Of Central Political Council; The
Konoye Principles Are Reiterated

EULOGY OF MR. WANG CHING-WEI;
NEW ORDER IN EAST ASIA

TOKYO, March 13.—Japan's intention to respect China's independence and freedom was reiterated by the Prime Minister, Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai, in a statement issued to-day in response to Mr. Wang Ching-wei's manifesto of yesterday in connection with the forthcoming meeting of the Central Political Council at Nanking.

"Every country should be enabled," the Premier states, "to find its proper place of peace and contentment."

The first step towards the reconstruction of East Asia, he points out, is to create and insure a new inter-national relationship between Japan, Manchoukuo and China, which conforms to the underlying ideal of the new order in East Asia. "That is why neighbourly amity and goodwill, common defence against the Comintern, and economic co-operation were advocated in the Konoye statement.

Respect For China's Independence
"That Japan will respect China's independence and freedom," Admiral Yonai continues, "has been made clear in successive statements issued by the Japanese Government, and will be proved in fact as the present disturbances subside.

"Although China and Japan are now engaged in hostilities, the two peoples retain in their hearts a spirit of mutual sympathy and tolerance."

many political and social leaders.
Wholehearted Assistance
"Japan," he asserts, "will render wholehearted assistance towards the formation of the new Government and is prepared to extend speedy recognition after its establishment."

In conclusion, the Premier expresses the ardent hope that Mr. Wang Ching-wei and all those other men of vision and leadership united in purposes and resolute in action, will proceed with the great task for the regeneration of Asia.

"I am convinced that their earnest endeavours will meet with popular approval and support...... and that the misfortune brought on by the present Sino-Japanese conflict will be turned into eternal blessing."—Reuter.

Statement In Detail
TOKYO, March 13.—Japan will extend "full support" to the forthcoming new Central Government of China, which she is "prepared to recognise promptly," Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai declared here to-day in a statement issued in his capacity as Prime Minister.

The impending establishment of the central administration he stated, was "a matter of rejoicing" for the Japanese Empire in that it would bring about the re-establishment of peace in East Asia.

The statement was issued in the form of a reply by the Japanese Premier to the Manifesto issued in Shanghai yesterday by Mr. Wang Ching-wei announcing the impending convocation of the Central Political Conference in Nanking. It read:

"The great ideal embodied in the spirit of the founding of our nation, lies in extending a world of conflict and strife in order to realize a benevolent and universal peace. Also rests therein the source of the concept of establishing a new order in East Asia. All nations should rightly acquire the means of living in peace; neighbours should co-operate with one another while respecting their basic traits, and thus proceed jointly upon the road to development and prosperity.

However, to achieve this sacred task of rebuilding East Asia, it is necessary first to inaugurate and firmly establish a new relationship based upon justice, between Japan, China, and Manchoukuo.

It goes without saying that these new relations shall be in harmony with the essence of the establishment of a New Order in East Asia, which has been urged the spirit described above. That is why this Government has advocated the

FILE

ADMIRAL YONAI

The Premier then eulogises Mr. Wang Ching-wei, "who is bringing light to his people who are suffering from the chaos of war, and adherence of his principles."

Mr. Wang Ching-wei's peace and national salvation movement has won a sympathetic hearing and rapid headway since the Hanoi Congress in August last year.

He has formed the Central Political Council and the new Government will be inaugurated soon with the united support of the people.

米内光政海军大将承诺
支持并承认新中央政府

日本首相就即将召开的中央政治委员会会议发表声明；重申近卫原则

颂扬汪精卫先生；
东亚新秩序

东京，3月13日电。——日本首相米内光政（Mitsumasa Yonai）海军大将在今日发表的一份声明中，重申了日本尊重中国独立与自由的意图。该声明是针对汪精卫先生昨日就即将在南京举行的中央政治委员会会议所发表的宣言而作出的回应。

首相在声明中指出：“应使每个国家都能找到其应有的和平与满足之位。”

他指出，重建东亚的第一步，是建立并确保日本、满洲国与中国之间符合东亚新秩序基本理想的新型国际关系。“这正是近卫声明中倡导睦邻友好、共同防共以及经济合作的原因。

尊重中国的独立
米内光政海军大将继续说道：“日本政府已在历次声明中明确表明将尊重中国的独立与自由，随着当前事变的平息，这一立场将在事实上得到证明。

尽管中日目前处于敌对状态，但两国人民心中仍保留着相互同情与宽容的精神。”

许多政治和社会领袖。
全心全意的援助
他断言：“日本将全心全意协助新政府的组建，并准备在其成立后迅速予以承认。”

最后，首相热烈希望汪精卫先生以及其他所有目标一致、行动坚决的有识之士和领袖人物，能够推进亚洲复兴的伟大事业。

“我深信，他们的真诚努力将获得民众的赞同与支持____，并且由当前中日冲突带来的不幸将转化为永恒的祝福。”——路透社。

声明详情
东京，3月13日电。——日本首相米内光政海军大将今日在此发表声明称，日本将对即将成立的中国新中央政府给予“全力支持”，并“准备迅速予以承认”。

他表示，中央行政机构的即将建立对日本帝国来说是“一件值得庆幸的事”，因为它将带来东亚和平的重建。

该声明以日本首相回复汪精卫先生昨日在上海发布的宣言的形式发表，汪氏在宣言中宣布即将在南京召开中央政治会议。声明内容如下：

“体现于我国建国精神中的伟大理想，在于消除冲突与争斗的世界，以实现仁爱与普遍的和平。建立东亚新秩序的概念之源亦在于此。所有国家都应正当地获得和平生活的手段；邻国应在尊重彼此基本特性的基础上相互合作，从而共同走上发展与繁荣之路。

然而，要实现重建东亚这一神圣任务，首先必须在日本、中国和满洲国之间开创并 firmly establish（稳固建立）基于正义的新关系。

不言而喻，这些新关系应与上述精神所倡导的东亚新秩序建立的本质相和谐。正因如此，本政府倡导

随后，首相对汪精卫先生予以颂扬，称他“正为遭受战乱之苦的人民带来光明，并坚持其原则”。

自去年八月河内会议以来，汪精卫先生的和平救国运动赢得了同情的倾听并取得了迅速进展。

他已组建中央政治委员会，新政府将在人民的 united support（联合支持）下不久后正式成立。

ly relations, joint defence against

operation in the previous Konoye
Statement. Our course is clear.

Concrete Measures
"The concrete measures for a
New Order which the Government
proposes to establish in conjunction
with the new Central Government
of China, also are in harmony with
the Konoye Statement. They aim
essentially at promoting amity
through mutual assistance and co-
operation, with scrupulous respect
for the inherent character of nation
and race; at establishing peace in
East Asia by jointly preventing the
infiltration of Communism; at estab-
lishing a mutually beneficial
economic system which will fulfil
each other's needs.

"It is evident from the repeated
statements made by this Govern-
ment in the past that it will respect
China's independence and liberty.
This should be proven by facts
when the situation is normalized.

Generosity And Pity
"Although Japan and China are
engaged in conflict, generosity and
commiseration should prevail. The
longer the hostilities are permitted
to continue, the larger will be the
sacrifices of East Asia.

"However, it is evident that no
matter how long it may take and
how large the sacrifices may be we
cannot abandon this divinely-impos-
ed task. The determination of this
Government and of the Japanese
people is now firmer than ever,
while national strength has been
systematically fostered since the
outbreak of the current China
Affair. The Japanese nation is pre-
pared to meet a protracted war, no
matter how lengthy, so long as the
anti-Japanese and pro-Communist
regime in China persists in its illu-
sions.

The Light Of Justice
"China's vast population, number-
ing 400,000,000, includes many who
are not blind to the situation. For
some time past, enlightened men
have been advocating peace and
national salvation. Having seen the
light of justice, they have placed
themselves at the service of man-
kind, even at the risk of their own
lives, to rescue their people from
the clutches of misery. They were
motivated by their concern of the
prevailing situation in East Asia,
sharing our views and travelling on
the same road. Is there anyone who
can belittle their valour and not
exalt their courage?

"Among them all, Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, impelled by an un-
quenchable love for his country,
could not bear watching idly the
people of China being driven into
distress and privation by the policy
of national reconstruction through
resistance adopted by the Chung-
king regime, which was speeding
China along the road to Bolsheviza-
tion. He, thereupon, advocated na-
tional salvation through anti-Com-
munism and peace with Japan.

Groping In The Dark
"In the face of all manner of
pressure and persecution by the
Chungking regime, he pursued the
path of his convictions by bringing
light to his people lost in the dark-
ness. Thus, he has won the confid-
ence and the following of his coun-
trymen.

"His peace and national salvation
movement as well as the prepara-
tions for a new Central Government
have made rapid headway since the
Sixth Plenary Session of the Kuo-
mintang, which was held in Shang-
hai last year. For the sake of peace
in East Asia, we are truly gratified
to know that the Central Political
Conference is to meet soon and that
a new Central Government will be
brought into being with the united
support and co-operation of exist-
ing administrations, of many lead-
ers representing various political
parties and various sections of
society.

"Japan will, of course, render full
support towards the new Govern-
ment and is prepared promptly to
extend it recognition following its
establishment.

The Road To Peace
"We are deeply moved that the
leaders of the established adminis-
trations, who, for the last two years
have devoted their efforts towards
the rehabilitation and the normaliza-
tion of the life of the people within
their jurisdictions, have agreed
with Mr. Wang in his basic convic-
tions thereby to proceed along the
path of peace and rational recon-
struction.

"At this time, when the establish-
ment of the Central Government of
China appears imminent, I wish to
express my ardent hope that Mr.
Wang and other men of vision will
make further endeavours in the vast
task of developing East Asia by
maintaining harmony and co-opera-
tion.

"It is our firm belief that their
efforts will earn them the support
of people both at home and abroad,
thus to turn the misfortunes of the
present conflict into an everlasting
blessing."—Domei.

近卫声明中的善邻友好、共同防共及经济合作三原则。我们的方针是明确的。

具体措施
“政府拟与中国新中央政府共同建立‘新秩序’的具体措施，亦与近卫声明相一致。其宗旨本质上在于：在严格尊重各国各民族固有特性的基础上，通过互助与合作促进和睦；通过共同防止共产主义渗透，确立东亚和平；建立一种互惠互利的经济体系，以满足彼此的需求。

“从本政府过去的一再声明中可以明显看出，我们将尊重中国的独立与自由。待局势正常化时，这一点应以事实予以证明。

宽宏与怜悯
“尽管中日之间处于冲突状态，但仍应秉持宽宏与怜悯之心。敌对行动持续越久，东亚所付出的牺牲就越大。

“然而，显而易见的是，无论耗时多久，无论牺牲多大，我们都不能放弃这项上天赋予的使命。本政府与日本国民的决心如今比以往任何时候都更加坚定，而自当前‘中国事变’爆发以来，国力已得到系统性的培养。只要中国的反日亲共政权继续沉溺于幻想之中，日本民族已准备好应对一场持久的战争，无论其多么漫长。

正义之光
“中国四亿人口中，有许多人并非对局势视而不见。一段时间以来，有识之士一直倡导和平与救国。他们目睹正义之光，不惜冒生命危险，投身于人类事业，以将人民从苦难的魔掌中拯救出来。他们的动机源于对东亚 prevailing situation（ prevailing situation 译为： prevailing situation）的关切，他们与我们观点相同，道路一致。有谁能够轻视他们的英勇而不颂扬他们的勇气呢？

“其中，汪精卫先生出于对祖国不可抑制的热爱，不忍坐视中国人民因重庆政权采取的‘抗战建国’政策而陷入困苦与匮乏，该政策正加速中国走向布尔什维克化。因此，他倡导通过反共和与日本和平来实现救国。

在黑暗中摸索
“面对重庆政权的种种压力与迫害，他坚守信念之路，为迷失在黑暗中的人民带来光明。因此，他赢得了同胞的信任与追随。

“自去年在上海举行的国民党六中全会以来，他的和平救国运动以及为新中央政府的筹备工作取得了迅速进展。为了东亚的和平，我们深感欣慰地获悉，中央政治会议即将召开，并且在现有各行政机构、代表各政党及社会各界的众多领袖的 united support and co-operation（ united support and co-operation 译为：统一支持与合作）下，一个新的中央政府即将诞生。

“日本当然将对新政府给予全力支持，并准备在其成立后 promptly extend it recognition（ promptly extend it recognition 译为：迅速予以承认）。

和平之路
“既存各行政机构的领导人在过去两年中致力于其管辖范围内民生的恢复与正常化，他们同意汪先生的基本信念，从而沿着和平与理性重建的道路前进，对此我们深为感动。

“值此中国中央政府成立指日可待之际，我谨表示热切希望，汪先生及其他有远见之士在开发东亚这一宏大任务中，通过保持和谐与合作，作出进一步的努力。

“我们坚信，他们的努力将赢得国内外人民的支持，从而将当前冲突的不幸转化为永恒的祝福。”——同盟社

ACCEPTANCE OF NEW
GOVERNMENT URGED

Interests Of 3rd Party
Powers To Be Defended
States Spokesman

Referring to the manifesto of
Mr. Wang Ching-wei, issued yes-
terday on the occasion of the
anniversary of the death of the
late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, founder of
the Chinese Republic, stressing the
necessity for the readjustment of
conditions in Asia and Sino-
Japanese relations in harmony
with Prince Konoye's statement,
the Japanese Embassy spokesman
at the press conference yesterday
evening, pointed out that the
Japanese Government had de-
clared its position and was not
seeking the destruction of China
nor the subjection of the Chinese
people.
These opinions, said the spokes-
man, had been reiterated by
Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai, Japan-
ese Prime Minister, and these points
should be weighed by Third Party
Powers in considering their opin-
ions of Sino-Japanese relations.
Moreover, he continued, the prin-
ciple concern of Third Party Powers
in China appeared to be:—
1. Their ability to trade and
engage in lawful industrial enter-
prises.
2. Freedom in cultural endea-
vours such as religious missions and
medical institutions.

"No Political Mystery"

In consequence, it would seem,
continued the spokesman, that so
long as the Chinese government
would, and the Chinese government
should, prove capable of protecting
lawfully acquired rights and inter-
ests, the establishment and concern
of Third Party Powers should end.
It is not necessary to inject so much
political mystery into the matter.
Should two regimes be establish-
ed in China following the creation
of the Central Government, Third
Party Powers should not assist
Chungking and reject the Nanking
regime, which protects them of their
lawfully acquired rights and inter-
ests.
The test of any government, the
spokesman continued, is whether it
can establish a good administration.
When the new Central government
is organized and gives protection to
lawfully acquired third party in-
terests, it should be a government
that receives the support and as-
sistance of all. The belief that re-
cognition by Japan would tend to
give Japan a monopoly of trade, is
a predication that is prejudicial and
an entirely unfair attitude to take.
It is necessary for Japan to take
a long view of the problem of
China, since it must win the trust
and co-operation of the 400,000,000
Chinese and his point, needless to
say, is well understood by those
who are shaping Japan's policies,
the spokesman concluded.

敦促接受新政府

第三方列强利益将获维护
发言人称

日本大使馆发言人在昨晚的新闻发布会上，提及汪精卫先生于昨日中华民国创始人孙中山博士逝世周年纪念日发表的宣言，该宣言强调有必要按照近卫亲王声明的精神，调整亚洲局势及中日关系。发言人指出，日本政府已表明其立场，并非寻求毁灭中国或使中国人民屈服。

发言人称，这些观点已由日本首相米内光政海军大将重申，第三方列强在考量其对中日关系的看法时，应权衡这些要点。此外，他继续说道，第三方列强在华的主要关切似乎在于：—
1. 其进行贸易及从事合法工业企业的能力。
2. 在宗教传教和医疗机构等文化事业方面的自由。

“无政治奥秘”

因此，发言人继续说道，看来只要中国政府能够——且应当——证明其有能力保护合法取得的权利和利益，第三方列强的建立与关切便应终止。没有必要在此事中注入如此多的政治奥秘。如果在中国成立中央政府后出现两个政权，第三方列强不应援助重庆并拒绝保护其合法取得之权利和利益的南京政权。

发言人继续说，检验任何政府的标准在于其能否建立良好的行政治理。当新的中央政府组建起来并对合法取得的第三方利益提供保护时，它应当成为一个获得各方支持与协助的政府。认为日本的承认将导致日本垄断贸易的看法，是一种带有偏见的预设，也是一种完全不公平的态度。

日本有必要从长远角度看待中国问题，因为它必须赢得四亿中国人的信任与合作。发言人最后总结道，毋庸赘言，这一观点已为制定日本政策的人士所充分理解。

新政权与
外国权益

请求第三方列强支持
汪精卫政府

在昨日的日本记者招待会上，日本大使馆发言人请求第三方列强不要援助重庆政府，并不要在汪精卫先生于南京组建新的“中央政府”时对其加以排斥。他断言，新的南京政权将保证保护第三方列强在中国合法取得的权益。

February 29, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Pao :-

PERSONNEL OF NEW PUPPET GOVERNMENT

During the Tsingtao meeting, Wang Ching-wei decided to hold a Central Political Conference in February and to form the "Central Government" in Nanking on March 1. Yet the dates are again to be postponed. Since the action of Kao Chung-woo (高宗武) and Tao Hsi-sen (陶希聖) in denouncing Wang Ching-wei's traitorous secret treaties with Japan, many of Wang's followers have quitted their master. The denunciation of Wang by Zung Kwei-tsung (程克俊) was closely followed by the suicide of Wang Kai-tsang (王開藏). Feeling himself deserted, Wang Ching-wei decided to get closer co-operation with the old puppets, thinking they might be more trustworthy.

Learning of the participation of the puppet officers from the "Reformed Government", however, Chen Chung-fu (陳中孚) and Dr. Hu Shih-tseng (胡士楨) of the New Doong Meng Wei (新同盟會) suddenly refused to join the "Government". Chen Fu-mo (陳孚木) and Tsang Ts-ping (曾子平) of the "Asia Development and National Reconstruction Clique" joined only with superficial enthusiasm. Kiang Kong-fu (江亢虎), Wu Tsoong-yien (吳仲賢) and Ying Sz (應時) of the "Constitutional Ruling Party" also showed their dissatisfaction.

There is not a single individual trusted by the Chinese people and well-known on the international scene, who still remains loyal to Wang Ching-wei; those who remain are only such as Liang Hung-tse (梁鴻志), Chen Chun (陳群) etc.

It is learned that the leader of the "National Socialist Party", Tsang Chuin-lih (張君), has sent telegraphic despatches denying the actions of Loh Ting-kwan (羅廷寬) himself. Tsu Suen-sun (徐孫孫), leader of the "Youth Party" also denounced Wang's doings. Though so many followers have quitted Wang, recently many persons were seen coming in and out of Lane 1036, Yu Yuen Road, all with the intention of obtaining a position in the "Government". In order to give positions to his own followers, Wang has decided to include 5 Yuans and 14 Ministries in the "Government". The heads of these Yuans and Ministries are learned to be as follows :-

Wang Ching-wei, Chairman of the Executive Yuan.
Liang Hung-tse, President of the Legislative Yuan.
Chen Kung-poh (陳公博), President of the Judicial Yuan.
Wong Yih-dong (溫宗堯), President of the Examination Yuan.
Wen Tsung-yao (文宗耀), President of the Control Yuan.
Liu Yoeh-feng (劉越豐), Chairman of the Military Council.
Chen Chun (陳群), Minister of Interior.
Jen Yuen-dao (任援道), Minister of War.
Chow Fu-hai (周佛海), Minister of Finance.
Loh Ting-kwan (羅廷寬), Minister of Justice.
Chao Han-sun (趙漢孫), Minister of Education.
Chao Su-yung (趙蘇庸), Minister of Industry and Commerce.
Chu Ching-lai (朱景來), Minister of Communications.
Ling Pah-sen (林柏森), Minister of Publicity.
Mei Sz-ping (梅思平), Minister of Railways.
Chen Tsung-pi (陳宗璧), Minister of Overseas Chinese Affairs.
Tsang Tsing (曾靜), Minister of Public Health (sister of the late Tseng Chung-ming (曾仲鳴)).
Wang Ching-wei to act concurrently as Minister of Foreign Affairs. (The position of Vice-Minister is being sought by one Wu (吳) and another named Chu (朱)).
Chu Min-nyi (褚民誼), Chief Secretary of the Executive Yuan.
Dr. Chu Min-nyi will become Mayor of Shanghai, while Ting Muh-tsung (丁默邨) will be Mayor of Nanking.

《大美报》：

新傀儡政府的人员构成

在青岛会议期间，汪精卫决定于二月召开中央政治会议，并于三月一日在南京成立“中央政府”。然而，日期再次推迟。自从高宗武和陶希圣揭露汪精卫与日本签订的卖国秘密条约以来，汪的许多追随者已离他而去。程克俊对汪的谴责紧随其后的是王开藏的自杀。感到众叛亲离的汪精卫决定与旧傀儡们更紧密地合作，认为他们可能更值得信赖。

然而，得知来自“维新政府”的傀儡官员参与后，新同盟会的陈中孚和胡士楨博士突然拒绝加入该“政府”。“亚洲发展与国家重建派”的陈孚木和曾子平仅以表面的热情加入。“宪政统治党”的江亢虎、吴仲贤和应时也表达了不满。

没有一个受中国人民信任且在国际舞台上知名的人仍然忠于汪精卫；留下来的人只有梁鸿志、陈群等。

据悉，“国家社会党”领袖张君（音译）已发出电报，否认罗廷宽本人的行为。“青年党”领袖徐孙孙（音译）也谴责了汪的行为。尽管有这么多追随者离开了汪，但最近许多人被看到进出愚园路1036弄，都意在谋求“政府”中的职位。为了给自己的追随者安排职位，汪决定在“政府”中设立五院和十四部。据悉这些院部的首长如下：

汪精卫，行政院院长。
梁鸿志，立法院院长。
陈公博，司法院院长。
温宗尧，考试院院长。
文宗耀，监察院院长。
刘越丰，军事委员会主席。
陈群，内政部长。
任援道，军政部长。
周佛海，财政部长。
罗廷宽，司法部长。
赵汉孙，教育部长。
赵苏庸，工商部长。
朱景来，交通部长。
林柏森，宣传部长。
梅思平，铁道部长。
陈宗璧，侨务部长。
曾静，卫生部长（已故曾仲鸣之妹）。
汪精卫兼任外交部长。（副部长一职正由一名姓吴者和一名姓朱者争取）。
褚民谊，行政院秘书长。
褚民谊博士将出任上海市长，而丁默邨将出任南京市长。

February 15, 1940.
Afternoon Translation.
8986
National Herald, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao and Shun Pao 23 2 46
published on February 13 the following letter from
Hongkong written by Tao Hai-sen :-

IV - The Mental State of Members of Wang
Ching-wei Clique.

Under the circumstances, will Chow Vei-hai,
Mei Shih-ping and Mr. and Mrs. Wang Ching-wei still be
pleased to proceed to Nanking and officiate at the
inauguration of a "People's Government" with an easy mind?
I feel sorry for them and I can say that they, especially
Wang Ching-wei, will have no pleasure.
Between China and Japan a life-and-death
struggle is now in progress, a struggle that will decide
the fate of the two countries. In a struggle like the
present one, we must maintain our national prestige if we
wish to uphold our standing in case of war and secure
equality in case of peace. We must maintain our own
military and economic strength, uphold our independent
and political status as well as our national psychology.
Consequently, a nation-wide war should be carried out if
war is decided, while in case of peace, peace should be
instituted throughout the country. If any individual or
a clique works independently without national standing,
not only will such work prove detrimental to the nation,
but the person or clique in question will eventually be
annihilated and their sacrifice will not win any sympathy
from the people.
This is the mistake Wang Ching-wei, Chow
Vei-hai and Mei Shih-ping are making, for they have lost
their national status. They want to talk peace with the
Japanese and dream of securing terms that will assure their
independence and freedom and the creation of an independent
government. It is this blunder that has led them into
an irreparable situation. At first they thought the Japanese
were easy to deal with; eventually they began to realize
that the Japanese were hard to deal with, but it was already
too late. Consequently, they have no alternative but to
obey the instructions of the Japanese. They thought that
with money they could buy over any person and that with
firearms they could overcome all opposition, but they seem
to have overlooked the fact that the present struggle is
a national struggle and though some are willing to accept
bribes because of circumstances of livelihood or of
personal connections, yet many of them have refused to work
for the Japanese and have gone on strike. They seem unaware
of the proverb: "It is useless to threaten with death people
who are not afraid of death."
Ting Muh-tsung (丁默) and his followers
are not fond of resorting to assassination; they have on
many occasions reminded Chow Vei-hai that assassinations
should stop at a certain stage, otherwise the reaction on
the people would be too dreadful. They seem to believe
everything Japanese and to have forgotten that the Japanese
troops are now shelling our soldiers at the front.
I am sorry for them and hope that my
fellow countrymen will deliver them from their mental decay.
I believe that the day will come when they will come fully
to their senses and leave the service of the Japanese.
pages.zh:
1940年2月15日。
下午译文。

《国民日报》、《大美报》、《新闻报》及《申报》于2月13日刊登了陶海森（音译）从香港写来的如下信件：

四、汪精卫集团成员的心理状态。

在此情形下，周佛海、梅思平以及汪精卫夫妇是否仍能心安理得地前往南京，主持“国民政府”的成立典礼？我为他们感到遗憾，可以说，他们，尤其是汪精卫，绝不会感到愉快。

中日之间正在进行一场生死搏斗，这场斗争将决定两国的命运。在像当前这样的斗争中，如果我们希望在战时保持地位并在和平时获得平等，就必须维护我们的国家威望。我们必须保持自身的军事和经济实力，维护我们独立的政治地位以及民族心理。因此，如果决定开战，就应进行全国性的战争；而如果实现和平，则应在全国范围内确立和平。如果任何个人或派系在没有国家立场的情况下独立行动，不仅这种行为将对国家有害，而且该个人或派系最终将被消灭，他们的牺牲也不会赢得人民的同情。

这正是汪精卫、周佛海和梅思平所犯的错误，因为他们已经失去了国家立场。他们想与日本人谈和平，梦想着获得能确保其独立和自由以及建立独立政府的条件。正是这一错误导致他们陷入了无法挽回的境地。起初，他们认为日本人容易对付；最终他们开始意识到日本人难以对付，但为时已晚。因此，他们别无选择，只能服从日本人的指令。他们以为用钱可以收买任何人，用枪支可以克服所有反对，但他们似乎忽略了一个事实，即当前的斗争是一场民族斗争，尽管有些人因生计或个人关系愿意接受贿赂，但许多人拒绝为日本人工作并进行了罢工。他们似乎不知道这句谚语：“吓不怕不怕死的人。”

丁默邨及其追随者并不喜欢诉诸暗杀；他们曾多次提醒周佛海，暗杀应在一定阶段停止，否则对民众引起的反响将过于可怕。他们似乎相信日本人的一切，却忘记了日军正在前线炮击我们的士兵。

我为他们感到遗憾，希望我的同胞能将他们从精神堕落中拯救出来。我相信总有一天他们会完全清醒过来，脱离为日本人服务的行列。

pages.en:
February 15, 1940.                                      Afternoon Translation.

Natinnal Herald, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao and Shun pao
published on February 13 the following letter from
Hongkong written by Tao Hsi-sen :-
V - The Ccnditions and The New Gcvernment.

The new gcvernment will be established cn
the basis cf harsh and hypocritical ccnditions. We should
realize clearly that even if the Japanese terms are nct
harsh, the new gcvernment will nct be in a position to
maintain itself and it will hardly be able to achieve any
gcod result.

From the Japanese point of view, the new
government will never be able tc bring about the termination
cf the China incident. On the contrary, it will prcve
a great hindrance tc Japan's policy vis-a-vis the
Powers and China; its establishment will be of nc
advantage tc Japan. Sooner or later, the "Principal
measures fcr the readjustment cf the new relations between
China and Japan" and the new Central Gcvernment will be
discarded by Japan.

I still hcpe that Wang Ching-wei, Chow
Vai-hai, Mei Shih-ping and others will hesitate cn the
